body.text: śrīḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Śrīḥ</s> (Auspiciousness)

body.text: oṃ tatsadbrahmaṇe namaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. Salutation to that which is truth, to <s>Brahman</s>.

body.text: atha rasaratnasamuccayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now begins the <s>Rasaratnasamuccaya</s> (Compendium of Mercury and Gems).

body.text: rasotpattirnāma prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The first chapter, named the Origin of <s>Rasa</s> (Mercury).

children.text: yasyānandabhavena maṅgalakalāsaṃbhāvitena sphura- dhāmnā siddharasāmṛtena karuṇāvīkṣāsudhāsindhunā /
children.translated_text: He whose radiance, born of bliss, auspicious and esteemed, shining forth, is the nectar of perfected <s>rasa</s> (mercury), an ocean of the ambrosia of compassionate glances,

children.text: bhaktānāṃ prabhavaprasaṃhṛtijarārāgādirogāḥ kṣaṇā- cchāntiṃ yānti jagatpradhānabhiṣaje tasmai parasmai namaḥ // VRrs_1.1 //
children.translated_text: by whom the diseases of creation, dissolution, old age, passion and the like of the devoted are instantly pacified — salutation to that supreme one, the foremost physician of the world.
<s>Ādima</s>, <s>Candrasena</s>, and the skilled lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>,
<s>Kapālī</s>, <s>Matta</s>, <s>Māṇḍavya</s>, <s>Bhāskara</s>, and <s>Śūrasenaka</s>,

children.text: ratnakośaś ca śaṃbhuś ca sāttviko naravāhanaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Ratnakośa</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Sāttvika</s>, and <s>Naravāhana</s>,
<s>Indrada</s>, <s>Gomukha</s>, <s>Kambali</s>, and <s>Vyāḍi</s> as well,
<s>Nāgārjuna</s>, <s>Surānanda</s>, <s>Nāgabodhi</s>, <s>Yaśodhana</s>,

children.text: khaṇḍaḥ kāpāliko brahmā govindo lampako hariḥ // VRrs_1.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, <s>Kāpālika</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Lampaka</s>, and <s>Hari</s>,
these twenty-seven are the bestowers of success in <s>rasa</s> (mercury).

children.text: rasāṅkuśo bhairavaś ca nandī svacchandabhairavaḥ // VRrs_1.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasāṅkuśa</s>, <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Nandī</s>, and <s>Svacchandabhairava</s>,
<s>Manthānabhairava</s> as well, and <s>Kākacaṇḍīśvara</s> likewise,
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, the sage <s>Śṛṅga</s>, the compiler of the <s>Kriyātantrasamuccaya</s>,
<s>Rasendratilaka</s>, the <s>yogī</s>, <s>Bhālukī</s>, the one called <s>Maithila</s>,

children.text: mahādevo narendraś ca vāsudevo harīśvaraḥ // VRrs_1.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Narendra</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and <s>Harīśvara</s>,
having examined the treatises of these and others, a compendium is made
of the <s>rasas</s> (mercurial preparations) and <s>siddhas</s> (perfected substances) useful for therapeutic purposes.
By the son of <s>Siṃhagupta</s>, this <s>Rasaratnasamuccaya</s> (Compendium of Mercury and Gems) is composed.
<s>Rasa</s> (mercury), <s>uparasa</s> (secondary minerals), <s>loha</s> (metals), as well as instruments and apparatus,
and also the processes for purification of metals,

children.text: śuddhiḥ sattvaṃ drutirbhasma- karaṇaṃ ca pravakṣyate // VRrs_1.10 //
children.translated_text: purification, extraction of essence, liquefaction, and calcination will be described.
There exists in the northern direction, with its abode in the mists,
a great mountain whose clusters of lofty peaks surpass the clouds.
As if for resting from the great exertion of traversing the path through the sky,

children.text: avatīrṇa iva kṣoṇīṃ śaradambumucāṃ gaṇaḥ // VRrs_1.12 //
children.translated_text: the multitude of autumn rain-clouds has, as it were, descended upon the earth.
With heaps of rays from the hood-jewels of the lords of serpents,

children.text: bhittvā bhuvamivottīrṇo yo vibhāti bhṛśonnataḥ // VRrs_1.13 //
children.translated_text: it appears as though having burst through the earth and risen up, exceedingly lofty.
On whose slopes the blazing herbs, on the jeweled terraces,
imitate at night the unrestrained lightning of the rain-clouds.
Of the <s>Kinnara</s> women who wander on its ridges,
on their feet, through the color of minerals, the semblance of lac-dye is accomplished.
Adorned with the moon as a crest-ornament, with the directions as its garment concealed,

children.text: yo guhādhigato lokair girīśa iti gīyate // VRrs_1.16 //
children.translated_text: he who, dwelling in the cave, is sung by the worlds as <s>Girīśa</s> (Lord of the Mountain).
Sages with closed eyes on its ridges constantly
directly perceive <s>Girīśa</s> (Lord of the Mountain), who is beyond speech and mind.
By the spray of waterfalls dashed against the rocky surfaces of that mountain,
even during the day the <s>Yakṣas</s> behold a sky marked with stars.
Where people, unable to endure the excess of mist-laden wind,
constantly seek the warmth of the bosoms of their own women.
The sun, moving along its ridges even in summer,
with its heat obstructed by the unbounded snow, does not differ from the moon.
In cave-dwellings fragrant with the musk of deer navels,
<s>Kinnara</s> women sing there of the marriage-festival of <s>Gaurī</s>.
There shines the primordial lord, great <s>Maheśvara</s>,
from whom <s>Mahārasa</s> (the great mercury) was born, in the form of <s>rasa</s>, to protect the world.
The merit gained from performing a hundred <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifices), from giving ten million cows and a thousand gold pieces,

children.text: nṛṇāṃ bhavet sūtakadarśanena yat sarvatīrtheṣu kṛtābhiṣekāt // VRrs_1.23 //
children.translated_text: that merit comes to people merely from beholding <s>sūta</s> (mercury), equal to bathing in all the sacred fords.
He who, having made a <s>rasaliṅga</s> (mercury liṅga), worships it with devotion,
obtains the fruit of worshipping all the <s>liṅgas</s> in the three worlds.

children.text: bhakṣaṇaṃ sparśanaṃ dānaṃ dhyānaṃ ca paripūjanam /
children.translated_text: Consuming, touching, gifting, meditating upon, and worshipping —
these are said to be the fivefold worship of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), which destroys the greatest sins.
By merely consuming it, the mass of diseases born from sins of previous births
of all people is destroyed — there is no doubt in this.
The sin committed in a previous birth is instantly destroyed for embodied beings
if <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) is anointed with <s>sūta</s> (mercury) ground with fragrant substances.
He who offers to <s>rasa</s> (mercury) even a tiny amount of <s>abhraka</s> (ite),
for him the fruit of a hundred sacrifices shall be — thus spoke <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: yaś ca nindati sūtendraṃ śaṃbhostejaḥ parātparam /
children.translated_text: And he who reviles <s>Sūtendra</s> (the lord of mercury), the supreme radiance of <s>Śambhu</s>,
he falls into a terrible hell for the duration of a cosmic age.
He who gives to the sick <s>rasa</s> (mercury) endowed with purification and proper preparation,
obtains the eternal fruit of <s>tulādāna</s> (gift of one's weight) and <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifices).
"When mercury is perfected, I shall make the world free from poverty and disease" —
this meditation on <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is declared to remove sins such as <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing of a Brahmin).
The consumption of <s>abhraka</s> (mica) by <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is proclaimed as <s>naivedya</s> (food-offering),
having thus performed worship of <s>rasa</s>, one obtains the fruit born of sacrificial rites.
He in whose belly <s>sūta</s> (mercury) remains when life departs,

children.text: sa mukto duṣkṛtādghorāt prayāti paramaṃ padam // VRrs_1.33 //
children.translated_text: he is freed from terrible misdeeds and attains the supreme state.

children.text: mūrchitvā harati rujaṃ bandhanam anubhūya muktido bhavati /
children.translated_text: When swooned it removes disease; when bound it becomes a bestower of liberation;

children.text: amarīkaroti hi mṛtaḥ ko 'nyaḥ karuṇākaraḥ sūtāt // VRrs_1.34 //
children.translated_text: when killed it makes one immortal — who else is a mine of compassion other than <s>sūta</s> (mercury)?
The mass of sins arising from violence against gods, preceptors, cows, and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> causes incurable

children.text: śvitraṃ tad api ca śamayati yas tasmāt kaḥ pavitrataraḥ sūtāt // VRrs_1.35 //
children.translated_text: <s>śvitra</s> (leucoderma), yet even that it cures — who then is more purifying than <s>sūta</s> (mercury)?

children.text: rasabandha eva dhanyaḥ prārambhe yasya satatamitikaraṇā /
children.translated_text: Blessed indeed is the binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), at the commencement of which there is constant resolution:

children.text: setsyati rase kariṣye mahīmahaṃ nirjarāmaraṇām // VRrs_1.36 //
children.translated_text: "I shall succeed with <s>rasa</s>; I shall make the earth free from old age and death."

children.text: sukṛtaphalaṃ tāvadidaṃ sukule yajjanma dhīś ca tatrāpi /
children.translated_text: This is the fruit of meritorious deeds: birth in a good family, and therein intelligence;

children.text: sāpi ca sakalamahītalatulanaphalā bhūtalaṃ ca suvidheyam // VRrs_1.37 //
children.translated_text: and that intelligence, equal to weighing the entire earth, and the earth itself being amenable.
The fruit of the earth's amenability is wealth, and those various enjoyments as fruits;

children.text: bhogāś ca santi śarīre tadanityamato vṛthā sakalaṃ // VRrs_1.38 //
children.translated_text: but enjoyments depend on the body, and that is impermanent — therefore all is in vain.
Thus, having understood that wealth, body, and enjoyments are always impermanent, one should ever strive

children.text: muktau sāca jñanāttaccābhyāsātsa ca sthire dehe // VRrs_1.39 //
children.translated_text: for liberation; and that comes from knowledge, and knowledge from practice, and practice from a stable body.

children.text: tatsthairye na samarthaṃ rasāyanaṃ kimapi mūlalohādi /
children.translated_text: For that stability, no <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) based on base metals and the like is capable,

children.text: svayamasthirasvabhāvaṃ dāhyaṃ kledyaṃ ca śoṣyaṃ ca // VRrs_1.40 //
children.translated_text: being itself unstable by nature, combustible, liable to moisture, and desiccable.

children.text: kāṣṭhauṣadhyo nāge nāgo vaṅge 'tha vaṅgamapi śulbe /
children.translated_text: Herbal medicines dissolve in lead, lead in tin, and tin in copper,

children.text: śulbaṃ tāre tāraṃ kanake kanakaṃ ca līyate sūte // VRrs_1.41 //
children.translated_text: copper in silver, silver in gold, and gold dissolves in <s>sūta</s> (mercury).

children.text: amṛtatvaṃ hi bhajante haramūrtau yogino yathā līnāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>yogīs</s> merged in the form of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) attain immortality,
so too gold, metals and the rest, when swallowed by the king of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) who pervades the sky.

children.text: paramātmanīva satataṃ bhavati layo yatra sarvasattvānām /
children.translated_text: Just as in the supreme self there is constant dissolution of all beings,
so this one king of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) makes the body free from old age and death.
In a stable body, through the power of practice, having attained knowledge endowed with the eightfold qualities,
one attains the state of <s>Brahman</s> and no longer suffers the sorrows of rebirth and worldly existence.
The supreme light that, with a single portion, simultaneously pervades and sustains the world —
that immortality with its three quarters is not easily attainable by mere detachment alone.
For with a body afflicted by disease, old age, death, and suffering,
perishable in an instant, one cannot worship that subtle <s>Brahman</s>.
Who would even take the name of bodily perfection without the body?

children.text: yadyogagamyamamalaṃ manaso 'pi na gocaraṃ tattvaṃ // VRrs_1.47 //
children.translated_text: That reality which is attainable through <s>yoga</s>, pure, beyond the reach even of the mind.
Greater by far than from sacrifice, charity, austerity, study of the <s>Vedas</s>, self-control, and righteous conduct,
is self-realization through the power of <s>yoga</s>, indeed exceedingly so.
That which, situated between the two eyebrows, illumines the world like a peacock's lightning or the sun —
for some of blessed vision, that supreme light of pure consciousness is unveiled.
Of the nature of supreme bliss, the supreme light, self-luminous and beyond conceptualization,
with all afflictions dissolved — it is to be known as peaceful and self-experienced.
Fixing the mind upon that, seeing the entire world as shining with consciousness,
with the bondage of <s>karma</s> destroyed, one attains <s>Brahman</s>-hood here in this very life.
Free from passion and aversion, truthful in conduct, devoid of falsehood,
they become impartial everywhere through contact with <s>Brahman</s> of pure consciousness.
They abide endowed with <s>aṇimā</s> and other powers, with radiant bodies, ever-arisen in bliss,
having attained the immortal nature of <s>Brahman</s>, their purpose fulfilled.
The abode of all knowledge, the root of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) —
what other supreme good is there, apart from this one body free from old age and death?

children.text: pratyakṣeṇa pramāṇena yo na jānāti sūtakam /
children.translated_text: He who does not know <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) by direct perception as a means of proof,

children.text: adṛṣṭavigrahaṃ devaṃ kathaṃ jñāsyati cinmayam // VRrs_1.55 //
children.translated_text: how will he know the invisible God, who is of the nature of pure consciousness?
That body which is shattered by old age, helpless with the suffering of cough, asthma, and the like,
is not fit for <s>samādhi</s> (deep meditation), with the activity of intellect and senses obstructed.
A youth of sixteen years is infatuated with the taste of sensory pleasures; beyond that,
an old man with discernment gone — how shall a mortal attain liberation?

children.text: asminneva śarīre yeṣāṃ paramātmano na saṃvedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who have no realization of the supreme self in this very body,
for them, after abandonment of the body, that <s>Brahman</s> is even more distant.
<s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods strive for that, having resorted to a divine body,
and other sages, liberated while living, endure until the end of the cosmic cycle.
Therefore, by the <s>yogī</s> who aspires to <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living), first
a divine body must be fashioned, through the union of the creation of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) and <s>Gaurī</s>.
On this very mountain, out of mutual desire to conquer each other, through the love of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>,
when their lovemaking commenced, causing agitation in the three worlds,
<s>Agni</s> (Fire) was sent by the gods to interrupt the lovemaking,
they desiring from the two a son who would be the slayer of <s>Tārakāsura</s>.
Having arrived in the form of a pigeon at the cave of <s>Himavat</s> (the Himālaya), <s>Agni</s>,
agitated by his non-bird state, was observing the play of love.
Seeing him, <s>Śambhu</s>, ashamed, ceased from lovemaking then;
the last <s>dhātu</s> (seminal fluid) that had fallen was seized by the Trident-bearer (<s>Śiva</s>).
Cast into the mouth of <s>Agni</s>, it fell also into the <s>Gaṅgā</s>;
cast outside by her too, as she was being scorched,
from the impurities of that seed the metals that cause perfection were born.
As long as the semen fell from the mouth of <s>Agni</s>, rich in essence,
it created five wells, a hundred <s>yojanas</s> deep.
From that time onward, that semen, situated in the wells, became fivefold.

children.text: raso rasendraḥ sūtaś ca pārado miśrakastathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s>, <s>Rasendra</s>, <s>Sūta</s>, <s>Pārada</s>, and <s>Miśraka</s> —

children.text: iti pañcavidho jātaḥ kṣetrabhedena śaṃbhujaḥ // VRrs_1.68 //
children.translated_text: thus fivefold was born the offspring of <s>Śambhu</s>, differentiated by the region.
<s>Rasa</s> is red, free from all defects, and a <s>rasāyana</s> (elixir of rejuvenation);
from it the gods were born — free from disease, free from old age, and immortal.
<s>Rasendra</s> is free from defects, dark-colored, dry, and very mobile;
from it the <s>Nāgas</s> (serpents) became seekers of the elixir, freed from death and old age.

children.text: devairnāgaiś ca tau kūpau pūritau mṛdbhiraśmabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: By the gods and <s>Nāgas</s>, those two wells were filled with earth and stones;
from that time onward, those two became extremely rare for the people of the world.

children.text: īṣatpītaś ca rūkṣāṅgo doṣayuktaś ca sūtakaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūtaka</s> (mercury) is slightly yellow, dry-bodied, and endowed with defects;

children.text: daśāṣṭasaṃskṛtaiḥ siddho dehaṃ lohaṃ karoti saḥ // VRrs_1.72 //
children.translated_text: when perfected through the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory processes), it transforms both the body and metals.
Now, another type — the mine-born (<s>kūpaja</s>) — is mobile and white in color;

children.text: pārado vividhairyogaiḥ sarvarogaharaḥ sa hi // VRrs_1.73 //
children.translated_text: that <s>pārada</s> (mercury), through various preparations, is indeed the destroyer of all diseases. // VRrs_1.73 //
That mercury which has the hue of a peacock's eye-spot is considered the mixed (<s>miśraka</s>) type;
it too, when endowed with the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory processes), is exceedingly efficacious. // VRrs_1.74 //
The three types of mercury beginning with <s>sūta</s> are all capable of bestowing all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments),
and through their respective processing procedures, they possess power to an extraordinary degree. // VRrs_1.75 //

children.text: etāṃ rasasamutpattiṃ yo jānāti sa dhārmikaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who knows this origin of mercury is a righteous person;
he obtains longevity, health, progeny, and the <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) of mercury. // VRrs_1.76 //
Because it pervades (<s>rasana</s>) all metals, it is called <s>rasa</s>;

children.text: jarāruṅmṛtyunāśāya rasyate vā raso mataḥ // VRrs_1.77 //
children.translated_text: or because it is relished (<s>rasyate</s>) for the destruction of old age, disease, and death, it is considered <s>rasa</s>. // VRrs_1.77 //
Because of its sovereignty over <s>rasa</s>s (mercury preparations) and <s>uparasas</s> (subsidiary minerals), it is celebrated as <s>Rasendra</s> (lord of mercury);

children.text: dehalohamayīṃ siddhiṃ sūte sūtastataḥ smṛtaḥ // VRrs_1.78 //
children.translated_text: because it produces (<s>sūte</s>) perfection regarding both body and metals, it is called <s>sūta</s>. // VRrs_1.78 //
Because it delivers (<s>pāradānāt</s>) those drowning in the mire-ocean of disease, it is called <s>pārada</s>;
wherein the radiance of all metals resides in combined form, // VRrs_1.79 //
therefore it is called <s>miśraka</s> (mixed), bestowing fruits of various kinds.
Of such <s>sūta</s> (mercury), which severs the mortality, death, and disease of mortals,
by its power, humans became equal to the gods in strength and lifespan. // VRrs_1.80 //
Seeing them, <s>Rudra</s> was entreated by <s>Indra</s>, and thereupon

children.text: doṣaiś ca kañcukābhiś ca rasarājo niyojitaḥ // VRrs_1.81 //
children.translated_text: the king of mercury was bound with defects (<s>doṣas</s>) and sheaths (<s>kañcukas</s>). // VRrs_1.81 //
From that time onward, that <s>sūta</s> (mercury) does not become perfected without purificatory processing (<s>saṃskāra</s>).

children.text: jalago jalarūpeṇa tvarito haṃsago bhavet // VRrs_1.82 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jalaga</s> (water-movement) — in the form of water it becomes swift; <s>haṃsaga</s> (swan-movement) it would be; // VRrs_1.82 //
<s>malaga</s> (impurity-movement) — in the form of impurity; with smoke it becomes <s>dhūmaga</s> (smoke-movement);
another is the divine life-movement (<s>jīvagati</s>) — the life-force departs like a bird from an egg. // VRrs_1.83 //

children.text: sa tāṃś ca jīvayejjīvāṃstena jīvo rasaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: It enlivens those living beings, and therefore mercury is called <s>jīva</s> (life);

children.text: catasro gatayo dṛśyā adṛśyā pañcamī gatiḥ // VRrs_1.84 //
children.translated_text: four movements are visible, and the fifth movement is invisible. // VRrs_1.84 //

body.text: mantradhyānādinā tasya rudhyate pañcamī gatiḥ // VRrs_1.85 //
body.translated_text: Through <s>mantra</s>, <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and other means, its fifth movement is restrained. // VRrs_1.85 //

children.translated_text: Thus, because of these different movements, the sovereignty of mercury is difficult to attain;

children.text: saṃskārastasya bhiṣajā nipuṇena tu rakṣayet // VRrs_1.86 //
children.translated_text: its processing should be carefully guarded by a skillful physician. // VRrs_1.86 //
A bride, bathed during her first menstruation, mounted on a horse, beautifully adorned,

children.text: vīkṣamāṇāṃ vadhūṃ dṛṣṭvā jighṛkṣuḥ kūpago rasaḥ // VRrs_1.87 //
children.translated_text: gazing about — seeing her, the mine-dwelling mercury, desiring to seize her, // VRrs_1.87 //

children.text: udgacchati javātsāpi taṃ dṛṣṭvā yāti vegataḥ /
children.translated_text: rises up swiftly; she too, seeing it, departs with speed;

children.text: anugacchati tāṃ sūtaḥ sīmānaṃ yojanonmitam // VRrs_1.88 //
children.translated_text: the mercury follows her up to a boundary measuring one <s>yojana</s> (league). // VRrs_1.88 //
Then it swiftly returns to the mine, that offspring of <s>Śiva</s>.
They collect the <s>pārada</s> (mercury) settled in pits dug along the path;
having fallen in the <s>Darada</s> region due to its weight, from the mouth of fire. // VRrs_1.89 //
That mercury, absorbed into the earth, the inhabitants of those respective regions

children.text: tāṃ mṛdaṃ pātanāyantre kṣiptvā sūtaṃ haranti ca // VRrs_1.90 //
children.translated_text: cast that earth into a distillation apparatus and extract the mercury. // VRrs_1.90 //
Thus, in the composition of the illustrious <s>Vāgbhaṭācārya</s>, son of <s>Siṃhagupta</s>, the chief physician —
in the <s>Rasaratnasamuccaya</s>, the chapter named 'The Origin of Mercury' (<s>Rasotpatti</s>) —
the first chapter. || 1 ||

body.text: atha dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Now, the second chapter.

body.text: mahārasāḥ
body.translated_text: The Great Mineral Substances (<s>Mahārasas</s>)

children.translated_text: <s>Abhra</s> (mica), <s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>Mākṣīka</s> (pyrite), <s>Vimala</s>, <s>Adrija</s> (shilajit), <s>Syaka</s>,
<s>Capala</s> (bismuth), and <s>Rasaka</s> (zinc ore) — knowing these eight, one should collect the <s>rasas</s> (mineral substances). // VRrs_2.1 //

body.text: devyā rajo bhavedgandho dhātuḥ śukraṃ tathābhrakam iti kṣepakaḥ
body.translated_text: The menstrual flow of the Goddess becomes the fragrance; <s>dhātu</s> (metal) is the semen; and <s>abhra</s> (mica) likewise — thus is the interpolated verse.

children.text: gaurītejaḥ paramamamṛtaṃ vātapittakṣayaghnaṃ prajñābodhi praśamitarujaṃ vṛṣyamāyuṣyamagryam /
children.translated_text: The supreme radiance of <s>Gaurī</s> (Pārvatī), an ambrosia that destroys <s>Vāta</s> (wind), <s>Pitta</s> (bile), and consumption, awakening wisdom, pacifying diseases, aphrodisiac, promoting longevity, and foremost;

children.text: balyaṃ snigdhaṃ rucidamakaphaṃ dīpanaṃ śītavīryaṃ tattadyogaiḥ sakalagadahṛdvyoma sūtendrabandhi // VRrs_2.3 //
children.translated_text: strengthening, unctuous, appetizing, destroying <s>Kapha</s> (phlegm), digestive stimulant, cool in potency — <s>vyoma</s> (mica), through various preparations, destroys all diseases and binds <s>Sūtendra</s> (the lord of mercury). // VRrs_2.3 //
That which is extracted from below the hands of the king (the upper strata) of a mine, being dense,
yields the stated results; that which is devoid of essence (<s>sattva</s>) is utterly fruitless. // VRrs_2.4 //
<s>Pināka</s>, <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Maṇḍūka</s>, and <s>Vajra</s> — thus is <s>abhraka</s> (mica) classified;
by color distinctions of white and so forth, each is again fourfold. // VRrs_2.5 //
<s>Pināka</s> mica, when heated by fire, releases layers of flakes;

children.text: tatsevitaṃ malaṃ baddhvā mārayatyeva mānavam // VRrs_2.6 //
children.translated_text: when consumed, it binds impurities and indeed kills a person. // VRrs_2.6 //
<s>Nāga</s> mica, when placed in fire, produces a sound like a serpent;

children.text: tadbhuktaṃ kurute kuṣṭhaṃ maṇḍalākhyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ // VRrs_2.7 //
children.translated_text: when consumed, it causes the skin disease called <s>maṇḍala</s> (circular leprosy), without doubt. // VRrs_2.7 //
<s>Maṇḍūka</s> (frog-type) mica, when smelted, jumps and falls repeatedly;
it causes urinary stone disease (<s>aśmarī</s>), incurable except by surgery. // VRrs_2.8 //
<s>Vajra</s> (diamond-type) mica, when heated by fire, is freed from all impurities;
it effects transformation of body and metals, and is the supreme destroyer of all diseases. // VRrs_2.9 //

children.text: śvetaṃ raktaṃ ca pītaṃ ca kṛṣṇamevaṃ caturvidham /
children.translated_text: White, red, yellow, and black — thus it is fourfold.
The white is prescribed for white (silver) procedures; the red-hued for red (gold) procedures;
that mica which is yellow-hued is best for yellow (gold-making) procedures. // VRrs_2.10 //
Although <s>vyoma</s> (mica) is said to be excellent in all four varieties for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation),
nevertheless, the black-colored mica is superior by tens of millions of times. // VRrs_2.11 //
Unctuous, with broad flakes, endowed with luster, heavy in weight,
with easily separable leaves — such mica is declared to be excellent. // VRrs_2.12 //

children.text: sacandrikaṃ ca kiṭṭābhaṃ vyoma na grāsayedrasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mica that has a sparkle (<s>candrikā</s>) and a slag-like appearance — mercury will not devour it;

children.text: grasitaś ca niyojyo 'sau lohe caiva rasāyane // VRrs_2.13 //
children.translated_text: and that which is devoured should be employed in metallic and <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) preparations. // VRrs_2.13 //

children.text: niścandrikaṃ mṛtaṃ vyoma sevyaṃ sargadeṣu ca /
children.translated_text: Mica that is sparkle-free and calcined (<s>mṛta</s>) is to be used in disease treatments;

children.text: sevitaṃ candrasaṃyuktaṃ mehaṃ mandānalaṃ caret // VRrs_2.14 //
children.translated_text: if the sparkle-bearing type is consumed, it causes diabetes (<s>meha</s>) and weak digestion. // VRrs_2.14 //
Those who, devoid of proper methodology, have prescribed leaf-mica as a <s>rasāyana</s>,
they have seen the <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison as a means of sustaining life! // VRrs_2.15 //
For extracting <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence) and for medicinal use, one should employ purified mica;

children.text: anyathā tvaguṇaṃ kṛtvā vikarotyeva niścitam // VRrs_2.16 //
children.translated_text: otherwise, being rendered devoid of virtue, it certainly causes harm. // VRrs_2.16 //
Mica heated seven times and immersed in sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>)

children.text: nirdoṣaṃ jāyate nūnaṃ prakṣiptaṃ vāpi gojale // VRrs_2.17 //
children.translated_text: becomes free of defects; or it may be cast into cow's urine. // VRrs_2.17 //
Also in a decoction of <s>Triphalā</s>, or especially in cow's milk;

children.text: tato dhānyābhrakaṃ kṛtvā piṣṭvā matsyākṣikārasaiḥ // VRrs_2.18 //
children.translated_text: then, having prepared <s>dhānyābhra</s> (grain-mica), grinding it with <s>matsyākṣikā</s> (a mineral) juices, // VRrs_2.18 //
making it into a cake, drying it, and calcining it with a half-elephant <s>puṭa</s> (calcination process),

children.text: puṭedevaṃ hi ṣaḍvāraṃ paunarnavarasaiḥ saha // VRrs_2.19 //
children.translated_text: calcining thus six times with the juices of <s>Punarnava</s> (Boerhavia diffusa), // VRrs_2.19 //
grinding with one-quarter measure of borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>) and forming into cakes,
one should calcine it seven times with half-elephant <s>puṭa</s>s in the same manner. // VRrs_2.20 //
Likewise, with the juice of <s>Vāsā</s> (Adhatoda vasica) and with <s>Taṇḍulīya</s> (Amaranthus) juice,
one should calcine it seven times according to the previously stated procedure. // VRrs_2.21 //

body.text: evaṃ siddhaṃ ghanaṃ sarvayogeṣu viniyojayet // VRrs_2.22 //
body.translated_text: The mica thus perfected and dense should be employed in all preparations. // VRrs_2.22 //

children.translated_text: Powdered mica combined with rice (<s>Śāli</s>), tied in cloth, (placed) in sour gruel —
what passes through the cloth by grinding is called <s>dhānyābhra</s> (grain-mica). // VRrs_2.23 //
<s>Dhānyābhra</s> ground with the juice of <s>Kāsamarda</s> (Cassia occidentalis)

children.text: puṭitaṃ daśavāreṇa mriyate nātra saṃśayaḥ // VRrs_2.24 //
children.translated_text: and calcined ten times is killed (calcined) — there is no doubt about this. // VRrs_2.24 //
Similarly, with <s>Mustā</s> (Cyperus rotundus) juice and <s>Taṇḍulīya</s> (Amaranthus) juice,
mica made into cakes, ground with yellow <s>Āmalaka</s> (Emblica) and <s>Saubhāgya</s> (a mineral), // VRrs_2.25 //
calcined sixty times, becomes vermilion-colored;
it destroys all diseases beginning with consumption, according to the disease-specific vehicle (<s>anupāna</s>). // VRrs_2.26 //
With decoctions of the bark of <s>Vaṭa</s> (banyan) root, with the essence of betel (<s>Tāmbūlī</s>) leaves,
with <s>Vāsā</s> and <s>Matsyākṣikā</s>, or with <s>Mīnākṣī</s> (a plant) and <s>Kaṭilla</s> (a plant), // VRrs_2.27 //
ground with the latex of the banyan tree and calcined — the dense (mica)
becomes vermilion-colored after twenty times. // VRrs_2.28 //
Combined with one-quarter part borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), ground with <s>Musalī</s> (Curculigo) juice,

children.text: rundhyātkoṣṭyāṃ dṛḍhaṃ dhmātaṃ sattvarūpaṃ bhaved dhanam // VRrs_2.29 //
children.translated_text: firmly sealed in a crucible (<s>koṣṭhī</s>) and smelted — the metallic essence (<s>sattva</s>) is obtained as wealth. // VRrs_2.29 //
With the juices of <s>Kāsamarda</s>, <s>Ghana</s> (Cyperus), <s>Dhvana</s>, <s>Vāsā</s>, and <s>Punarbhū</s> (Punarnava),

children.text: matsyākṣyāḥ kāṇḍavallyāś ca haṃsapādyā rasaiḥ pṛthak // VRrs_2.30 //
children.translated_text: <s>Matsyākṣī</s>, <s>Kāṇḍavallī</s>, and <s>Haṃsapādī</s> — separately, // VRrs_2.30 //
grinding and grinding with effort, one should dry it according to the proper method.

children.text: palaṃ godhūmacūrṇasya kṣudramatsyāś ca ṭaṅkaṇam // VRrs_2.31 //
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of wheat flour, small fish, and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), // VRrs_2.31 //
adding one-eighth part of each, one should grind repeatedly;
after each grinding, one should properly dry it in sunlight. // VRrs_2.32 //
The five products of a goat (<s>pañcāja</s>), or the five products of a cow (<s>pañcagavya</s>), or the five products of a buffalo (<s>pañcamāhiṣa</s>) —
adding these, one should make balls slightly larger than a <s>Tinduka</s> (Diospyros) fruit. // VRrs_2.33 //

children.text: payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ mūtraṃ saviṭkaṃ cājamucyate /
children.translated_text: Milk, curd, ghee, urine, and dung — these are called (the five products) of a goat.

children.text: adhaḥpātanakoṣṭyāṃ hi dhmātvā sattvaṃ nipātayet // VRrs_2.34 //
children.translated_text: In a downward-distillation crucible, having smelted, one should cause the <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence) to fall downward. // VRrs_2.34 //
Collecting the slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>) from the crucible, powdering it, one should extract the droplets;

children.text: tatkiṭṭaṃ svalpaṭaṅkena gomayena vimardya ca // VRrs_2.35 //
children.translated_text: that slag, with a little borax and cow-dung, ground together, // VRrs_2.35 //
made into balls, dried in the sun, and again as before,

children.text: bhūyaḥ kiṭṭaṃ samāhṛtya mṛditvā sattvamāharet // VRrs_2.36 //
children.translated_text: collecting the slag again, softening it, one should extract the essence. // VRrs_2.36 //
Then those essence-granules should be boiled with sour gruel (<s>āmlakāñjika</s>);
combined with purifying substances (<s>śodhanīyagaṇa</s>) and sealed in a crucible, // VRrs_2.37 //
properly melted and collected, one should smelt the metal twice;

children.text: iti śuddhaṃ bhavetsattvaṃ yojyaṃ rasarasāyane // VRrs_2.38 //
children.translated_text: thus the <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence) becomes purified, fit for use in mercury and <s>rasāyana</s> preparations. // VRrs_2.38 //
Melted and quenched in honey, oil, <s>Vāsā</s> (Adhatoda) juice, and ghee,

children.text: mṛdu syāddaśavāreṇa sattvaṃ lohādikaṃ kharam // VRrs_2.39 //
children.translated_text: the <s>sattva</s> (essence) of metals and such becomes soft after ten times; (otherwise) it is hard. // VRrs_2.39 //
Then, having made it into thin plate-powder and saturated with cow's ghee,
one should roast it seven times on a potsherd placed on a stove. // VRrs_2.40 //
Until it becomes fire-colored, one should powder it each time;

children.text: tṛṇaṃ kṣiptvā dahedyāvattāvadvā bharjanaṃ caret // VRrs_2.41 //
children.translated_text: or one should continue roasting until straw thrown on it burns. // VRrs_2.41 //
Then, grinding it with sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>) using a decoction of banyan root,
one should calcine it twenty times with the <s>Vārāha</s> (boar) <s>puṭa</s> (calcination method). // VRrs_2.42 //
Again twenty times with a decoction prepared from <s>Triphalā</s>;
with <s>Triphalā</s>, <s>Muṇḍikā</s>, <s>Bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), leaves, <s>Pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula), and <s>Akṣamūlaka</s> (Vibhītaka root), // VRrs_2.43 //
having macerated, it should be administered in proper doses for all diseases.
Nothing is more beneficial than <s>sattva</s> (essence) of mica — it is free from side effects and superior in qualities. // VRrs_2.44 //
If thus processed with a hundred calcinations by <s>puṭapāka</s>,
it becomes exceedingly virtuous — a supreme digestive and appetizer. // VRrs_2.45 //
Macerated with <s>Gandharvapatrā</s> (castor leaf) water and jaggery,

children.text: adhordhvaṃ vaṭapatrāṇi niścandraṃ tripuṭaiḥ khagam // VRrs_2.46 //
children.translated_text: (placed) between banyan leaves above and below, the sparkle-free mica (calcined) with three <s>puṭa</s>s, // VRrs_2.46 //
produces extreme hunger when taken in a dose of half a <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seed);
combined with disease-specific preparations, it is the supreme destroyer of all diseases. // VRrs_2.47 //
A ball of the <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence), smelted and (placed) in grain-mixed sour gruel,
quenched — immediately one should hammer it with an iron mallet. // VRrs_2.48 //
Reheating the thick dense granules and casting them in sour gruel,
immediately collecting and hammering them, one should reduce them to powder. // VRrs_2.49 //
That powder should be roasted in cow's ghee as before, three times;
similarly with <s>Dhātrī</s> (Āmalaka/Emblica) fruit juice, or with <s>Dhātrī</s> leaf juice, // VRrs_2.50 //
after each roasting, one should grind it on a stone slab;
then, with juices of <s>Punarnava</s> (Boerhavia) and <s>Vāsā</s> (Adhatoda) mixed with sour gruel, // VRrs_2.51 //
one should calcine it ten times, and ten times with sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>);
thus purified, the <s>sattva</s> (essence) of mica is supreme in all qualities. // VRrs_2.52 //
It should be employed as desired in <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation of mercury) and <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) preparations.

children.text: drutayo naiva nirdiṣṭāḥ śāstre dṛṣṭā api dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: The meltings (<s>druti</s>) are not prescribed in the treatises, though they have been firmly observed;

children.text: vinā śaṃbhoḥ prasādena na sidhyanti kadācana // VRrs_2.53 //
children.translated_text: without the grace of <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), they never succeed. // VRrs_2.53 //

children.text: vellavyoṣasamanvitaṃ ghṛtayutaṃ vallonmitaṃ sevitaṃ divyābhraṃ kṣayapāṇḍuruggrahaṇikāśūlāmakuṣṭhāmayam /
children.translated_text: The divine mica, combined with <s>Vella</s> (Embelia) and <s>Vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), mixed with ghee, taken in the measure of a <s>Valla</s>, destroys consumption, anemia, severe <s>Grahaṇī</s> (sprue), colic, <s>Āma</s> (undigested toxins), and skin diseases;

children.text: jūrtiṃ śvāsagadaṃ pramehamaruciṃ kāsāmayaṃ durdharaṃ mandāgniṃ jaṭharavyathāṃ vijayate yogairaśeṣāmayān // VRrs_2.54 //
children.translated_text: It conquers indigestion, asthma, diabetes (<s>prameha</s>), loss of appetite, severe cough, sluggish digestive fire, abdominal pain, and all diseases through (various) preparations. // VRrs_2.54 //
Now, <s>Vaikrānta</s> (tourmaline) —
Eight-edged, with eight facets, six-cornered, smooth, and heavy,

children.text: śuddhamiśritavarṇaiś ca yukto vaikrānta ucyate // VRrs_2.55 //
children.translated_text: endowed with pure and mixed colors — it is called <s>Vaikrānta</s>. // VRrs_2.55 //

children.text: śveto raktaś ca pītaś ca nīlaḥ pārāpatacchaviḥ /
children.translated_text: White, red, yellow, blue, pigeon-colored,

children.text: śyāmalaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇaś ca karburaścāṣṭadhā hi saḥ // VRrs_2.56 //
children.translated_text: dark, black, and mottled — thus it is of eight kinds. // VRrs_2.56 //
It bestows longevity, gives strength and complexion, is extremely aphrodisiac,
grants wisdom, removes all humoral disorders and diseases,
stimulates the digestive fire, possesses qualities equal to the thunderbolt, and is vigorous —
<s>Vaikrānta</s> indeed acts upon the body and metals (making them strong). // VRrs_2.57 //
Among all <s>rasāyana</s>s (rejuvenation preparations), it is to be counted foremost, possessing great efficacy;
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, the destroyer of all disorders, should be employed in the place of diamond. // VRrs_2.58 //
In another text:
The lord of the <s>Daitya</s>s (demons), <s>Māhiṣa</s> (the buffalo-demon), was accomplished, born from <s>Sahadeva</s>.

children.text: durgā bhagavatī devī taṃ śūlena vyamardayat // VRrs_2.59 //
children.translated_text: The goddess <s>Durgā</s>, the blessed deity, crushed him with her trident. // VRrs_2.59 //

children.text: tasya raktaṃ tu patitaṃ yatra yatra sthitaṃ bhuvi /
children.translated_text: Wherever his blood fell and remained on the earth,

children.text: tatra tatra tu vaikrāntaṃ vajrākāraṃ mahārasam // VRrs_2.60 //
children.translated_text: there <s>Vaikrānta</s>, diamond-shaped and of great essence, (appeared). // VRrs_2.60 //

children.text: vindhyasya dakṣiṇe vāsti hyuttare vāsti sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: It is found south of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains, or to the north, or everywhere.

children.text: vikṛntayati lohāni tena vaikrāntakaḥ smṛtaḥ // VRrs_2.61 //
children.translated_text: Because it cuts metals, it is known as <s>Vaikrānta</s>. // VRrs_2.61 //
White, yellow, red, blue, pigeon-hued,
one resembling a peacock's neck, and another with the luster of emerald. // VRrs_2.62 //

children.text: dehasiddhikaraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ pīte pītaṃ site sitam /
children.translated_text: The black one accomplishes bodily perfection (<s>dehasiddhi</s>); yellow for yellow (gold), white for white (silver);
the red one grants the accomplishment of all purposes; likewise the emerald-hued one. // VRrs_2.63 //

body.text: śeṣe dve niṣphale varjye vaikrāntamiti saptadhā // VRrs_2.64 //
body.translated_text: The remaining two are fruitless and should be avoided; thus <s>Vaikrānta</s> is of seven kinds. // VRrs_2.64 //

children.translated_text: Now, the method of collection —

children.text: yatra kṣetre sthitaṃ caiva vaikrāntaṃ tatra bhairavam /
children.translated_text: In whatever field <s>Vaikrānta</s> is found, there one should worship <s>Bhairava</s>
and <s>Vināyaka</s> (Gaṇeśa), and collect it with a pure mind. // VRrs_2.65 //
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, resembling diamond, is regarded as acting on the body and metals;
it destroys poison, is the king of <s>rasa</s>s (mercury preparations), and removes fever, leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), and consumption. // VRrs_2.66 //

children.text: vaikrāntakāḥ syustridinaṃ viśuddhāḥ saṃsveditāḥ kṣārapaṭūni datvā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s>s become purified in three days by being steamed with alkaline and pungent substances,
in sour liquids, urines, horse-gram and plantain water, or cooked in <s>Kodrava</s> (millet) water. // VRrs_2.67 //
<s>Vaikrānta</s> steamed in horse-gram decoction becomes purified.
It is calcined (<s>mriyate</s>) with eight <s>puṭa</s>s (calcination cycles), combined with sulfur and lemon juice. // VRrs_2.68 //
Into heated <s>Vaikrānta</s>s, one should cast horse urine;

children.text: paunaḥpunyena vā kuryāddravaṃ datvā puṭaṃ tvanu // VRrs_2.69 //
children.translated_text: or one should repeatedly apply liquid and then perform <s>puṭa</s> (calcination). // VRrs_2.69 //
<s>Vaikrānta</s> reduced to ash should be employed in the place of diamond,
treated with the alkali of <s>Mokṣa</s> (Moringa), <s>Moraṭa</s>, and <s>Palāśa</s> (Butea), and cow's urine. // VRrs_2.70 //
Combined with the paste of <s>Vajrakanda</s>, turmeric (<s>niśā</s>), and fruit powder,
that paste with borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), lac (<s>lākṣā</s>) powder, derived from <s>Vaikrānta</s>, // VRrs_2.71 //
combined with sal ammoniac (<s>navasāra</s>) and the juice of <s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s>,

children.text: piṇḍitaṃ mūkamūṣasthaṃ dhmāpitaṃ ca haṭhāgninā // VRrs_2.72 //
children.translated_text: formed into a ball, placed in a sealed crucible (<s>mūkamūṣā</s>), and smelted with intense fire — // VRrs_2.72 //

children.text: tatraiva patate sattvaṃ vaikrāntasya na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: the essence (<s>sattva</s>) of <s>Vaikrānta</s> falls therein, without doubt.
Through the method of extracting the essence, it is ground and made into pills;
placed in a crucible and blown for one <s>ghaṭikā</s> (24 minutes), <s>Vaikrānta</s> releases its essence. // VRrs_2.73 //

children.text: bhasmatvaṃ samupāgato vikṛtako hemnā mṛtenānvitaḥ pādāṃśena kaṇājyavellasahito guñjāmitaḥ sevitaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s> reduced to ash, combined with calcined gold (<s>hema mṛta</s>), with one-quarter portion of <s>Kaṇā</s> (long pepper), ghee, and <s>Vella</s> (Embelia), taken in the dose of one <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seed),

children.text: yakṣmāṇaṃ jaraṇaṃ ca pāṇḍugudajaṃ śvāsaṃ ca kāsāmayaṃ duṣṭāṃ ca grahaṇīmuraḥkṣatamukhānrogāñjayyeddehakṛt // VRrs_2.74 //
children.translated_text: conquers consumption (<s>yakṣman</s>), chronic fever, diseases born of anemia and piles, asthma, cough, corrupted <s>grahaṇī</s> (sprue), chest wounds, and all diseases — it builds the body. // VRrs_2.74 //
The ash of blue <s>Vaikrānta</s> combined with half (its weight of) mercury ash,
with the essence of calcined mica (<s>abhra</s>), the two (being) weighed equally and ground together, // VRrs_2.75 //
taken in the morning in the dose of one <s>guñjā</s>, mixed with honey and ghee,
it destroys all diseases that are incurable by other medicines,
in thrice-seven (twenty-one) days for men — like the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> (destroy) sin. // VRrs_2.76 //
Now, <s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrite/chalcopyrite) —
Born from the golden mountain, the golden <s>rasa</s> (essence) is (associated with) <s>Viṣṇu</s>;

children.text: tāpyāṃ kirātacīneṣu yavaneṣu ca nirmitaḥ // VRrs_2.77 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Tāpya</s> (iron pyrite) variety is found among the <s>Kirāta</s>s, Chinese, and <s>Yavana</s>s (Greeks). // VRrs_2.77 //
<s>Tāpya</s>, heated by sunbeams, is visible in the month of <s>Mādhava</s> (Vaiśākha);
it is sweet, with the luster of gold, slightly sour, and resembles silver. // VRrs_2.78 //
Somewhat astringent and sweet, cooling, pungent after digestion, and light;
by its regular use, one is not overcome by old age, disease, or poison. // VRrs_2.79 //
<s>Mākṣika</s> is of two kinds: gold-pyrite (<s>hemamākṣika</s>) and silver-pyrite (<s>tāramākṣika</s>).
Of these, the first <s>Mākṣika</s>, originating from <s>Kānyakubja</s>, resembles gold. // VRrs_2.80 //
That born on the banks of the <s>Tapatī</s> (Tapi river) has five colors like gold.
The one called <s>Tārā</s> (silver-variety), being stone-heavy, is said to have lesser qualities. // VRrs_2.81 //

children.text: mākṣīkadhātuḥ sakalāmayaghnaḥ prāṇo rasendrasya paraṃ hi vṛṣyaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> mineral destroys all diseases, is the life-force of the lord of <s>rasa</s>s (mercury), and is supremely aphrodisiac;
it effects the joining of two difficult-to-combine metals, is superior in qualities, and is the foremost of all <s>rasāyana</s>s. // VRrs_2.82 //
<s>Mākṣika</s> is purified when processed in castor oil and citrus water,
or processed in plantain-stem juice for two <s>ghaṭikā</s>s (48 minutes). // VRrs_2.83 //
<s>Mākṣika</s>, when heated and cast into <s>Triphala</s> decoction, attains purity.
Ground with citron water and sulfur, placed in the belly of a crucible, // VRrs_2.84 //
and calcined with five <s>Kroḍa</s> <s>puṭa</s>s (calcination cycles), <s>Mākṣika</s> is indeed killed (calcined).
With castor oil, cow products, or citron juice, // VRrs_2.85 //
firmly cooked in a shallow dish, it becomes like the mineral (metallic ash).

children.text: evaṃ mṛtaṃ rase yojyaṃ rasāyanavidhāvapi // VRrs_2.86 //
children.translated_text: Thus calcined, it should be employed in mercury preparations and in <s>rasāyana</s> procedures as well. // VRrs_2.86 //
Combined with one-thirtieth part lead, rolled with alkalies and sour substances,

children.text: dhmātaṃ prakaṭamūṣāyāṃ sattvaṃ muñcati mākṣikam // VRrs_2.87 //
children.translated_text: and smelted in an open crucible, <s>Mākṣika</s> releases its essence. // VRrs_2.87 //
After being melted seven times and cast into <s>Nirguṇḍikā</s> (Vitex) juice,
the lead mixed with <s>Mākṣika</s> essence certainly perishes. // VRrs_2.88 //
With honey, <s>Gandharvataila</s> (castor oil), cow's urine, and ghee,
and with the essence of plantain stem, <s>Mākṣika</s> is treated repeatedly. // VRrs_2.89 //

body.text: mūṣāyāṃ muñcati dhmātaṃ sattvaṃ śulbanibhaṃ mṛdu // VRrs_2.90 //
body.translated_text: When smelted in a crucible, it releases a soft essence resembling copper. // VRrs_2.90 //

children.translated_text: With a color like <s>Guñjā</s> (Abrus) seeds, quick-flowing and cool,
that purified <s>Tāpya</s> essence is supreme in acting on body and metals. // VRrs_2.91 //

children.text: mākṣīkasattvena rasendrapiṣṭaṃ kṛtvā vilīne ca baliṃ nidhāya /
children.translated_text: Mercury ground with <s>Mākṣika</s> essence, having placed an offering (<s>bali</s>) in the melted (substance),

children.text: saṃmiśrya saṃmardya ca khalvamadhye nikṣipya sattvaṃ drutimabhrakasya // VRrs_2.92 //
children.translated_text: mixing and grinding in a mortar, casting in the essence and the fluid of mica — // VRrs_2.92 //

children.text: vidhāya golaṃ lavaṇākhyayantre paceddinārdhaṃ mṛduvahninā ca /
children.translated_text: forming into a ball and cooking in a <s>Lavaṇa</s> apparatus (salt-sealed vessel) for half a day with gentle fire,

children.text: svataḥ suśītaṃ paricūrṇya samyagvallonmitaṃ vyoṣaviḍaṅgayuktam // VRrs_2.93 //
children.translated_text: when it cools naturally, grinding it well, measured by the <s>Valla</s> (dosage), combined with <s>Vyoṣa</s> (three pungents) and <s>Viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia) — // VRrs_2.93 //

children.text: saṃsevitaṃ kṣaudrayutaṃ nihanti jarāṃ sarogāṃ tvapamṛtyumeva /
children.translated_text: taken with honey, it destroys old age with all its diseases and even untimely death;
it conquers even incurable diseases in seven days — not even the nectar of immortality (<s>sudhārasa</s>) is its equal. // VRrs_2.94 //
With castor oil, one <s>Ṭaṅka</s> measure of <s>Guñjā</s> and honey,

children.text: marditaṃ tasya vāpena sattvaṃ mākṣīkajaṃ dravet // VRrs_2.95 //
children.translated_text: ground and smelted with its vapors, the <s>Mākṣika</s>-born essence flows. // VRrs_2.95 //
Now, <s>Vimala</s> (a mineral) —
<s>Vimala</s> is declared to be of three kinds: the gold variety first, then the silver variety,
and the third is bronze-<s>Vimala</s>; each is identified by its respective luster. // VRrs_2.96 //
Round, having corners, unctuous, and possessing facets;
<s>Vimala</s> removes <s>Vāta</s> (wind) and <s>Pitta</s> (bile), is aphrodisiac, and is a great <s>rasāyana</s>. // VRrs_2.97 //
The first is prescribed for gold-making procedures, the second is regarded as producing silver;

children.text: tṛtīyo bheṣaje teṣu pūrvapūrvo guṇottaraḥ // VRrs_2.98 //
children.translated_text: the third is for medicines; among them, each earlier one is superior in qualities. // VRrs_2.98 //
<s>Vimala</s> steamed in <s>Āṭarūṣa</s> (Adhatoda vasica) water becomes pure.
Steamed in lemon juice, or in the juice of <s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, // VRrs_2.99 //

children.text: āyāti śuddhiṃ vimalo dhātavaś ca yathā pare /
children.translated_text: <s>Vimala</s> attains purity — and the other minerals likewise.

children.text: gandhāśmalakucāmlaiś ca mriyate daśabhiḥ puṭaiḥ // VRrs_2.100 //
children.translated_text: It is calcined with ten <s>puṭa</s>s using sulfur, <s>Aśmala</s> (stone), and sour <s>Kucu</s> (substances). // VRrs_2.100 //
Ground with borax, <s>Kucu</s> juices, and the ash of <s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s>,

children.text: piṣṭo mūṣodare liptaḥ saṃśoṣya ca nirudhya ca // VRrs_2.101 //
children.translated_text: smeared inside a crucible, dried, and sealed, // VRrs_2.101 //
<s>Vimala</s>, when smelted with six <s>Prastha</s>s of <s>Kokila</s> (charcoal), releases

children.text: sattvaṃ muñcati tadyukto rasaḥ syātsa rasāyanaḥ // VRrs_2.102 //
children.translated_text: an essence resembling lead; combined with it, <s>rasa</s> (mercury) becomes a <s>rasāyana</s>. // VRrs_2.102 //
<s>Vimala</s> with <s>Śigru</s> (Moringa) water, <s>Kāṅkṣī</s> (alum), <s>Kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), and borax,
combined with <s>Vajrakanda</s>, treated with plantain juices, // VRrs_2.103 //
combined with <s>Mokṣaka</s> alkali, placed in a sealed crucible and smelted —

children.text: sattvaṃ candrārkasaṃkāśaṃ patate nātra saṃśayaḥ // VRrs_2.104 //
children.translated_text: an essence resembling the moon and sun falls therein, without doubt. // VRrs_2.104 //
That essence combined with mercury, ground and well-mixed,
cast into melted sulfur, one should digest it with three times (its weight of) hair (alkali). // VRrs_2.105 //
And with five times (its weight of) realgar (<s>śilā</s>), indeed in a sand-bath apparatus;
with one-tenth part calcined silver (<s>tārabhasma</s>) and that much calcined <s>Vaikrānta</s>, // VRrs_2.105 //
all powdered together and filtered through cloth,
placed in a bottle (<s>kūpikā</s>) and filled carefully — // VRrs_2.107 //

children.text: līḍho vyoṣavarānvito vimalako yukto ghṛtaiḥ sevito hanyāddurbhagakṛjjvarāñśvayathukaṃ pāṇḍupramehārucīḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vimala</s>, licked with <s>Vyoṣa</s> (three pungents) and <s>Triphala</s>, combined with ghee and taken, destroys misfortune-causing fevers, swelling, anemia, diabetes, and loss of appetite,

children.text: mūlārtiṃ grahaṇīṃ ca śūlamatulaṃ yakṣmāmayaṃ kāmalāṃ sarvānpittamarudgadānkimaparairyogairaśeṣāmayān // VRrs_2.108 //
children.translated_text: hemorrhoids, <s>Grahaṇī</s> (sprue), unparalleled colic, consumption, jaundice (<s>kāmalā</s>), all <s>Pitta</s> and <s>Vāta</s> diseases — what need of other preparations? — and all diseases. // VRrs_2.108 //

body.text: iti vimalaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus <s>Vimala</s> //

children.translated_text: Now, <s>Śilādhātu</s> (bitumen/shilajit) —
<s>Śilādhātu</s> is declared to be of two kinds: the first, (used with) cow's urine, is a <s>rasāyana</s>;
and the other, preceded by 'camphor' (camphor-like); of these, the first is again twofold. // VRrs_2.109 //
With essence and without essence; of the two, the former has superior qualities.
In summer, from the feet of the snow-bearing mountain (<s>Himālaya</s>) intensely heated by the sun, // VRrs_2.110 //
from (mountains) bearing gold, silver, and copper ores, <s>Śilādhātu</s> exudes.
That born from a gold-bearing mountain is heavy, resembling the <s>Japā</s> (hibiscus) flower; // VRrs_2.111 //
slightly bitter yet very sweet, it is the supreme <s>rasāyana</s>.
That born from a silver-bearing mountain is sweet, whitish, and heavy. // VRrs_2.112 //
That <s>Śilāja</s> (shilajit) destroys <s>Pitta</s> diseases and especially removes anemia (<s>pāṇḍuroga</s>).

children.text: tāmragarbhaṃ girerjātaṃ nīlavarṇaṃ ghanaṃ guru // VRrs_2.113 //
children.translated_text: That born from a copper-bearing mountain is blue-colored, dense, and heavy. // VRrs_2.113 //
That <s>Śilāja</s> destroys <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Vāta</s>, is bitter and hot, and removes consumptive diseases.
That which, when cast into fire, assumes a <s>liṅga</s>-shape (phallic form) and is smokeless,

children.text: salile 'tha vilīnaṃ ca tacchuddhaṃ hi śilājatu // VRrs_2.114 //
children.translated_text: and when dissolved in water — that is pure <s>Śilājatu</s> (shilajit). // VRrs_2.114 //

children.text: nūnaṃ sajvarapāṇḍuśophaśamanaṃ mehāgnimāndyāpahaṃ medaśchedakaraṃ ca yakṣmaśamanaṃ śūlāmayonmūlanam /
children.translated_text: It certainly alleviates fever, anemia, and swelling, removes diabetes and weak digestion, cuts fat, calms consumption, and uproots colic,

children.text: gulmaplīhavināśanaṃ jaṭharahṛcchūlaghnamāmāpahaṃ sarvatvaggadanāśanaṃ kimaparaṃ dehe ca lohe hitam // VRrs_2.115 //
children.translated_text: destroys abdominal tumors and splenic enlargement, cures stomach pain, removes undigested toxins (<s>āma</s>), destroys all skin diseases — what more? — and is beneficial for both body and metals. // VRrs_2.115 //
The qualities that reside in <s>rasa</s>s (mercury preparations), subsidiary <s>rasa</s>s, the lord of <s>rasa</s>s (mercury), gems, and metals —
they all dwell in <s>Śilādhātu</s>, with the power to conquer old age and death. // VRrs_2.116 //
<s>Śilājatu</s> is purified by washing with alkaline, sour, and cow-dung waters.
<s>Śilādhātu</s>, with milk, <s>Triphala</s>, and <s>Arka</s> (Calotropis) juices, // VRrs_2.117 //
placed in an iron vessel, should be purified with great care,
with alkaline, sour, and <s>Guggulu</s> (bdellium) substances, placed inside a steaming apparatus. // VRrs_2.118 //
<s>Śilādhātu</s>, steamed for the duration of one <s>ghaṭikā</s>, is purified.
With realgar (<s>śilā</s>), orpiment (<s>gandha</s>), and citron juice, // VRrs_2.119 //

body.text: puṭitaṃ hi śilādhātu mriyate 'ṣṭagiriṇḍakaiḥ // VRrs_2.120 //
body.translated_text: <s>Śilādhātu</s>, when calcined, is killed (calcined) with eight <s>giriṇḍaka</s> (cow-dung cake) <s>puṭa</s>s. // VRrs_2.120 //

children.text: bhasmībhūtaśilodbhavaṃ samatulaṃ kāntaṃ ca vaikrāntakaṃ yuktaṃ ca triphalākaṭutrikaghṛtairvallena tulyaṃ bhajet /
children.translated_text: The ash of rock-born (shilajit), equal in measure, combined with <s>Kānta</s> (magnetite) and <s>Vaikrānta</s>, with <s>Triphala</s>, the three pungents (<s>Kaṭutraya</s>), and ghee, should be taken in the dose of one <s>Valla</s>.

children.text: pāṇḍau yakṣmagade tathāgnisadane meheṣu mūlāmaye gulmaplīhamahodare bahuvidhe śūle ca yonyāmaye // VRrs_2.121 //
children.translated_text: in anemia, consumption, and likewise in digestive disorders, urinary diseases, hemorrhoids, abdominal tumors, splenic enlargement, ascites, various types of colic, and diseases of the womb. // VRrs_2.121 //
If one uses it for six months according to the method of <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy),
free from wrinkles and grey hair, one would live a hundred years in happiness. // VRrs_2.122 //
The mountain-born [mineral] (<s>śilājatu</s>), ground with the group of solvents and sour substances,

children.text: kṣiptvā mūṣodare ruddhvā gāḍhairdhmātaṃ hi kokilaiḥ // VRrs_2.123 //
children.translated_text: having been placed in the belly of a crucible, sealed, and strongly blown with bellows — // VRrs_2.123 //
the mineral ore releases its essence (<s>sattva</s>) through blasts, resembling metal;
white, having the appearance of sand grains — this is the camphor-type <s>śilājatu</s> (bitumen). // VRrs_2.124 //
It destroys difficulty in urination, urinary stones, urinary diseases, jaundice, and anemia.
When combined with cardamom water and processed, it attains purity;

children.text: naitasya māraṇaṃ sattvapātanaṃ vihitaṃ buddhaiḥ // VRrs_2.125 //
children.translated_text: neither killing nor extraction of essence has been prescribed for it by the wise. // VRrs_2.125 //
Now, <s>sasyaka</s> (green vitriol/copper sulfate):
Having drunk the <s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison) vomited by <s>Garutmat</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) who had drunk the nectar,
combined with poison and nectar, on the mountain called <s>Marakata</s> (Emerald) — // VRrs_2.126 //

children.text: tadvāntaṃ hi ghanībhūtaṃ saṃjātaṃ sasyakaṃ khalu /
children.translated_text: that vomited substance, having solidified, became <s>sasyaka</s> indeed;
having the true color of a peacock's neck, heavy in weight, it is highly praised. // VRrs_2.127 //
A substance combined with poison becomes superior in qualities to that substance;
<s>hālāhala</s> combined with nectar likewise becomes superior in qualities to nectar. // VRrs_2.128 //
Destroying all humoral imbalances, poisoning, cardiac disorders, colic, root diseases, leprosy, acidic and bilious conditions, and constipation, and moreover

children.text: rasāyanaṃ vamanarekakaraṃ garaghnaṃ śvitrāpahaṃ gaditamatra mayūratuttham // VRrs_2.129 //
children.translated_text: being a rejuvenative, causing emesis and purgation, destroying poisons, and removing leucoderma — thus is described peacock vitriol (<s>mayūratuttha</s>). // VRrs_2.129 //
<s>Sasyaka</s> attains purity when treated with the group of red substances;
sprinkled with the group of oils, [processed] seven times, it becomes uncontaminated. // VRrs_2.130 //
<s>Sasyaka</s>, well-steamed in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus) for three <s>praharas</s> (nine hours),
in the urine of cows, buffaloes, and goats — thus <s>pañcakharpara</s> (zinc oxide) is purified. // VRrs_2.131 //
Combined with <s>lakuca</s> (breadfruit) extract, <s>gandhāśma</s> (sulphur ore), and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),

children.text: nirudhya mūṣikāmadhye mriyate kaukvuṭaiḥ puṭaiḥ // VRrs_2.132 //
children.translated_text: confined in the interior of a crucible, it is killed by <s>kaukkuṭa</s> (hen-egg-shaped) firings. // VRrs_2.132 //
The powder of <s>sasyaka</s>, combined with a quarter portion of <s>saubhāgya</s> (good-fortune salt),
placed in <s>karañja</s> oil, should be kept for one day. // VRrs_2.133 //
Placed in the mouth of a sealed crucible, it should be blown with three bellows-blasts;

children.text: indragopākṛti caiva sattvaṃ bhavati śobhanam // VRrs_2.134 //
children.translated_text: the essence produced becomes beautiful, resembling the <s>indragopa</s> (scarlet insect). // VRrs_2.134 //
Confined in a crucible with <s>nimbu</s> (lemon) juice and a small amount of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),

children.text: tāmrarūpaṃ paridhmātaṃ sattvaṃ muñcati sasyakam // VRrs_2.135 //
children.translated_text: when thoroughly blown, <s>sasyaka</s> releases its essence in a copper-like form. // VRrs_2.135 //
Pure <s>sasyaka</s>, processed on stone, combined with the previously mentioned medicines,
through various procedural methods, it certainly releases its essence. // VRrs_2.136 //
Having obtained this essence, one who consumes the essences of donkey, earth, and <s>nāga</s> (lead) —
a ring made from it, when touched, becomes a colic-destroyer instantly. // VRrs_2.137 //
It conquers poison of mobile and immobile [beings], and [afflictions] caused by <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits), <s>ḍākinīs</s>, and the evil eye;
this ring should be made — it produces visible results. // VRrs_2.138 //
On the ring of <s>Rāmavat</s>, <s>Somasenānī</s>, these syllables also [should be inscribed]:
"On the northern slope of the <s>Himālaya</s>, there is a great tree called <s>Aśvakarṇa</s>;

children.text: tatra śūlaṃ samutpannaṃ tatraiva vilayaṃ gatam /
children.translated_text: there the colic arose, and there itself it dissolved."
The water [empowered by] this <s>mantra</s>, enchanted seven times, should be drunk from the ring. // VRrs_2.140 //
It is said to immediately destroy colic — thus spoke <s>Bhāluki</s>;

children.text: anayā mudrayā taptaṃ tailamagnau suniścitam // VRrs_2.141 //
children.translated_text: oil heated over fire with this ring, with certainty, // VRrs_2.141 //

children.text: lepitaṃ hanti vegena śūlaṃ yatra kvacidbhavet /
children.translated_text: when applied, destroys colic wherever it may be, with speed;

children.text: sadyaḥ sūtikaraṃ nāryāḥ sadyo netrarujāpaham // VRrs_2.142 //
children.translated_text: it immediately facilitates childbirth for women and immediately removes eye pain. // VRrs_2.142 //
Now, <s>capala</s> (bismuth):
<s>Capala</s> is of four kinds: tawny, white, reddish, and black;
the gold-colored and silver-colored are especially [useful for] binding mercury. // VRrs_2.143 //

children.text: śeṣau tu madhyau lākṣāvacchīghradrāvau tu niṣphalau /
children.translated_text: The remaining two are middling; lac-colored, quick-melting, and fruitless;
it melts in fire like tin — therefore it is called <s>capala</s> (the fickle one). // VRrs_2.144 //
<s>Capala</s> is considered scraping, unctuous, and a maker of body-metal (<s>dehaloha</s>);
it is an ally of the king of mercury (<s>rasarāja</s>), considered bitter, hot, and sweet. // VRrs_2.145 //
<s>Capala</s> has a crystal-like luster, is hexagonal, unctuous, and heavy;
it destroys the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors), is highly aphrodisiac, and effects the binding of mercury;
by some, <s>capala</s> is enumerated among the <s>mahārasas</s> (great minerals). // VRrs_2.146 //

body.text: jambīrakarkoṭakaśṛṅgaverairvibhāvanābhiścapalasya śuddhiḥ // VRrs_2.147 //
body.translated_text: The purification of <s>capala</s> is achieved by treating it with lemon, <s>karkoṭaka</s> (bitter gourd), and ginger. // VRrs_2.147 //

children.translated_text: Having powdered the mineral and [combining it] with grain-vinegar, <s>upaviṣas</s> (sub-poisons), and poisons,

children.text: piṇḍaṃ baddhvā tu vidhivatpātayeccapalaṃ tathā // VRrs_2.148 //
children.translated_text: having formed a ball according to procedure, one should precipitate <s>capala</s> likewise. // VRrs_2.148 //
Now, <s>rasaka</s> (zinc calamine):
<s>Rasaka</s> is said to be of two kinds: <s>durdura</s> (frog-type) and <s>kārevellaka</s> (bitter-gourd-type);

children.text: sadalo durduraḥ prokto nirdalaḥ kāravellakaḥ // VRrs_2.149 //
children.translated_text: the one with layers is called <s>durdura</s>; the one without layers is <s>kārevellaka</s>. // VRrs_2.149 //
The first is excellent for essence-extraction; the second for medicines and the like;
<s>rasaka</s> destroys all urinary diseases and eliminates <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>. // VRrs_2.150 //
It destroys eye diseases and consumption, and colors metals and mercury;

children.text: nāgārjunena saṃdiṣṭau rasaś ca rasakāvubhau // VRrs_2.151 //
children.translated_text: both mercury and <s>rasaka</s> were prescribed by <s>Nāgārjuna</s>. // VRrs_2.151 //
Both are renowned as supreme perfected mercurial preparations, supremely making body-metal;

children.text: rasaś ca rasakaś cobhau yenāgnisahanau kṛtau // VRrs_2.152 //
children.translated_text: both mercury and <s>rasaka</s>, by whom they are made fire-resistant — // VRrs_2.152 //
the <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) of body-metal becomes his servant, without doubt.
One should cook <s>rasaka</s> by stirring it with the juice of bitter gourd. // VRrs_2.153 //
Purified, freed from defects, it becomes yellow in color.
<s>Kharpara</s> (zinc oxide), thoroughly heated, immersed seven times // VRrs_2.154 //
in the juice of citron, attains purity.

children.text: nṛmūtre vāśvamūtre vā takre vā kāñjike 'thavā // VRrs_2.155 //
children.translated_text: In human urine, or horse urine, or buttermilk, or sour gruel, // VRrs_2.155 //
<s>kharpara</s>, properly heated and immersed, becomes purified.

children.text: naramūtre sthito māsaṃ rasako rañjayeddhruvam // VRrs_2.156 //
children.translated_text: Kept in human urine for a month, <s>rasaka</s> certainly colors // VRrs_2.156 //
pure copper, mercury, and silver to the luster of pure gold.
With turmeric, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>rālā</s> (resin), <s>sindhu</s> (rock salt), smoke-soot, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), // VRrs_2.157 //

children.text: sāruṣkaraiś ca pādāṃśaiḥ sāmlaiḥ saṃmardya kharparam /
children.translated_text: and with <s>āruṣkara</s> (marking-nut) in a quarter portion, all with sour [substances], grinding <s>kharpara</s>,

children.text: liptaṃ vṛntākamūṣāyāṃ śoṣayitvā nirudhya ca // VRrs_2.158 //
children.translated_text: smearing [it] in an eggplant-shaped crucible, drying, and sealing — // VRrs_2.158 //
placing <s>kharpara</s> on top of the crucible mouth, one should then blow;

children.text: kharpare prahṛte jvālā bhavennīlā sitā yadi // VRrs_2.159 //
children.translated_text: when the <s>kharpara</s> is [fully] fired, if the flame becomes blue or white, // VRrs_2.159 //

children.text: tadā saṃdaṃśato mūṣāṃ ghṛtvā kṛtvā tvadhomukhīm /
children.translated_text: then, grasping the crucible with tongs, turning it upside down,

children.text: śanairāsphālayedbhūmau yathā nālaṃ na bhajyate // VRrs_2.160 //
children.translated_text: one should gently tap it on the ground so that the tube is not broken. // VRrs_2.160 //
The fallen essence, resembling tin, should be collected and employed;

children.text: evaṃ tricaturairvāraiḥ sarvaṃ sattvaṃ viniḥsaret // VRrs_2.161 //
children.translated_text: thus, in three or four rounds, all the essence will come out. // VRrs_2.161 //
With <s>abhaya</s> (Terminalia chebula), lac, <s>bhūnāga</s> (earth-serpent mineral), <s>niśā</s> (turmeric), smoke-soot, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),

children.text: mūkamūṣāgataṃ dhmātaṃ śuddhaṃ sattvaṃ vimuñcati // VRrs_2.162 //
children.translated_text: placed in a sealed crucible and blown, it releases pure essence. // VRrs_2.162 //
With lac, jaggery, mustard, <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula), turmeric, resin, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,

children.text: samyaksaṃcūrṇya tatpakvaṃ godugdhena ghṛtena ca // VRrs_2.163 //
children.translated_text: well-powdered, cooked with cow's milk and ghee, // VRrs_2.163 //
confined in an eggplant-shaped crucible in pellet form,

children.text: dhmātvā dhmātvā samākṛṣya ḍhālayitvā śilātale // VRrs_2.164 //
children.translated_text: blowing repeatedly, extracting, and pouring on a stone surface — // VRrs_2.164 //
the beautiful essence of <s>rasaka</s>, in tin-like form, should be collected.
Alternatively, a water-filled pot should be buried in the interior of a furnace; // VRrs_2.165 //
a perforated crucible [placed] on its mouth, and on that mouth an inverted crucible should be placed;

children.text: mūṣopari śikhitrāṃś ca prakṣipya pradhameddṛḍham // VRrs_2.166 //
children.translated_text: placing fuel on top of the crucible, one should blow firmly. // VRrs_2.166 //
The essence fallen into the water of the pot should be collected and employed.

children.text: tatsattvaṃ tālakopetaṃ prakṣipya khalu kharpare // VRrs_2.167 //
children.translated_text: That essence, combined with <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment), placed in <s>kharpara</s>, // VRrs_2.167 //
when ground with an iron rod, it certainly becomes ash.

children.text: tadbhasma mṛtakāntena samena saha yojayet // VRrs_2.168 //
children.translated_text: That ash should be combined in equal parts with <s>mṛtakānta</s> (processed iron). // VRrs_2.168 //
The powder, measured at eight <s>guñjā</s> (seeds), combined with <s>triphalā</s> decoction,
placed in an iron vessel at night, with sesame oil added — // VRrs_2.169 //

body.text: niṣevitaṃ nihantyāśu madhumehamapi dhuvam // VRrs_2.170 //
body.translated_text: when regularly consumed, it quickly destroys even diabetes (<s>madhumeha</s>) certainly. // VRrs_2.170 //

children.text: pittaṃ kṣayaṃ ca pāṇḍuṃ ca śvayathuṃ gulmameva ca /
children.translated_text: Bilious disorders, consumption, anemia, edema, and abdominal tumors,

children.text: raktagulmaṃ ca nārīṇāṃ pradaraṃ somarogakam // VRrs_2.171 //
children.translated_text: blood-tumors of women, vaginal discharge, and <s>somaroga</s> (a urinary disorder), // VRrs_2.171 //
all diseases of the womb, and irregular fevers,

children.text: rajaḥśūlaṃ ca nārīṇāṃ kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ ca hidhmikām // VRrs_2.172 //
children.translated_text: menstrual pain of women, cough, asthma, and hiccups — // VRrs_2.172 //
Thus, in the composition of the <s>Rasaratnasamuccaya</s> by <s>Vāgbhaṭācārya</s>, son of the physician-chief <s>Siṃhagupta</s>,
the chapter describing the purification etc. of the eight subsidiary minerals — this is the second chapter. || 2 ||

body.text: atha tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Now the third chapter.

body.text: athoparasāḥ sādhāraṇarasāśca
body.translated_text: Now the sub-minerals and common minerals

children.translated_text: Now, <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur):
<s>Gandhāśma</s> (sulphur ore), <s>gairika</s> (ochre), <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), <s>kāṅkṣī</s> (alum), <s>tāla</s> (orpiment), <s>śilā</s> (realgar), <s>añjana</s> (antimony),
and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> — these are the eight sub-minerals (<s>uparasas</s>) used in mercurial operations. // VRrs_3.1 //

body.text:
pārvatyuvāca -
gandhakasya tu māhātmyaṃ tadguhyaṃ vada me prabho /

children.translated_text: <s>Īśvara</s> said:
"In <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (the White Island), O Goddess, in ancient times, adorned with all gems,
fulfilling all desires, delightful, on the shore of the Ocean of Milk — // VRrs_3.2 //

body.translated_text: <s>Pārvatī</s> said: "Tell me, O Lord, the greatness of <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) and its secret."

children.translated_text: with women of the <s>Vidyādharas</s> and others, and with the female companions of yogins,
with the excellent female <s>Siddhas</s>, and likewise with hosts of <s>Apsarases</s>, // VRrs_3.3 //
with charming divine women, with captivating sports,
with songs, various dances, and manifold musical instruments — // VRrs_3.4 //
while thus sporting, your menstrual blood (<s>rajas</s>) flowed forth;
that menstrual flow, O beautiful-hipped one, was exceedingly fragrant and enchanting. // VRrs_3.5 //
Due to the abundance of the menstrual flow, your garment became reddened;

children.text: tatra tyaktvā tu tadvastraṃ susnātā kṣīrasāgare // VRrs_3.6 //
children.translated_text: having discarded that garment there, having bathed well in the Ocean of Milk, // VRrs_3.6 //
surrounded by divine women, you returned again to <s>Kailāsa</s>;
that blood-stained garment was carried by the waves to the middle of the Ocean. // VRrs_3.7 //

children.text: evaṃ te śoṇitaṃ bhadre praviṣṭaṃ kṣīrasāgare /
children.translated_text: Thus your blood, O auspicious one, entered the Ocean of Milk;
and during the churning of the Milk Ocean, it arose together with the nectar. // VRrs_3.8 //
By its own fragrance, it delighted all the <s>Dānavas</s> (demons);
then the hosts of gods said: 'Let this be called <s>gandhaka</s> (the fragrant one).' // VRrs_3.9 //
'Let it serve for the binding of mercury and for its digestion;

children.text: ye guṇāḥ pārade proktāste caivātra bhavantviti // VRrs_3.10 //
children.translated_text: the qualities that are declared in mercury — let those same exist in this also.' // VRrs_3.10 //

children.text: iti devagaṇaiḥ prītaiḥ purā proktaṃ sureśvari /
children.translated_text: Thus was it spoken in ancient times by the delighted hosts of gods, O Queen of the Gods;

children.text: tenāyaṃ gandhako nāma vikhyātaḥ kṣitimaṇḍale // VRrs_3.11 //
children.translated_text: therefore this is renowned as <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) in the terrestrial realm. // VRrs_3.11 //

children.text: sa cāpi trividho devi śukacañcunibho varaḥ /
children.translated_text: And it is of three kinds, O Goddess: the best resembles a parrot's beak;
the middling is yellow-colored; the inferior is white-colored, O beloved. // VRrs_3.12 //

children.text: granthāntare caturdhā gandhako jñeyo varṇaiḥ śvetādibhiḥ khalu /
children.translated_text: In other texts, <s>gandhaka</s> should be known as fourfold, by colors beginning with white;
the white one is called <s>khaṭikā</s> (chalk-like), used in coating and killing of metals. // VRrs_3.13 //
And the <s>amalasāra</s> (pure-essence) type is the one that is yellow-colored;

children.text: śukapicchaḥ sa eva syācchreṣṭho rasarasāyane // VRrs_3.14 //
children.translated_text: that one, called <s>śukapiccha</s> (parrot-feather), is the best for mercury and rejuvenation. // VRrs_3.14 //
The red one, called <s>śukatuṇḍa</s> (parrot-beak), is excellent in the procedures of alchemy;

children.text: durlabhaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇaś ca sa jarāmṛtyunāśanaḥ // VRrs_3.15 //
children.translated_text: the black-colored one is rare, and it destroys old age and death. // VRrs_3.15 //

children.text: gandhāśmātirasāyanaḥ sumadhuraḥ pāke kaṭūṣṇo mataḥ kaṇḍūkuṣṭhavisarpadadrudalano dīptānalaḥ pācanaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Gandhāśma</s> (sulphur) is supremely rejuvenative, very sweet, considered pungent and hot in digestion; it destroys itching, leprosy, spreading skin diseases, and ringworm; it kindles the digestive fire and promotes digestion;

children.text: āmonmocanaśoṣaṇo viṣaharaḥ sūtendravīryaprado gaurīpuṣpabhavastathā kṛmiharaḥ satyātmakaḥ sūtajit // VRrs_3.16 //
children.translated_text: it releases undigested matter (<s>āma</s>), dries [excess moisture], destroys poison, bestows the potency of the lord of mercury; born from the flower of <s>Gaurī</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), it also destroys worms; it is of the nature of truth and conquers mercury. // VRrs_3.16 //

body.text: balinā sevitaḥ pūrvaṃ prabhūtabalahetave // VRrs_3.17 //
body.translated_text: It was formerly used by <s>Bali</s> for the purpose of abundant strength. // VRrs_3.17 //

children.translated_text: As he was pulling <s>Vāsuki</s> (the serpent), by the flame from its mouth,

children.text: vasā gandhakagandhāḍhyā sarvato niḥsṛtā tanoḥ // VRrs_3.18 //
children.translated_text: the fat, rich with the fragrance of sulphur, oozed out from all over its body. // VRrs_3.18 //
and having attained the nature of sulphur, <s>gandha</s> (sulphur) is said to be poisonous.
Therefore it is called <s>balivasa</s> (excrement of the demon <s>Bali</s>), and <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) is most attractive. // VRrs_3.19 //
Sulphur, moistened with milk for one <s>ghaṭī</s> (24 minutes) and washed with water,
melted in cow's ghee and filtered through cloth, attains purity. // VRrs_3.20 //
Thus purified, it gives up stones and impurities;

children.text: ghṛte viṣaṃ tuṣākāraṃ svayaṃ piṇḍatvameva ca // VRrs_3.21 //
children.translated_text: the poison in the ghee assumes a husk-like form, and it itself becomes a solid mass. // VRrs_3.21 //

children.text: iti śuddho hi gandhāśmā nāpathyairvikṛtiṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: Thus purified, <s>gandhāśma</s> (sulphur stone) does not undergo deterioration even with unwholesome foods;
otherwise, unpurified, it would kill like <s>hālāhala</s> poison consumed. // VRrs_3.22 //
Sulphur melted and cast into <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta alba) juice is purified;

children.text: tadrasaiḥ saptadhā bhinno gandhakaḥ pariśudhyati // VRrs_3.23 //
children.translated_text: split seven times by its juices, sulphur becomes thoroughly purified. // VRrs_3.23 //

children.text: sthālyāṃ dugdhaṃ vinikṣipya mukhe vastraṃ nibadhya ca /
children.translated_text: Placing milk in a pot and tying cloth over the mouth,

children.text: gandhakaṃ tatra nikṣipya cūrṇitaṃ sikatākṛti // VRrs_3.24 //
children.translated_text: one should place powdered sulphur therein, like sand granules. // VRrs_3.24 //
One should cover the sulphur with a broad, long potsherd;
one should light a fire above the potsherd with forest cow-dung cakes and stones;

children.text: dugdhe nipatito gandho galitaḥ pariśudhyati // VRrs_3.25 //
children.translated_text: the sulphur, having dropped into the milk and melted, becomes purified. // VRrs_3.25 //
Thus purified, combined with <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), ghee, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, and honey, licked in the measure of one <s>śāṇa</s> (a small weight),
it makes the pair of eyes equal to a vulture's, and produces long life free from disease. // VRrs_3.26 //
Sulphur combined with a <s>kalā</s>-portion of <s>vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents), finely powdered,

children.text: aratnimātre vastre tadviprakīrya viveṣṭya tat // VRrs_3.27 //
children.translated_text: spreading it on a cloth of one cubit's length, one should roll it up. // VRrs_3.27 //
Having wrapped it with thread, one should immerse it in oil for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours);

children.text: ghṛtvā saṃdaṃśato vartimadhyaṃ prajvālayecca tam // VRrs_3.28 //
children.translated_text: then holding it with tongs, one should light the middle of the wick. // VRrs_3.28 //
The melted sulphur drops, drop by drop, into a glass vessel;
one should place three drops of that melted sulphur on a betel leaf. // VRrs_3.29 //

children.text: vallena pramitaṃ svacchaṃ sūtendraṃ ca vimardayet /
children.translated_text: One should grind it with pure <s>sūtendra</s> (mercury), measured by the leaf,

children.text: aṅgulyātha sapatrāṃ tāṃ drutiṃ sūtaṃ ca bhakṣayet // VRrs_3.30 //
children.translated_text: and then with the finger, one should consume that melted sulphur with the leaf and mercury. // VRrs_3.30 //

children.text: karoti dīpanaṃ tīvraṃ kṣayaṃ pāṇḍuṃ ca nāśayet /
children.translated_text: It produces intense digestive fire, destroys <s>kṣaya</s> (consumption) and <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia),

children.text: kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ ca śūlārti grahaṇīmatidurdharām // VRrs_3.31 //
children.translated_text: cough, asthma, colic pain, and extremely difficult <s>grahaṇī</s> (chronic diarrhea). // VRrs_3.31 //
It quickly destroys <s>āma</s> (undigested matter) and produces lightness of body;

children.text: ghṛtākte lohapātre tu vidrutaṃ śuddhagandhakam // VRrs_3.32 //
children.translated_text: purified sulphur melted in a ghee-smeared iron vessel— // VRrs_3.32 //
cast with a ghee-smeared ladle, one should take a dose of two <s>niṣkas</s> (a weight measure);
it cures diseases beginning with consumption, and especially skin disease (<s>kuṣṭha</s>). // VRrs_3.33 //
Alkalis, sour substances, oil, <s>sauvīra</s> (a type of vinegar), pungent substances, and pulses—
during the regimen of purified sulphur, one should avoid these with proper <s>yoga</s> (discipline). // VRrs_3.34 //
Sulphur with an equal quantity of pepper, combined with six times the amount of <s>triphalā</s>,
ground with the root of <s>śamyāka</s> (Prosopis cineraria) and drunk, destroys all skin diseases. // VRrs_3.35 //
Ground with the water of that root, one should apply it daily on the body as a paste;
this is a proven formula, effective in all cases. // VRrs_3.36 //
This was properly proclaimed by the illustrious <s>Somadeva</s>;

children.text: dviniṣkapramitaṃ gandhaṃ piṣṭvā tailena saṃyutam // VRrs_3.37 //
children.translated_text: having ground sulphur measured at two <s>niṣkas</s> and combined with oil— // VRrs_3.37 //
then with <s>apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes aspera) water and pepper mixed with oil,

children.text: vilipya sakalaṃ dehaṃ tiṣṭheddharme tataḥ param // VRrs_3.38 //
children.translated_text: one should anoint the entire body and then remain in a prescribed regimen. // VRrs_3.38 //

children.text: takrabhaktaṃ ca bhuñjīta tṛtīye prahare khalu /
children.translated_text: One should eat food with buttermilk in the third <s>prahara</s> (watch of the day);

children.text: bhajedrātrau tathā vahniṃ samutthāya tathā prage // VRrs_3.39 //
children.translated_text: at night one should likewise attend to the fire, and then rise early. // VRrs_3.39 //
Having anointed oneself with buffalo dung, one should bathe with cold water;
then, having oiled the body with ghee, one should bathe with moderately warm water. // VRrs_3.40 //
By this sequential regimen, there is destroyed very quickly

children.text: durjayā bahukālīnā pāmā kaṇḍuḥ suniścitaṃ // VRrs_3.41 //
