children.translated_text: the hard-to-cure, long-standing <s>pāmā</s> (scabies) and itching, certainly. // VRrs_3.41 //
A hundred applications of sulphur have not been described here
by King <s>Somadeva</s>, out of fear of expanding the treatise. // VRrs_3.42 //
Alternatively, cloth should be smeared seven times with the milk of <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) and <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia);

children.text: gandhakaṃ navanītena piṣṭvā vastraṃ lipeddhanam // VRrs_3.43 //
children.translated_text: having ground sulphur with fresh butter, one should smear the cloth generously. // VRrs_3.43 //
That wick, lit and held with tongs, should be placed mouth-downward;

children.text: tailaṃ patedadhobhāṇḍe grāhyaṃ yogeṣu yojayet // VRrs_3.44 //
children.translated_text: the oil that falls below into a vessel should be collected and employed in formulations. // VRrs_3.44 //
Purified sulphur removes diseases such as skin disease, death, and aging;

children.text: agnikārī mahānuṣṇo vīryavṛddhiṃ karoti ca // VRrs_3.45 //
children.translated_text: it is fire-producing, very hot, and increases virility. // VRrs_3.45 //
Now, <s>gairika</s> (ochre):
One type is <s>pāṣāṇa-gairika</s> (stone ochre), the second is <s>svarṇa-gairika</s> (golden ochre);
<s>pāṣāṇa-gairika</s> is said to be hard and copper-colored. // VRrs_3.46 //
Extremely red, unctuous, and smooth is <s>svarṇa-gairika</s>;

children.text: svādu snigdhaṃ himaṃ netryaṃ kaṣāyaṃ raktapittanut // VRrs_3.47 //
children.translated_text: it is sweet, unctuous, cooling, beneficial for the eyes, astringent, and removes <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders). // VRrs_3.47 //
<s>Svarṇa-gairika</s> cures hiccup, vomiting, and poisoning, and removes blood disorders;
the other <s>pāṣāṇa-gairika</s> is inferior to it in qualities. // VRrs_3.48 //
<s>Gairika</s> treated with cow's milk attains purity;

children.text: gairikaṃ sattvarūpaṃ hi nandinā parikīrtitam // VRrs_3.49 //
children.translated_text: <s>gairika</s> is indeed a <s>sattva</s>-form (essence-bearing), as declared by <s>Nandin</s>. // VRrs_3.49 //
Some say that the <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence) falls from ochre moistened with alkalis and acids;
it attains unity with <s>sūtendra</s> (mercury), becoming superior in qualities. // VRrs_3.50 //
Now, <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol):
One type of <s>kāsīsa</s> is <s>vālukā</s> (sandy), and another is <s>puṣpa</s> (flower) type;
it has the color of alkali, acid, and <s>aguru</s> (aloe) smoke, is hot in potency, and destroys poison. // VRrs_3.51 //

body.text: bālukāpuṣpakāsīsaṃ śvitraghnaṃ keśarañjanam // VRrs_3.52 //
body.translated_text: <s>Bālukā</s> and <s>puṣpa kāsīsa</s> cure white leprosy and serve as hair dye. // VRrs_3.52 //

children.translated_text: The flower type of <s>kāsīsa</s> is most excellent—hot, astringent, sour, very beneficial for the eyes,
it destroys poison, wind, phlegm, diseases, and wounds, cures white leprosy and consumption, and serves as a hair dye. // VRrs_3.53 //
<s>Kāsīsa</s> moistened once with <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> water becomes purified;
one should extract its <s>sattva</s> (essence) just as with <s>tuvarī</s> (alum);

children.text: kāsīsaṃ śuddhimāpnoti pittaiś ca rajasā striyaḥ // VRrs_3.54 //
children.translated_text: <s>kāsīsa</s> attains purity through bile and through the menstrual discharge of a woman. // VRrs_3.54 //
<s>Kāsīsa</s> treated with <s>balinā</s> (a plant) is 'killed'; <s>kāsīsa</s> 'subdued' is 'slain';
both in equal parts, combined with <s>triphalā</s> and <s>elā</s> (cardamom), // VRrs_3.55 //
mixed with unequal parts of ghee and honey, taken in the amount of one <s>śāṇa</s> in the morning,

children.text: sevitaṃ hanti vegena śvitraṃ pāṇḍukṣayāmayam // VRrs_3.56 //
children.translated_text: when consumed, quickly cures white leprosy, anemia, and consumption, // VRrs_3.56 //
abdominal tumors, splenic disease, colic pain, and hemorrhoids especially;
when taken according to the <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) method for up to one year— // VRrs_3.57 //
it is the best for drying up <s>āma</s> (undigested matter) and kindling weak digestive fire;

children.text: palitaṃ valibhiḥ sārdhaṃ vināśayati niścitam // VRrs_3.58 //
children.translated_text: it certainly destroys grey hair along with wrinkles. // VRrs_3.58 //
Now, <s>tuvarī</s> (alum):
Born in <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>, that is considered <s>tuvarī</s>;

children.text: vastreṣu lipyate yāsau mañjiṣṭā rāgabandhinī // VRrs_3.59 //
children.translated_text: it is that which is applied to cloth, and <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder) which binds color. // VRrs_3.59 //
The second type is called <s>phaṭakī</s> or <s>phullikā</s>;

children.text: īṣatpītā guruḥ snigdhā pītikā viṣanāśanī // VRrs_3.60 //
children.translated_text: slightly yellow, heavy, unctuous, yellowish, and poison-destroying. // VRrs_3.60 //

body.text: vraṇakuṣṭhaharā sarvakuṣṭhaghnī ca viśeṣataḥ // VRrs_3.61 //
body.translated_text: It cures wounds and skin diseases, and especially destroys all types of <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease). // VRrs_3.61 //

children.text: nirbhārā śubhravarṇā ca snigdhā sāmlāparā matā /
children.translated_text: Light in weight, of bright white color, unctuous, and somewhat sour is the other type;

children.text: sā phullatuvarī proktā lepāttāmraṃ caredayaḥ // VRrs_3.62 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>phulla-tuvarī</s> (efflorescent alum), which when applied turns copper-colored. // VRrs_3.62 //

children.text: kāṅkṣī kaṣāyā kaṭukāmlakaṇthyā keśyā vraṇaghnī viṣanāśanī ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kāṅkṣī</s> (a type of alum) is astringent, pungent, sour, beneficial for the throat, good for hair, heals wounds, and destroys poison;

children.text: śvitrāpahā netrahitā tridoṣa- śāntipradā pāradajāraṇī ca // VRrs_3.63 //
children.translated_text: it removes white leprosy, is beneficial for the eyes, pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s>, and promotes the killing (fixation) of mercury. // VRrs_3.63 //
<s>Tuvarī</s> placed in sour gruel for three days attains purity;

children.text: kṣārāmlairmarditā dhmātā sattvaṃ muñcati niścitam // VRrs_3.64 //
children.translated_text: when ground with alkalis and acids and smelted, it certainly releases its <s>sattva</s> (essence). // VRrs_3.64 //
One should treat <s>Saurāṣṭrā</s> (alum) a hundred times with cow's bile, then
after smelting, extract the <s>sattva</s>; this is a most secret method of <s>krāmaṇa</s> (transmutation). // VRrs_3.65 //
Now, <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment):
<s>Haritāla</s> (orpiment) is said to be of two kinds: the leaf type and the lump type;

children.text: svarṇavarṇa guru snigdhaṃ tanupatraṃ ca bhāsuram // VRrs_3.66 //
children.translated_text: golden in color, heavy, unctuous, thin-leafed, and lustrous— // VRrs_3.66 //
that is called <s>patra-tālaka</s> (leaf orpiment), with many layers, and is a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative);
without leaves, resembling a lump, with little <s>sattva</s> (essence), and heavy;
it removes the menses of women, but is low in qualities—this is <s>piṇḍa-tālaka</s> (lump orpiment). // VRrs_3.67 //
It removes phlegm, blood disorders, poison, wind, and evil spirits, and removes the menses of women;

children.text: snigdhamuṣṇakaṭukaṃ ca dīpanaṃ kuṣṭhahāri haritālamucyate // VRrs_3.68 //
children.translated_text: unctuous, hot, pungent, and digestive-fire-kindling, destroying skin disease—such is <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment). // VRrs_3.68 //
Moistened in ash-gourd juice, or in sesame-and-alkali water,

children.text: toye vā cūrṇasaṃyukte dolāyantreṇa śudhyati // VRrs_3.69 //
children.translated_text: or in water mixed with powders, it is purified by the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus). // VRrs_3.69 //
Unpurified <s>tāla</s> (orpiment) reduces lifespan and causes phlegm, wind disorders, and urinary diseases;
it causes fever, boils, and contraction of limbs—therefore one should purify it. // VRrs_3.70 //

children.text: tālakaṃ kaṇaśaḥ kṛtvā daśāṃśena ca ṭaṅkaṇam /
children.translated_text: Having made the orpiment into small pieces with one-tenth part <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),
it should be washed with lemon juice, then washed with sour gruel. // VRrs_3.71 //

body.text: vastre caturguṇe baddhvā dolāyantre dinaṃ pacet // VRrs_3.72 //
body.translated_text: Tied in a four-layered cloth, it should be cooked for one day in the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus). // VRrs_3.72 //

children.translated_text: With sour gruel mixed with powder for one day, and in ash-gourd juice—
it should be steamed, or with <s>śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton tree) water—orpiment attains purity. // VRrs_3.73 //
In a thickened decoction of <s>brāhmī</s> root, as thick as honey,

children.text: trivāraṃ tālakaṃ bhāvyaṃ piṣṭvā mūtre 'tha māhiṣe // VRrs_3.74 //
children.translated_text: orpiment should be treated three times, having been ground with buffalo urine. // VRrs_3.74 //
It should be given <s>puṭa</s> (calcination) with ten cow-dung cakes, then after sealing, ground;

children.text: evaṃ dvādaśadhā pācyaṃ śuddhaṃ yogeṣu yojayet // VRrs_3.75 //
children.translated_text: thus cooked twelve times, purified, it should be employed in formulations. // VRrs_3.75 //
Immersed in <s>kulattha</s> (horse gram) decoction, <s>saubhāgya</s> (a mineral), buffalo ghee, and honey,

children.text: sthālyāṃ kṣiptvā vidadhyācca tvamlena cchidrayoginā // VRrs_3.76 //
children.translated_text: one should place it in a pot and cover it with a cloth having a hole. // VRrs_3.76 //
Properly sealing it, one should light fire, gradually increasing;
for the duration of one <s>prahara</s> (three hours), covering the hole with cow-dung— // VRrs_3.77 //

children.text: yāmānte chidramuddhāṭya dṛṣṭe dhūme ca pāṇḍure /
children.translated_text: at the end of one <s>yāma</s> (three hours), opening the hole, when white smoke is seen,

children.text: śītāṃ sthālīṃ samuttārya sattvamutkṛṣya cāharet // VRrs_3.78 //
children.translated_text: one should remove the cooled pot and extract the <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence). // VRrs_3.78 //
The methods for extracting <s>sattva</s> from all minerals are countless millions;

children.text: granthavistārabhītyāto likhitā na mayā khalu // VRrs_3.79 //
children.translated_text: out of fear of expanding the text, they have not been written by me. // VRrs_3.79 //
One should grind <s>palālaka</s> (a mineral) with <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) milk for one day;

children.text: kṣiptvā ṣoḍaśikātelai miśrayitvā tataḥ pacet // VRrs_3.80 //
children.translated_text: casting it into sixteen-part oils and mixing, one should then cook it. // VRrs_3.80 //
In an open place, for seven <s>yāmas</s> (21 hours) certainly,

children.text: svāṅgaśītamadhasthaṃ ca sattvaṃ śvetaṃ samāharet // VRrs_3.81 //
children.translated_text: one should collect the white <s>sattva</s> settled below, self-cooled. // VRrs_3.81 //
Combined with the fat of a young goat
and two pairs of <s>duvasa</s> (a substance), having ground orpiment with great effort, // VRrs_3.82 //
combined with the <s>drāvaṇa</s> group (fluxing agents), one should place it in a glass flask;

children.text: tridhā tāṃ ca mṛdā liptvā pariśoṣya kharātape // VRrs_3.83 //
children.translated_text: having coated the flask three times with clay and dried it in strong sunlight— // VRrs_3.83 //
then, having inserted the flask halfway into the hole of a potsherd,
one should light the fire for twelve <s>praharas</s> (36 hours). // VRrs_3.84 //
One should collect the pure, cooled <s>sattva</s> settled at the flask's neck;

children.text: palārdhapramitaṃ tālaṃ baddhvā vastre site dṛḍhe // VRrs_3.85 //
children.translated_text: having tied half a <s>pala</s> of orpiment in a firm white cloth, // VRrs_3.85 //
having smeared it carefully with <s>balinā</s> (a plant) and dried it three times,
one should cast the orpiment bundle into melted <s>triphalā</s>-copper. // VRrs_3.86 //
One should quickly cover it with ash; the white substance wrapped in copper—
one should take the soft <s>sattva</s>; this is stated in <s>Rasarasāyana</s>. // VRrs_3.87 //
Now, <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar):
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is said to be of three kinds: <s>śyāmāṅgī</s> (dark-bodied), <s>kaṇavīrakā</s>,

children.text: khaṇḍākhyā ceti tadrūpaṃ vivicya parikathyate // VRrs_3.88 //
children.translated_text: and <s>khaṇḍākhyā</s> (lump-named); their forms are described after examination. // VRrs_3.88 //

children.text: śyāmā raktā sagaurā ca bhārāḍhyā śyāmikā matā /
children.translated_text: Dark, red, somewhat fair, and heavy in weight is <s>śyāmikā</s>;

children.text: tejasvinī ca nirgaurā tāmrābhā kaṇavīrakā // VRrs_3.89 //
children.translated_text: lustrous, without fairness, copper-hued is <s>kaṇavīrakā</s>. // VRrs_3.89 //
Powdery, with very red body, heavy, is the <s>khaṇḍa</s> (lump) variety;
it is declared the best by the above-mentioned qualities, with abundant <s>sattva</s> (essence). // VRrs_3.90 //
<s>Manaḥśilā</s> is foremost among all <s>rasāyanas</s> (rejuvenatives); bitter, pungent, hot, it destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind).
It is of the nature of <s>sattva</s> (essence), and destroys poisoning from elements, digestive weakness (<s>agnimāndya</s>), itching, cough, and consumption. // VRrs_3.91 //

children.text: aśmarīṃ mūtrakṛcchraṃ ca aśuddhā kurute śilā /
children.translated_text: Impure <s>śilā</s> (realgar) causes urinary stones and dysuria,

children.text: mandāgniṃ malabandhaṃ ca śuddhā sarvarujāpahā // VRrs_3.92 //
children.translated_text: weak digestion and constipation; when purified, it removes all diseases. // VRrs_3.92 //
Soaked seven times in water infused with <s>agastyapatra</s> (Sesbania grandiflora) leaves,
or with the juice of <s>śṛṅgavera</s> (ginger), <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) becomes purified. // VRrs_3.93 //

One should cook <s>śilā</s> (realgar) in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus) for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) with juices of <s>jayantī</s>, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta prostrata), red <s>agastya</s>,
then for another <s>yāma</s> with goat's urine,
and wash with <s>āranāla</s> (sour gruel); it may then be employed in all diseases. // VRrs_3.94 //
With one-eighth part of iron slag, jaggery, <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium resin), and ghee,

children.text: koṣṭhyāṃ ruddhvā dṛḍhaṃ dhmātā sattvaṃ muñcenmanaḥśilā // VRrs_3.95 //
children.translated_text: sealed firmly in a crucible and blown with bellows, <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) releases its <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence). // VRrs_3.95 //
With <s>bhūnāga</s>, <s>dhauta</s>, <s>saubhāgya</s>, and <s>madana</s>, ground together,
one should make a crucible with the water of <s>kāravallī</s> (bitter gourd) leaves and place it therein. // VRrs_3.96 //
The realgar, ground with alkali and acid, should then be smelted;
by smelting an amount equal to two <s>kokilā</s> measures, it releases its <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence). // VRrs_3.97 //
Now, the <s>añjanas</s> (collyria) —
<s>Sauvīra añjana</s> is described first, then <s>rasāñjana</s> next,
then <s>srotoñjana</s>, and also <s>puṣpāñjana</s>. // VRrs_3.98 //

children.text: nīlāñjanaṃ ca teṣāṃ hi svarūpamiha varṇyate /
children.translated_text: And <s>nīlāñjana</s> — the characteristics of each are now described here.
<s>Sauvīra añjana</s> is smoky-grey, destroys disorders of blood and bile, and is cooling. // VRrs_3.99 //
It cures poisoning, hiccup, and eye diseases, and cleanses and heals wounds.
<s>Rasāñjana</s> is yellowish and removes poison, oral diseases, // VRrs_3.100 //
asthma, and hiccup; it improves complexion and destroys disorders of <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and blood.

children.text: srotoñjanaṃ himaṃ snigdhaṃ kaṣāyaṃ svādu lekhanam // VRrs_3.101 //
children.translated_text: <s>Srotoñjana</s> is cooling, unctuous, astringent, sweet, and scraping; // VRrs_3.101 //

body.text: netryaṃ hidhmāviṣacchardikaphapittāsraroganut // VRrs_3.102 //
body.translated_text: it is beneficial for the eyes and cures hiccup, poisoning, vomiting, and diseases of <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and blood. // VRrs_3.102 //

children.translated_text: <s>Puṣpāñjana</s> is white, unctuous, cooling, and cures all eye diseases;
it destroys severe intractable hiccup and removes poisoning, fever, and other ailments. // VRrs_3.103 //
<s>Nīlāñjana</s> is heavy, unctuous, beneficial for the eyes, and removes all three <s>doṣas</s>;
it is a rejuvenative (<s>rasāyana</s>), destroys impurities in gold, and softens metals. // VRrs_3.104 //
The <s>añjanas</s> (collyria) are purified by the juices extracted from <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta prostrata);
one should extract the <s>sattva</s> (essence) of the <s>añjanas</s> in the same manner as that of <s>manohvā</s>. // VRrs_3.105 //
Shaped like an anthill peak, with the lustre of a blue lotus when fractured,

children.text: ghṛṣṭaṃ tu gaurikacchāyaṃ srotojaṃ lakṣayedbudhaḥ // VRrs_3.106 //
children.translated_text: and having a chalk-like hue when rubbed — the wise should identify <s>srotoñjana</s> (stream-born collyrium) by these marks. // VRrs_3.106 //
Soaked repeatedly in cow-dung juice, urine, ghee, honey, and fat,

children.text: bhāvitaṃ bahuśastacca śīghraṃ badhnāti sūtakam // VRrs_3.107 //
children.translated_text: it quickly binds mercury (<s>sūtaka</s>). // VRrs_3.107 //
<s>Rasāñjana</s> attains purification by the <s>sūryāvarta</s> method and similar procedures;
the <s>sattva</s> (essence) should be extracted from <s>srotoñjana</s> as well, in the same manner as from <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli). // VRrs_3.108 //
Now, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> —
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is found on the foothills and peaks of the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas);

children.text: tatraikaṃ nālikākhyaṃ hi tadanyadreṇukaṃ matam // VRrs_3.109 //
children.translated_text: of these, one is called <s>nālikā</s>, and the other is known as <s>reṇuka</s>. // VRrs_3.109 //
The first type of <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is yellow-hued, heavy, unctuous, and superior;

children.text: śyāmapītaṃ laghu tyaktasattvaṃ neṣṭaṃ hi reṇukam // VRrs_3.110 //
children.translated_text: the <s>reṇuka</s> variety is dark-yellow, light, devoid of essence, and inferior. // VRrs_3.110 //
Some say that <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is the fresh dung of a newborn elephant,

children.text: varcaś ca śyāmapītābhaṃ recanaṃ parikathyate // VRrs_3.111 //
children.translated_text: which is dark-yellow in appearance and is said to be purgative. // VRrs_3.111 //
Others say that the stalk of <s>tejivāhā</s> plants is called <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>;
it is whitish-yellow and is an extremely powerful purgative. // VRrs_3.112 //
In alchemical use it is an excellent rejuvenative; when devoid of essence, it causes many disorders.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is bitter and pungent, hot in potency, and a strong purgative;
it cures wounds, intestinal torsion, colic pain, abdominal tumour (<s>gulma</s>), splenic disease, and rectal afflictions. // VRrs_3.113 //
<s>Sūryāvartaka</s>, <s>kadalī</s> (plantain), <s>vandhyā kośātakī</s> (barren luffa), <s>suradālī</s>,

children.text: śigruś ca vajrakando niraṅkaṇā kākamācī ca // VRrs_3.114 //
children.translated_text: <s>śigru</s> (Moringa), <s>vajrakanda</s>, <s>niraṅkaṇā</s>, and <s>kākamācī</s> (Solanum nigrum) — // VRrs_3.114 //
with the juice of any one of these, soaked repeatedly with salt, alkali, and acids,

children.text: śuddhyanti rasoparasā dhmātā muñcanti sattvāni // VRrs_3.117 //
children.translated_text: the <s>rasas</s> and <s>uparasas</s> (minerals and sub-minerals) are purified; when smelted, they release their <s>sattvas</s> (metallic essences). // VRrs_3.117 //
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> attains purification when soaked three times in water with <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger);

children.text: sattvākarṣo 'sya na prokto yasmātsattvamayaṃ hi tat // VRrs_3.116 //
children.translated_text: extraction of its essence is not prescribed, since it is itself entirely essence. // VRrs_3.116 //
One should administer it for purgation in doses of a barley-grain measure along with binding agents;
it purges instantly and destroys incomplete digestion (<s>āmapūrti</s>). // VRrs_3.117 //

body.text: bhakṣitaḥ saha tāmbūlairviricyāsūnvināśayet // VRrs_3.118 //
body.translated_text: Consumed along with betel leaves, it purges and destroys intestinal worms. // VRrs_3.118 //

children.translated_text: A decoction of <s>barburī</s> root with <s>jīra</s> (cumin) and <s>saubhāgya</s> in equal parts,

children.text: kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viṣanāśāya bhūyo bhūyaḥ pibennaraḥ // VRrs_3.119 //
children.translated_text: mixed with <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, a person should drink repeatedly for the destruction of poison. // VRrs_3.119 //

body.text: ityuparasāḥ
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>uparasas</s> (sub-minerals) are concluded.

children.translated_text: Now, the <s>sādhāraṇa rasas</s> (common mineral substances) —
<s>Kampilla</s>, <s>capala</s> (bismuth), <s>gaurīpāṣāṇa</s> (arsenic trioxide), <s>navasāra</s> (ammonium chloride),
<s>kaparda</s> (cowrie shell), <s>agnijāra</s> (fire-residue), <s>girisindūra</s> (native cinnabar), and <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) — // VRrs_3.120 //
along with <s>mṛddāraśṛṅga</s> (litharge) — these eight are known as the <s>sādhāraṇa rasas</s> (common mineral substances);
they are declared to be agents for accomplishing alchemical success (<s>rasasiddhi</s>) by the authorities headed by <s>Nāgārjuna</s>. // VRrs_3.121 //
Now, <s>kampilla</s> —
Resembling brick-powder, rich in crystalline flecks, and a strong purgative,

children.text: saurāṣṭradeśe cotpannaḥ sa hi kampillakaḥ smṛtaḥ // VRrs_3.122 //
children.translated_text: produced in the <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> region — that is known as <s>kampillaka</s>. // VRrs_3.122 //
It cures bilious disorders, wounds, flatulence, and constipation; it opposes phlegm, abdominal disease, pain, worms, and tumours (<s>gulma</s>);
it removes hemorrhoids, oedema, fever, and colic — <s>kampillaka</s> is a purgative that destroys diseases. // VRrs_3.123 //
Now, <s>gaurīpāṣāṇa</s> (arsenic trioxide) —
<s>Gaurīpāṣāṇa</s> comes in three varieties: yellow and rough with crushed powder-like appearance,

children.text: sphaṭikābhaś ca śuṅkhābho haridrābhastrayaḥ smṛtāḥ // VRrs_3.124 //
children.translated_text: crystal-like, conch-like, and turmeric-coloured — these three are recognized. // VRrs_3.124 //

children.text: pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaḥ kāravallīphale kṣipet /
children.translated_text: Each preceding variety is superior in qualities; one should place it inside a <s>kāravallī</s> (bitter gourd) fruit,
and steam it in a pot — thus the mineral becomes purified. // VRrs_3.125 //
One should extract its <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence) in the same manner as for <s>tāla</s> (orpiment); the purified, bright product should be used.
It binds mercury, is unctuous, destroys <s>doṣas</s>, and enhances the potency of mercury. // VRrs_3.126 //
Now, <s>navasāra</s> (ammonium chloride) —
It is produced when the wood of <s>karīra</s> (caper) and <s>pīlu</s> (Salvadora) is being burned;
that alkali is called <s>navasāra</s>, also known as <s>cūlikā lavaṇa</s> (chimney-salt). // VRrs_3.127 //
The white, light salt produced during the burning of bricks —
that is also called <s>navasāra</s> and <s>cūlikā lavaṇa</s>;
it enables the digestion of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>), dissolves metals, and kindles the digestive fire. // VRrs_3.128 //
It destroys abdominal tumours (<s>gulma</s>), splenic disease, and dryness of the mouth, and digests consumed meat and similar substances;

children.text: viḍākhyaṃ ca tridoṣaghnaṃ cūlikālavaṇam matam // VRrs_3.129 //
children.translated_text: <s>Cūlikā lavaṇa</s> is also known as <s>viḍa</s> (a type of salt) and is said to destroy all three <s>doṣas</s>. // VRrs_3.129 //
Now, <s>varāṭaka</s> (cowrie shells) —
Yellowish, with a knot on the back, elongated-oval — such is the <s>varāṭikā</s> (cowrie shell);
it is designated by alchemical physicians as <s>carācara</s> (animate-inanimate). // VRrs_3.130 //
One weighing one-and-a-half <s>niṣka</s> is best, one of one <s>niṣka</s> weight is medium,
and one weighing three-quarters of a <s>niṣka</s> is declared to be the lowest. // VRrs_3.131 //
It cures digestive colic and other pains, and destroys <s>grahaṇī</s> (chronic diarrhea) and consumption;

children.text: kaṭūṣṇā dīpanī vṛṣyā netryā vātakaphāpahā // VRrs_3.132 //
children.translated_text: it is pungent, hot, appetizing, aphrodisiac, beneficial for the eyes, and removes <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm). // VRrs_3.132 //

body.text: rasendrajāraṇe proktā biḍadravyeṣu śasyate // VRrs_3.133 //
body.translated_text: It is recommended for the digestion of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) and is praised among the <s>biḍa</s> substances (digestive salts). // VRrs_3.133 //

children.translated_text: Other types of cowries are heavy and aggravate <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) and <s>pitta</s> (bile);
cowries steamed in sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>) for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) attain purification. // VRrs_3.134 //
Now, <s>agnijāra</s> (fire-residue) —
The afterbirth of the fire-crocodile (<s>agninakra</s>), cast out into the ocean,

children.text: saṃśuṣko bhānutāpena so 'gnijāra iti smṛtaḥ // VRrs_3.135 //
children.translated_text: dried by the heat of the sun — that is known as <s>agnijāra</s>. // VRrs_3.135 //
<s>Agnijāra</s> destroys all three <s>doṣas</s> and cures <s>dhanurvāta</s> (tetanus) and other wind disorders;
it enhances the potency of mercury, is appetizing, and aids in digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>);
since it is purified by ocean alkali, no separate purification is required for it. // VRrs_3.136 //
Now, <s>girisindūra</s> (native cinnabar) —
In great mountains, mercury residing within rocks in small quantities,
dried and red in colour — that is designated as <s>girisindūra</s> (mountain vermillion). // VRrs_3.137 //
It pacifies all three <s>doṣas</s>, is purgative, and is foremost in binding mercury;
<s>Girisindūra</s> is said to transform the body and metals, and is beneficial for the eyes. // VRrs_3.138 //
Now, <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) — <s>Hiṅgula</s> is also known as <s>śukatuṇḍa</s> (parrot-beak); another variety is <s>haṃsapāka</s>;
the first is of lesser quality and is called <s>carmāra</s>. // VRrs_3.139 //
The one with white streaks and coral-like hue is called <s>haṃsapāka</s>.
<s>Hiṅgula</s> destroys all <s>doṣas</s>, is appetizing, and is a supreme rejuvenative; // VRrs_3.140 //
it cures all diseases, is aphrodisiac, and is highly praised for <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion of metals);
mercury extracted from it is equal in qualities to aged sulphur-treated mercury. // VRrs_3.141 //
Dried and processed seven times with fresh ginger juice, or with the water of <s>lakuca</s> (breadfruit),

children.text: śoṣito bhāvayitvā ca nirdoṣo jāyate khalu // VRrs_3.142 //
children.translated_text: it becomes free of defects. // VRrs_3.142 //

children.text: kimatracitraṃ daradaḥ subhāvitaḥ kṣīreṇa meṣyā bahuśo 'mlavargaiḥ /
children.translated_text: What wonder is there that <s>darada</s> (cinnabar), well-processed with ewe's milk and various sour substances,

children.text: evaṃ suvarṇaṃ bahugharmatāpitaṃ karoti sākṣādvarakuṅkumaprabham // VRrs_3.143 //
children.translated_text: turns gold, heated many times, into the colour of finest saffron? // VRrs_3.143 //
<s>Darada</s> (cinnabar), when distilled in a distillation apparatus into a water-reservoir,
yields an essence resembling mercury — there is no doubt about this. // VRrs_3.144 //
Now, <s>mṛddāraśṛṅgaka</s> (litharge) — having layers and yellow in colour, found in the <s>Gurjara</s> region,

children.text: arbudasya gireḥ pārśve jātaṃ mṛddāraśṛṅgakam // VRrs_3.145 //
children.translated_text: produced near <s>Arbuda</s> mountain (Mount Abu) — that is <s>mṛddāraśṛṅgaka</s> (litharge). // VRrs_3.145 //
It is the essence of lead, heavy, pacifies <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), and cures male diseases;
it is excellent for binding mercury and is the best for dyeing hair. // VRrs_3.146 //
All <s>sādhāraṇa rasas</s> (common mineral substances), soaked in the juice of <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron) and fresh ginger water

children.text: trirātraṃ bhāvitāḥ śuṣkā bhaveyurdoṣa varjitāḥ // VRrs_3.147 //
children.translated_text: for three nights and then dried, become free of defects. // VRrs_3.147 //

children.text: yāni kāni ca sattvāni tāni śudhyantyaśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever metallic essences (<s>sattvas</s>) there may be, all of them are purified completely

children.text: dhmātāni śuddhivargeṇa milanti ca parasparam // VRrs_3.148 //
children.translated_text: when smelted with the purification group of substances, and they merge with one another. // VRrs_3.148 //

body.text: iti karavālabhairavaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus [ends the section according to] <s>Karavālabhairava</s>.

children.translated_text: Now, <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli) —
<s>Rājāvarta</s> has a lustre mixed with slight red, orange, and blue hues;
the heavy and smooth one is the best; others are considered medium. // VRrs_3.149 //
It cures urinary disorders (<s>prameha</s>), consumption, hemorrhoids, anemia, and disorders of <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind);

children.text: dīpanaḥ pācano vṛṣyo rājāvarto rasāyanaḥ // VRrs_3.150 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rājāvarta</s> is appetizing, digestive, aphrodisiac, and a rejuvenative (<s>rasāyana</s>). // VRrs_3.150 //
Steamed with <s>nimbu</s> (lemon) juice, cow's urine, and alkali,
the minerals such as <s>rājāvarta</s> are purified in two or three rounds. // VRrs_3.151 //

body.text: śirīṣapuṣpārdrarasai rājāvartaṃ viśodhayet // VRrs_3.152 //
body.translated_text: One should purify <s>rājāvarta</s> with the fresh juice of <s>śirīṣa</s> (Albizia lebbeck) flowers. // VRrs_3.152 //

children.translated_text: <s>Rājāvarta</s>, powdered and combined with citron water and sulphur,
after seven rounds of calcination (<s>puṭana</s>), becomes killed (calcined). // VRrs_3.153 //
The powder of <s>rājāvarta</s>, mixed with <s>kunaṭī</s> ghee,
should be cooked in an iron vessel with buffalo milk. // VRrs_3.154 //
Bound into a ball with <s>saubhāgya</s> and the five products of the cow (<s>pañcagavya</s>), one should digest it;

children.text: dhmāpitaṃ khadirāṅgāraiḥ sattvaṃ muñcati śobhanaṃ // VRrs_3.155 //
children.translated_text: blown with charcoal of <s>khadira</s> (Acacia catechu), it releases a splendid <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence). // VRrs_3.155 //
By this sequential method, <s>gairika</s> (red ochre) also becomes purified;

children.text: kramātpītaṃ ca raktaṃ ca sattvaṃ patati śobhanam // VRrs_3.156 [418] //
children.translated_text: gradually, a yellow and then red splendid essence is obtained. // VRrs_3.156 [418] //
Thus, in the <s>Rasaratnasamuccaya</s> composed by <s>Vāgbhaṭa Ācārya</s>, son of the physician-lord <s>Siṃhagupta</s>,
the chapter describing the purification and related procedures of <s>uparasas</s> (sub-minerals) and <s>sādhāraṇa rasas</s> (common minerals), the third chapter. || VRrs_3 ||

body.text: atha caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now the fourth chapter.

body.text: atha ratnāni
body.translated_text: Now, gems (<s>ratnāni</s>)

children.translated_text: Now, the gems (<s>maṇayaḥ</s>) —
Gems too should be known as agents for binding mercury (<s>sūtabandha</s>):

children.text: vaikrāntaḥ sūryakāntaś ca hīrakaṃ mauktikaṃ maṇiḥ // VRrs_4.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s> (tourmaline), <s>sūryakānta</s> (sunstone), <s>hīraka</s> (diamond), <s>mauktika</s> (pearl), <s>maṇi</s> (gem), // VRrs_4.1 //
<s>Candrakānta</s> (moonstone), and <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli) as the seventh,
and <s>garuḍodgāra</s> (a bezoar stone) — these gems should be known. // VRrs_4.2 //
<s>Puṣparāga</s> (topaz), <s>mahānīla</s> (great sapphire), <s>padmarāga</s> (ruby), <s>pravālaka</s> (coral),

children.text: vaidūryaṃ ca tathā nīlamete ca maṇayo matāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>vaidūrya</s> (cat's eye), and <s>nīla</s> (sapphire) — these too are considered gems;
they should be carefully collected for the purpose of binding mercury. // VRrs_4.3 //
<s>Padmarāga</s> (ruby), <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire),  <s>marakata</s> (emerald) the best,
<s>Puṣparāga</s> (topaz) and <s>vajra</s> (diamond) — these are known as the five supreme gems. // VRrs_4.4 //

children.text: māṇikyamuktāphalavidrumāṇi tārkṣyaṃ ca puṣpaṃ bhiduraṃ ca nīlam /
children.translated_text: <s>Māṇikya</s> (ruby), <s>muktāphala</s> (pearl), <s>vidruma</s> (coral), <s>tārkṣya</s> (emerald), <s>puṣpa</s> (topaz), <s>bhidura</s> (diamond), and <s>nīla</s> (sapphire) —

children.text: gomedakaṃ cātha vidūrakaṃ ca krameṇa ratnāni navagrahāṇām // VRrs_4.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gomeda</s> (hessonite) and <s>Vidūraka</s> (cat's eye) — these are the nine gems of the nine planets in order. // VRrs_4.5 //
In accordance with planetary friendship: <s>Kuruvinda</s> (ruby), <s>Puṣpa</s> (topaz), <s>Pravāla</s> (coral), <s>Muktāphala</s> (pearl), <s>Tārkṣya</s> (emerald), <s>Vajra</s> (diamond),
<s>Nīla</s> (sapphire), <s>Gomeda</s> (hessonite), and <s>Vidūraka</s> (cat's eye) — worn as rings in order, for the attainment of desired results. // VRrs_4.6 //
In mercury preparations, <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation), charitable acts, wearing, and worship of deities,
well-preserved gems of good quality are prescribed for success. // VRrs_4.7 //
<s>Māṇikya</s> (ruby), also called <s>Padmarāga</s>, the second variety is called <s>Nīlagandhi</s>;
having the hue of lotus petals, transparent, unctuous, large, and brilliant, // VRrs_4.8 //

body.text: vṛttāyataṃ samaṃ gātraṃ māṇikyaṃ śreṣṭhamucyate // VRrs_4.9 //
body.translated_text: round or elongated, symmetrical in body — such <s>Māṇikya</s> is said to be the best. // VRrs_4.9 //

children.translated_text: The blue variety, born of <s>Gaṅgā</s> water, has a blue core with a reddish hue;
like the previously described <s>Māṇikya</s>, the best ruby is that called <s>Nīlagandhi</s>. // VRrs_4.10 //
Having holes, roughness, dullness, dryness, and lack of clarity,

children.text: cipiṭaṃ laghu vakraṃ ca māṇikyaṃ duṣṭamaṣṭadhā // VRrs_4.11 //
children.translated_text: flat, light, and crooked — such <s>Māṇikya</s> is defective in eight ways. // VRrs_4.11 //
<s>Māṇikya</s> (ruby) is a digestive stimulant, aphrodisiac, and destroys <s>Kapha</s>, <s>Vāta</s>, consumption, and pain;
it removes evil spirits (<s>bhūta</s>), vampires (<s>vetāla</s>), and sins, and destroys diseases born of past actions (<s>karmajavyādhi</s>). // VRrs_4.12 //
Now, <s>Mauktika</s> (pearl) —

children.text: hlādi śvetaṃ laghu snigdhaṃ raśmivannirmalaṃ mahat /
children.translated_text: Pleasing, white, light, unctuous, radiant like a ray of light, pure, large,

children.text: khyātaṃ toyaprabhaṃ vṛttaṃ mauktikaṃ navadhā śubham // VRrs_4.13 //
children.translated_text: renowned, with the luster of water, and round — a pearl is auspicious in nine ways. // VRrs_4.13 //

children.text: muktāphalaṃ laghu himaṃ madhuraṃ ca kānti- dṛṣṭyagnipuṣṭikaraṇaṃ viṣahāri bhedi /
children.translated_text: <s>Muktāphala</s> (pearl) is light, cooling, sweet, and beauty-giving; it strengthens vision, digestion, and nourishment; it is an antidote to poison and a laxative;

children.text: vīryapradaṃ jalanidherjanitā ca śuktir dīptā ca paktirujamāśu haredavaśyam // VRrs_4.14 //
children.translated_text: it bestows virility; born from an oyster of the ocean, with radiant digestive power, it quickly removes disease, without fail. // VRrs_4.14 //
Rough-bodied, dry, dark-hued, copper-colored, salt-like,

children.text: ardhaśubhraṃ ca vikaṭaṃ granthilaṃ mauktikaṃ tyajet // VRrs_4.15 //
children.translated_text: half-white, misshapen, and knotty — such pearls should be rejected. // VRrs_4.15 //
Destroying <s>Kapha</s>, <s>Pitta</s>, and consumption, removing cough, asthma, and weak digestion,

children.text: puṣṭidaṃ vṛṣyamāyuṣyaṃ dāhaghnaṃ mauktikaṃ matam // VRrs_4.16 //
children.translated_text: nourishing, aphrodisiac, promoting longevity, and cooling — pearl is so regarded. // VRrs_4.16 //
Now, <s>Pravāla</s> (coral) —
Having the color of a ripe <s>Bimbī</s> (Coccinia) fruit, round or elongated, straight,

children.text: snigdhamavraṇakaṃ sthūlaṃ pravālaṃ saptadā śubham // VRrs_4.17 //
children.translated_text: unctuous, without blemishes, and thick — coral is auspicious in seven ways. // VRrs_4.17 //
Pale, grayish, thin, blemished, with ridges,

children.text: nirbhāraṃ śulbavarṇaṃ ca pravālaṃ neṣyate 'ṣṭadhā // VRrs_4.18 //
children.translated_text: without weight, and copper-colored — coral is undesirable in eight ways. // VRrs_4.18 //
Destroying consumption, <s>Pitta</s>, blood disorders, and cough; a digestive stimulant, digestive, and light;
pacifying poison, evil spirits, and such — <s>Vidruma</s> (coral) removes eye diseases. // VRrs_4.19 //
Now, <s>Tārkṣya</s> (emerald) —
Golden in color, heavy, unctuous, with a mass of sparkling rays, auspicious,

children.text: masṛṇaṃ bhāsuraṃ tārkṣyaṃ gātraṃ saptaguṇaṃ matam // VRrs_4.20 //
children.translated_text: smooth, lustrous — <s>Tārkṣya</s> is endowed with seven good qualities. // VRrs_4.20 //

children.text: kapilaṃ karkaśaṃ nīlaṃ pāṇḍu kṛṣṇaṃ ca lāghavam /
children.translated_text: Tawny, rough, blue, pale, black, and light,

children.text: cipiṭaṃ vikaṭaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ tārkṣyaṃ na śasyate // VRrs_4.21 //
children.translated_text: flat, misshapen, black, and dry — such <s>Tārkṣya</s> is not recommended. // VRrs_4.21 //
Destroying fever, vomiting, poison, asthma, <s>saṃnipāta</s> (derangement of all three humors), and weak digestion;
removing hemorrhoids, anemia, and swelling — <s>Tārkṣya</s> increases vital energy (<s>ojas</s>). // VRrs_4.22 //
Now, <s>Puṣparāga</s> (topaz) —

children.text: puṣparāgaṃ guru svacchaṃ snigdhaṃ sthūlaṃ samaṃ mṛdu /
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣparāga</s> — heavy, transparent, unctuous, thick, symmetrical, soft,
having the color of <s>Karṇikāra</s> (Pterospermum) blossoms, smooth — is auspicious in eight ways. // VRrs_4.23 //

children.text: niṣprabhaṃ karkaśaṃ rūkṣaṃ pītaṃ śyāmaṃ natonnatam /
children.translated_text: Lusterless, rough, dry, yellowish, dark, uneven,

children.text: kapiśaṃ kapilaṃ pāṇḍu puṣparāgaṃ parityajet // VRrs_4.24 //
children.translated_text: tawny, brownish, and pale — such <s>Puṣparāga</s> should be rejected. // VRrs_4.24 //
<s>Puṣparāga</s> destroys poison, vomiting, <s>Kapha</s>, <s>Vāta</s>, and weak digestion;
it pacifies burning sensations, skin diseases, and blood disorders; it is a digestive stimulant, digestive, and light. // VRrs_4.25 //
Now, <s>Vajra</s> (diamond) —

children.text: vajraṃ ca trividhaṃ proktaṃ naro nārī napuṃsakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Vajra</s> is declared to be of three kinds: male, female, and neuter;
each preceding type is superior in <s>rasa</s> (taste), <s>vīrya</s> (potency), and <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect). // VRrs_4.26 //
Octahedral or eight-faceted, hexagonal, and extremely brilliant,
resembling water, rainbow, and rain — such is called the male diamond. // VRrs_4.27 //
The same with a flat shape is the female diamond; it is round and elongated;
round, with blunt-edged corners, and somewhat heavy — that is the neuter diamond. // VRrs_4.28 //
Female, male, and neuter diamonds should be used for female, male, and neuter (patients) respectively;

children.text: vyatyāsānnaiva phaladaṃ puṃvajreṇa vinā kvacit // VRrs_4.29 //
children.translated_text: if used in reverse, they yield no results; without the male diamond, never (will they work). // VRrs_4.29 //
By color distinctions of white and so forth, each type is again fourfold:
<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s> — each bestowing results appropriate to its class. // VRrs_4.30 //
The higher the color-class, the more it bestows the results of lower classes as well;
this principle was stated by <s>Bhairava</s> (Śiva) regarding all substances. // VRrs_4.31 //

children.text: āyuḥpradaṃ jhaṭiti sadguṇadaṃ ca vṛṣyaṃ doṣatrayapraśamanam sakalāmayaghnam /
children.translated_text: Bestowing longevity instantly, granting good qualities, aphrodisiac, pacifying the three <s>doṣas</s>, destroying all diseases,
like mercury-binding in producing excellent qualities, a digestive stimulant, conquering death — <s>Vajra</s> (diamond) is verily like ambrosia. // VRrs_4.32 //

children.text: gauratrāsaś ca binduś ca rekhā ca jalagarbhatā /
children.translated_text: Paleness (<s>gaura</s>), cracks (<s>trāsa</s>), specks (<s>bindu</s>), lines (<s>rekhā</s>), and internal cloudiness (<s>jalagarbhatā</s>) —

children.text: sarvaratneṣvamī pañca doṣāḥ sādhāraṇā matāḥ // VRrs_4.33 //
children.translated_text: these five defects are considered common to all gems. // VRrs_4.33 //

children.text: kṣetratoyabhavā doṣā ratneṣu na laganti te /
children.translated_text: Defects arising from the mine or water do not adhere to gems (if properly purified).
Steamed in horse gram (<s>Kulattha</s>) decoction, or boiled in <s>Kodrava</s> (millet) decoction, // VRrs_4.34 //
steamed for the duration of one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) — diamond is certainly purified.
Diamond, anointed four times with bedbug blood, // VRrs_4.35 //
wrapped with rolls made from the flesh of the musk rat (<s>sugandhimūṣikā</s>),
should be calcined with <s>Vārāha</s> (boar) <s>puṭas</s> thirty times; then further, // VRrs_4.36 //
smelting and smelting a hundred times, one should cast it into horse gram decoction;
others have stated this procedure should be repeated a hundred times. // VRrs_4.37 //
With a paste of <s>Lakuca</s> (breadfruit) extract mixed with horse gram decoction

children.text: śilayā liptamūṣāyāṃ vajraṃ kṣiptvā nirudhya ca // VRrs_4.38 //
children.translated_text: and stone (mortar), smeared inside a crucible — placing the diamond therein and sealing it, // VRrs_4.38 //
one should calcine it properly eight times with dry forest lotuses (<s>Vanotpala</s>);
then, smelting it a hundred times and placing it in pure mercury,

children.text: niścitaṃ mriyate vajraṃ bhasma vāritaraṃ bhavet // VRrs_4.39 //
children.translated_text: the diamond is certainly killed (calcined) — the ash becomes water-clear. // VRrs_4.39 //
<s>Satyavāk Somasenānī</s> has described this calcination of diamond,
supported by observed evidence — so has spoken the mercury-enthusiast (<s>Rasakautukī</s>). // VRrs_4.40 //

body.text: viliptaṃ matkuṇasyāsre saptavāraṃ viśoṣitam // VRrs_4.41 //
body.translated_text: Smeared with bedbug blood and dried seven times, // VRrs_4.41 //

children.translated_text: placed in an iron vessel filled with <s>Kāsamarda</s> (Cassia occidentalis) juice,
and smelted seven times — it becomes diamond-ash indeed. // VRrs_4.42 //
This procedure was proclaimed by the sage <s>Brahmajyoti</s>;
rubbed on the tuber of <s>Nīlajyotirlatā</s> (a creeper) and dried in the sun, // VRrs_4.43 //
diamond turns to ash, as <s>karma</s> is (burned) by the fire of knowledge.
With the juice extracted from the fruit of <s>Madana</s> (Randia dumetorum), with <s>Kṣoṇināga</s> (earthworms), // VRrs_4.44 //
making a paste and smearing it, one should calcine it twenty times;
the diamond powder becomes excellent and should be employed in mercury preparations and such. // VRrs_4.45 //
That diamond, having been powdered and combined with a little borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>),
is certainly assimilated by the <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence) of <s>kharabhūnāga</s> (tin/lead) with twenty (parts);
smelted with an equal amount of gold, it should be employed in mercury preparations. // VRrs_4.46 //
Ground with three times its weight of mercury and made into pills,
when placed in the mouth, it quickly firms loose teeth with ghee. // VRrs_4.47 //

children.text: triṃśadbhāgamitaṃ hi vajrabhasitaṃ svarṇaṃ kalābhāgikaṃ tāraṃ cāṣṭaguṇaṃ sitāmṛtavaraṃ rudrāṃśakaṃ cābhrakam /
children.translated_text: Thirty parts of diamond-ash, gold in one-sixteenth part, silver in eight times (that), the best white <s>amṛta</s> (mica-sattva), <s>Rudra</s>'s portion (eleven parts) of mica,

children.text: pādāṃṣaṃ khalu tāpyakaṃ vasuguṇaṃ vaikrāntakaṃ ṣāḍguṇaṃ bhogo 'pyuktarasai raso 'yamuditaḥ ṣāḍguṇyasaṃsiddhaye // VRrs_4.48 //
children.translated_text: one-quarter part of <s>Tāpya</s> (pyrite), eight parts of <s>Vaikrānta</s>, six parts — the dosage is also stated; this mercury (preparation) is proclaimed for the attainment of sixfold perfection. // VRrs_4.48 //
Now, <s>Nīla</s> (sapphire) —
<s>Jalanīla</s> (water-sapphire) and <s>Indranīla</s> (Indra's sapphire), also called <s>Śakranīla</s> — of the two, the latter is superior;
that which has a blue luster tinged with whiteness and is light — that is <s>Jalanīla</s>. // VRrs_4.49 //

body.text: kāṛṣṇyagarbhitanīlābhaṃ sabhāraṃ śakranīlakam // VRrs_4.50 //
body.translated_text: That which has a blue luster tinged with blackness and is heavy — that is <s>Śakranīla</s>. // VRrs_4.50 //

children.translated_text: Of uniform color, heavy, unctuous, transparent, with a compact body,

children.text: mṛdu madhye lasajjyotiḥ saptadhā nīlamuttamam // VRrs_4.51 //
children.translated_text: soft, with a light shining in its center — a sapphire is excellent in seven ways. // VRrs_4.51 //

children.text: komalaṃ vihitaṃ rūksaṃ nirbhāraṃ raktagandhi ca /
children.translated_text: Tender, cracked, rough, without weight, reddish-tinted,

children.text: cipiṭābhaṃ sasūkṣmaṃ ca jalanīlaṃ ca saptadhā // VRrs_4.52 //
children.translated_text: flat-looking, and very small — <s>Jalanīla</s> (water-sapphire) is defective in seven ways. // VRrs_4.52 //
Destroying asthma and cough, aphrodisiac, destroying the three <s>doṣas</s>, a great appetizer,
removing intermittent fever, hemorrhoids, and sins — thus is <s>Nīla</s> (sapphire) described. // VRrs_4.53 //
Now, <s>Gomeda</s> (hessonite) —
<s>Gomeda</s> is called <s>Gomeda</s> gem because of its resemblance to cow's fat (<s>go-meda</s>).
Having the hue of clear cow's urine, transparent, unctuous, symmetrical, heavy,

children.text: nirdalaṃ masṛṇaṃ dīptaṃ gomedaṃ śubhamaṣṭadhā // VRrs_4.54 //
children.translated_text: without layers, smooth, and lustrous — <s>Gomeda</s> is auspicious in eight ways. // VRrs_4.54 //
Lacking luster, light, rough-bodied, flat, layered,

children.text: niṣprabhaṃ pītakācābhaṃ gomedaṃ na śubhāvaham // VRrs_4.55 //
children.translated_text: without radiance, and resembling yellow glass — such <s>Gomeda</s> is not auspicious. // VRrs_4.55 //
<s>Gomeda</s> destroys <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Pitta</s>, causes the destruction of consumption and anemia,

children.text: dīpanaṃ pācanaṃ rucyaṃ tvacyaṃ buddhiprabodhanam // VRrs_4.56 //
children.translated_text: is a digestive stimulant, digestive, appetizing, beneficial for the skin, and an awakener of the intellect. // VRrs_4.56 //
Now, <s>Vaidūrya</s> (cat's eye) —

children.text: vaidūryaṃ śyāmaśubhrābhaṃ samaṃ svacchaṃ guru sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidūrya</s>, having a dark and bright luster, symmetrical, transparent, heavy, and clear,
with a shimmering band of light within — is declared auspicious. // VRrs_4.57 //
Dark, water-colored, flat, light, rough,

children.text: raktagarbhottarīyaṃ ca vaidūryaṃ naiva śasyate // VRrs_4.58 //
children.translated_text: and with a reddish internal band — such <s>Vaidūrya</s> is not recommended. // VRrs_4.58 //
<s>Vaidūrya</s> destroys blood and <s>Pitta</s> disorders, increases wisdom, longevity, and strength,
destroys <s>Pitta</s>-predominant diseases, is a digestive stimulant, and loosens impurities. // VRrs_4.59 //
Now, the purification of gems —
<s>Māṇikya</s> (ruby) is purified with sour substances; <s>Mauktika</s> (pearl) with <s>Jayantī</s> (a plant);
<s>Vidruma</s> (coral) with alkaline substances; <s>Tārkṣya</s> (emerald) with cow's milk. // VRrs_4.60 //
<s>Puṣparāga</s> (topaz) with fermented preparations; diamond with horse gram decoction in a sealed vessel;
<s>Vajra</s> with <s>Taṇḍulīya</s> (Amaranthus) water; <s>Nīla</s> (sapphire) with indigo (<s>Nīlī</s>) juice. // VRrs_4.61 //

body.text: rocanābhiś ca gomedaṃ vaidūryaṃ triphalājalaiḥ // VRrs_4.62 //
body.translated_text: <s>Gomeda</s> (hessonite) with <s>Rocanā</s> (yellow orpiment/gorocana); <s>Vaidūrya</s> (cat's eye) with <s>Triphalā</s> water. // VRrs_4.62 //

children.translated_text: Now, the procedure for making gem-ash —
Ground with <s>Lakuca</s> (breadfruit) extract, realgar (<s>śilā</s>), sulfur (<s>gandhaka</s>), and orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>),
gems other than diamond are killed (calcined) with eight <s>puṭa</s>s. // VRrs_4.63 //
<s>Rāmaṭha</s> (a type of salt), the five salts, the three alkalis,
meat extract, sour <s>Vetasa</s> (cane vinegar), and <s>Cūlikā</s> salt; // VRrs_4.64 //

children.text: sthūlaṃ kumbhīphalaṃ pakvaṃ tathā jvālāmukhī śubhā /
children.translated_text: a large ripe <s>Kumbhī</s> (Gmelina) fruit, and the excellent <s>Jvālāmukhī</s> (a plant),

children.text: dravantī ca rudantī ca payasyā citramūlakam // VRrs_4.65 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dravantī</s> (Jatropha) and <s>Rudantī</s> (a plant), <s>Payasyā</s> (Holostemma), and <s>Citramūlaka</s> (Plumbago); // VRrs_4.65 //
the latex of <s>Snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) and of <s>Arka</s> (Calotropis) — all ground together carefully;
making a ball, one should place (the gem) in its center thereafter. // VRrs_4.66 //
The nine gems of good quality, well-born, and auspicious,

children.text: bhūrje taṃ golakaṃ kṛtvā sūtreṇāveṣṭya yatnataḥ // VRrs_4.67 //
children.translated_text: making that ball, wrapping it in birch bark (<s>bhūrja</s>) and binding with thread carefully, // VRrs_4.67 //
wrapping again with cloth and placing it in a <s>Dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus),
inside a pot filled with a fermented mixture of all sour substances, // VRrs_4.68 //
one should steam it for three days and nights with intense fire;
removing from there and washing, one should extract the gem-derived liquid (<s>druti</s>). // VRrs_4.69 //
The liquid, equal in luster to the gem, light, auspicious, and effective for body and metals.

children.text: muktācūrṇaṃ tu saptāhaṃ vetasāmlena marditam // VRrs_4.70 //
children.translated_text: Pearl powder ground for seven days with sour <s>Vetasa</s> (cane vinegar), // VRrs_4.70 //
should be placed inside a lemon (<s>Jambīra</s>) and buried in a heap of grain;

children.text: saptāhāduddhṛtaṃ caiva puṭe dhṛtvā drutirbhavet // VRrs_4.71 //
children.translated_text: removed after seven days and placed in a <s>puṭa</s> — it becomes a liquid (<s>druti</s>). // VRrs_4.71 //
Placing the diamond inside a <s>Vajravallī</s> (a creeper) and sealing it,
it should be steamed in a sour vessel — after seven days it liquefies. // VRrs_4.72 //
Now, <s>Vaikrānta</s> —
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, white in color, macerated with sour <s>Vetasa</s> (cane vinegar),
liquefies after seven days in intense sun-heat — there is no doubt about this. // VRrs_4.73 //
The juice of <s>Ketakī</s> (Pandanus) should be taken, along with <s>Saindhava</s> (rock salt) and <s>Svarṇapuṣpikā</s> (a plant),
combined with <s>Indragopaka</s> (cochineal insects) — all should be placed in a vessel. // VRrs_4.74 //
Steaming for seven days therein, <s>Vaikrānta</s> liquefies.
In the group of eight metals, by the addition of <s>vajra</s> (diamond), by <s>svedana</s> (sudation), <s>druti</s> (liquefaction) is achieved.
There is no doubt about this, due to the power of this formulation.

children.text: kurute yogarājo 'yaṃ ratnānāṃ drāvaṇaṃ param // VRrs_4.76 //
children.translated_text: This king of formulations produces the supreme <s>drāvaṇa</s> (liquefaction) of gemstones.
The liquefied substances should be stored separately in safflower oil,

children.text: tiṣṭhanti cirakālaṃ tu prāpte kārye niyojayet // VRrs_4.77 //
children.translated_text: they remain stable for a long time; one should employ them when the occasion arises.

Wearing gemstones removes the afflictions of eclipses by <s>Sūrya</s> and other planets, bestows long life and freedom from disease, grants the rise of good fortune, luck, power of attraction, resources, enthusiasm, and produces steadfastness;

children.text: duśchāyācaladhūlisaṃgatibhavālakṣmīharaṃ sarvadā ratnānāṃ paridhāraṇaṃ nigaditaṃ bhūtādinirnāśanam // VRrs_4.78 [496] //
children.translated_text: it always removes misfortune arising from contact with bad complexion, mountains, and dust, and is declared to destroy <s>bhūta</s>s (evil spirits) and the like.
Thus, in the composition of <s>Rasaratnasamuccaya</s> by <s>Vāgbhaṭācārya</s>, son of the eminent physician <s>Siṃhagupta</s>,
the chapter named 'Examination of the purification and other processes of gemstones' is the fourth chapter.

body.text: atha pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now begins the fifth chapter.

body.text: atha lohāni
body.translated_text: Now, metals

children.translated_text: Now, the qualities of gold:

children.text: śuddhaṃ lohaṃ kanakarajataṃ bhānulohāśmasāraṃ pūtīlohaṃ dvitayamuditaṃ nāgavaṅgābhidhānam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śuddha loha</s> (pure metals) are said to be two: gold and silver; <s>bhānuloha</s> (sun-metal, i.e. copper) and <s>aśmasāra</s> (iron); <s>pūtīloha</s> (malodorous metals) are said to be two: <s>nāga</s> (lead) and <s>vaṅga</s> (tin);

children.text: miśraṃ lohaṃ tritayamuditaṃ pittalaṃ kāṃsyavartaṃ dhāturlohe luha iti mataḥ so 'pi karṣārthavācī // VRrs_5.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>miśra loha</s> (mixed metals) are said to be three: <s>pittala</s> (brass), <s>kāṃsya</s> (bell-metal), and <s>varta</s> (iron alloy); in the terminology of metal ores, <s>luha</s> is the accepted term, and it also denotes the weight of one <s>karṣa</s>.
<s>Prākṛta</s> (primordial), <s>sahaja</s> (innate), <s>vahnisaṃbhūta</s> (fire-born), <s>svanisaṃbhava</s> (self-originated),
and <s>rasendravedhasaṃjāta</s> (produced by mercury transmutation) — gold is thus remembered to be of five kinds.

Gold bestows longevity, wealth, radiance, intellect, and memory; it destroys all diseases, is meritorious, pacifies possession by <s>bhūta</s>s (spirits), grants the pleasure of the fullness of desire, and manifests happiness, nourishment, and brilliance.

children.text: gāṅgeyaṃ cātha rūpyaṃ gadaharamajarākāri mehāpahāri kṣīṇānāṃ puṣṭikāri sphuṭamatikaraṇaṃ vīryavṛddhiprakāri // VRrs_5.3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gāṅgeya</s> (gold refined like the Ganges) and also silver: they remove disease, counteract aging, cure <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders), nourish the emaciated, sharpen the intellect, and promote the increase of virility.
The cosmic egg (<s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>) was enveloped by that which arose from <s>rajoguṇa</s> (the quality of passion),
that is called <s>prākṛta</s> (primordial) gold, which is rare even for the gods.
<s>Brahmā</s> was born enveloped in a golden membrane (<s>jarāyu</s>),

children.text: tanmerurūpatāṃ yātaṃ suvarṇaṃ sahajaṃ hi tat // VRrs_5.5 //
children.translated_text: and that gold which assumed the form of Mount <s>Meru</s> is indeed <s>sahaja</s> (innate) gold.
The radiance emitted by <s>Agni</s> (fire), golden and exceedingly intense,
all that which has been designated became <s>vahnisaṃbhava</s> (fire-born) gold.
These three types of divine gold possess sixteen grades of color,
and merely by wearing them, they render the body free from old age and immortal.

children.text: tatra tatra girīṇāṃ hi jātaṃ khaniṣu yadbhavet /
children.translated_text: That gold which is born here and there in the mines of mountains,
possessing fourteen grades of color — when consumed, it removes all diseases.
That which is produced by transmutation with <s>rasendra</s> (mercury) is called <s>vedhaja</s> (transmutation-born);

children.text: rasāyanaṃ mahāśreṣṭhaṃ pavitraṃ vedhajaṃ hi tat // VRrs_5.9 //
children.translated_text: that <s>vedhaja</s> gold is a most excellent <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative) and is sacred.
Gold is unctuous, intellect-promoting, removes poisons and diseases, is nourishing, the foremost aphrodisiac,
excels in pacifying <s>yakṣa</s>-possession and madness, and destroys diseases of the body;
it promotes intellect, wisdom, memory, and happiness, destroys all <s>doṣa</s>s (humoral imbalances) and ailments,

children.text: rucyaṃ dīpi praśāmitarujaṃ khādupākaṃ suvarṇam // VRrs_5.10 //
children.translated_text: enhances taste, kindles digestive fire, alleviates pain, and when consumed produces beneficial effects.

children.text: saukhyaṃ vīryaṃ balaṃ hanti rogavargaṃ karoti ca /
children.translated_text: Impure and uncalcined gold destroys happiness, virility, and strength, and produces a host of diseases;

children.text: aśuddhaṃ na sṛtam svarṇaṃ tasmācchuddaṃ samācaret // VRrs_5.11 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should employ it only after proper purification.
A gold leaf of one <s>karṣa</s> measure, enclosed in an earthen saucer, combined with sharp alkali,

children.text: aṅgārasaṃ sthaṃ praharārdhamānaṃ dhmānena tatsyānnanu varṇapurṇam // VRrs_5.12 //
children.translated_text: placed on burning coals for the duration of half a <s>prahara</s> (approximately one and a half hours), by bellows-blowing it becomes fully restored in color.
The calcination of all metals is best accomplished with mercury-<s>bhasma</s> (calcined ash of mercury);
with plant roots it is declared middling; with <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) and the like, it is the lowest.
Calcination of a metal with its enemy metal produces harmful qualities.
Having made gold leaves perforated like thorns, one should coat them
with <s>luṅgā</s>-<s>bhasma</s> (calcined ash of luṅgā) and <s>sūta</s> (mercury); it dies (is calcined) in ten <s>puṭa</s>s (heating cycles).
Into molten gold, one should cast the dead (calcined) mercury in the measure equal to the metal,
having powdered it with <s>luṅgā</s>-water and combined it with <s>darada</s> (cinnabar).

body.text: jāyate kuṅkumacchāyaṃ svarṇaṃ dvādaśabhiḥ puṭaiḥ // VRrs_5.16 //
body.translated_text: The gold attains a saffron-like hue in twelve <s>puṭa</s>s (heating cycles).

children.text: hemnaḥ pādaṃ mṛtaṃ sūtaṃ piṣṭamamlena kenacit /
children.translated_text: Dead (calcined) <s>sūta</s> (mercury) equal to one-quarter of the gold, ground with some acid,

children.text: patre liptvā puṭaiḥ pacyādaṣṭabhirmriyate dhruvam // VRrs_5.17 //
children.translated_text: smeared on the leaf and heated by <s>puṭa</s>s — in eight cycles it is certainly killed (calcined).
With the addition of frog-bone, fat, <s>ṭaṅka</s> (borax), horse-saliva, and <s>indragopaka</s> (cochineal insects),

children.text: prativāpena kanakaṃ suciraṃ tiṣṭhati drutam // VRrs_5.18 //
children.translated_text: gold remains molten for a very long time.
The powder of <s>indragopaka</s> insects, treated with the juice of <s>devadālī</s> fruit,

children.text: bhāvitaṃ sadṛśaṃ hema karoti jalavaddrutam // VRrs_5.19 //
children.translated_text: renders gold equal to itself — liquefied like water.
This <s>bhasma</s> (calcined ash) born from gold, taken with pungent ghee in a dose of two <s>guñjā</s>s,

children.text: līḍhaṃ hanti nṛṇāṃ kṣayāgnisadanaṃ śvāsaṃ ca kāsārucim /
children.translated_text: when licked, destroys in men <s>kṣaya</s> (consumption), weakness of digestive fire, <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), <s>kāsa</s> (cough), and <s>aruci</s> (anorexia);
it increases <s>ojas</s> (vital essence) and <s>dhātu</s>s (bodily tissues), produces strength, destroys <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia) and related diseases,
is wholesome, removes all poisons, counteracts toxic preparations, and expels chronic <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption) and other afflictions.
Interpolated verse:

children.text: balaṃ ca vīryaṃ harate narāṇāṃ rogavrajaṃ kopayatīva kāye /
children.translated_text: Improperly processed gold destroys the strength and virility of men and excites a host of diseases in the body;

children.text: asaukhyakāraṃ ca sadaiva hemāpakvaṃ sadoṣaṃ maraṇaṃ karoti // VRrs_5.21 //
children.translated_text: it always causes unhappiness, and being improperly calcined and full of faults, it brings about death.
Now, silver:
<s>Sahaja</s> (innate), <s>khanisaṃjāta</s> (mine-born), and <s>kṛtrima</s> (artificial) — silver is considered to be of three kinds;
each preceding type is superior to the next in its qualities.
That silver which is born from <s>Kailāsa</s> and other mountains is <s>sahaja</s> (innate) silver;

children.text: tatspṛṣṭhaṃ hi sakṛdvyādhināśanaṃ dehināṃ bhavet // VRrs_5.23 //
children.translated_text: merely by touching it once, it becomes a destroyer of diseases for living beings.
Having carefully examined all the <s>rasaśāstra</s>s (treatises on mercury/alchemy) in proper sequence,
this is now being made manifest for the benefit of practitioners.

children.text: na krameṇa vinā śāstraṃ na śāstreṇa vinā kramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Without proper sequence there is no scripture, and without scripture there is no proper sequence;

children.text: śāstraṃ kramayutaṃ jñātvā yaḥ karoti sa siddhibhāk // VRrs_6.2 //
children.translated_text: one who knows the scripture combined with proper sequence and acts accordingly attains <s>siddhi</s> (success).
The <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) should be possessed of knowledge, skilled, proficient in <s>rasaśāstra</s> (the science of mercury),
accomplished in <s>mantra</s>s, greatly courageous, steadfast, and devoted to <s>Śiva</s>.
He should be devoted to the <s>Devī</s> (Goddess), always resolute, dedicated to the worship of deities,
expert in all the <s>āmnāya</s>s (sacred traditions), and skilled in <s>rasakarma</s> (alchemical operations);
one endowed with such qualifications becomes a <s>guru</s> (master) of <s>rasavidyā</s> (the science of mercury).
The disciples should be devoted to the <s>guru</s>, of virtuous conduct, truthful, firm in their vows,
free from laziness, knowledgeable of their own <s>dharma</s> (duty), and always obedient to commands.
They should be free from hypocrisy and envy, initiated in <s>kulācāra</s> (clan practices),
extremely dedicated practitioners, peaceful, devoted to <s>mantra</s> worship;

children.text: ityevaṃ lakṣaṇairyuktāḥ śiṣyāḥ syuḥ sūtasiddhaye // VRrs_6.6 //
children.translated_text: disciples endowed with such qualities are fit for the attainment of <s>sūta</s>-<s>siddhi</s> (mastery over mercury).
The assistants there should be industrious, even more qualified than the disciples,
of good family, and devoted to the master — they should be employed in <s>rasakarma</s> (alchemical operations).
Those who are atheists, of wicked conduct, and who, by deception from a teacher other than their own,
wish to seize knowledge through theft, disguise, and wicked celebration —
nothing succeeds for them, neither <s>maṇi</s> (gems), <s>mantra</s>s, <s>auṣadha</s> (medicines), nor anything else;

children.text: kurvanti yadi mohena nāśayanti svakaṃ dhanam /
children.translated_text: if they attempt out of delusion, they destroy their own wealth;

children.text: iha loke sukhaṃ nāsti paraloke tathaiva ca // VRrs_6.9 //
children.translated_text: there is no happiness for them in this world, nor in the next.
Therefore, when the <s>guru</s> is satisfied by the power of devotion alone,
then should the disciple receive that <s>rasavidyā</s> (science of mercury) for the attainment of self-realization;
having obtained the blessing through the laying of hands on the head, he should practice well.
In a land free from calamity, in a righteous kingdom, delightful,
graced by <s>Umā</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>, in a prosperous and auspicious city —
there should the wise one undertake the <s>sādhana</s> (practice) of <s>rasarāja</s> (mercury, the king of essences),
in a most beautiful garden adorned with four gates.
There, a hall should be constructed, spacious and pleasing,
properly furnished with windows, decorated with divine paintings.
Near that, on level and bright ground, the <s>rasamaṇḍapa</s> (mercury laboratory pavilion) should be built,
well-concealed, spacious, adorned with doors and bolts.
It should be rich with banners, parasols, and canopies, draped with garlands of flowers,
and resounding with the sounds of drums, <s>kāhala</s>s, bells, and horns.

children.text: bhūḥ samā tatra kartavyā sudṛḍhā darpaṇopamā /
children.translated_text: The floor there should be made level, firm, and mirror-like;

children.text: tanmadhye vedikā ramyā kartavyā lakṣaṇānvitā // VRrs_6.16 //
children.translated_text: in its center, a beautiful altar should be constructed, endowed with proper features.
Three <s>niṣka</s>s of gold leaf and nine <s>niṣka</s>s of <s>rasendra</s> (mercury)

children.text: amlena mardayed yāmaṃ tena liṅgaṃ tu kārayet // VRrs_6.17 //
children.translated_text: should be ground with acid for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours); from that, a <s>liṅga</s> should be fashioned.
It should be cooked for one day in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus) with acidic liquid, placed in a lemon;
that <s>liṅga</s> should be worshipped there with most auspicious offerings.
The fruit that accrues from the proper worship of a thousand <s>koṭi</s>s (ten billion) of <s>liṅga</s>s —
that fruit is obtained multiplied a <s>koṭi</s>-fold from the worship of a <s>rasaliṅga</s> (mercury liṅga).
Thousands of sins of <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a Brahmin) and tens of thousands of sins of <s>gohatyā</s> (killing a cow)
are instantly dissolved merely by the sight of a <s>rasaliṅga</s>.
By touching it, liberation is attained — this is the truth spoken by <s>Śiva</s>.
In the southeastern direction, one should worship with the great <s>Aghora</s> <s>mantrarāja</s> (king of mantras).
One should meditate upon the <s>rasaliṅga</s> as having eighteen arms, brilliant white, five faces, three eyes,
mounted upon a corpse, with a blue throat (<s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>).
In his lap, one should visualize the great <s>Devī</s> (Goddess), with one face and four arms,
holding a rosary and a goad in the right hands, and a noose and the gesture of fearlessness in the left,
resplendent like molten gold, wearing yellow garments.

The <s>vidyā</s> (sacred formula) called <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s> consists of <s>Vāṅmayī</s> (Sarasvatī's seed), <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī's seed), <s>Kāmarāja</s> (Kāma's seed), <s>śaktibīja</s>, and <s>rasāṅkuśā</s>;

children.text: yaiḥ samā dvādaśāḥ śaivajñeyā vidyā rasāṅkuśā // VRrs_6.24 //
children.translated_text: together with these, the twelve <s>Śaiva</s> syllables — this should be known as the <s>vidyā</s> called <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s>.
With this <s>vidyā</s>, one should worship the <s>Devī</s> with sandalwood paste, flowers, unbroken rice, and other offerings.
One should worship <s>Nandī</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, and <s>Kulīra</s>, starting from the eastern direction,
with name-mantras beginning with <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) and ending with <s>namaḥ</s>.

body.text: eva nityārcanaṃ tatra kartavyaṃ rasasiddhaye // VRrs_6.26 //
body.translated_text: Thus, daily worship should be performed there for the attainment of <s>rasasiddhi</s> (alchemical success).

children.translated_text: <s>Rasavidyā</s> (the science of mercury), spoken by <s>Śiva</s>, should be given to the practitioner
by the <s>guru</s> with a joyful mind, according to the prescribed method.
At an auspicious <s>muhūrta</s> (moment), under a favorable <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism), endowed with the strength of the moon and stars,
a <s>kalaśa</s> (consecrated vessel) filled with water, adorned with gold, gems, and fruits,
should be placed before the <s>rasaliṅga</s>, wrapped in divine cloth,
and worshipped well with sandalwood paste, flowers, unbroken rice, incense, and food offerings.
At the conclusion of worship, a fire oblation should be performed in a <s>yonikuṇḍa</s> (triangular fire-pit) of proper form,

children.text: tilājyaiḥ pāyasaiḥ puṣpaiḥ śatapuṣpādikaiḥ pṛthak // VRrs_6.30 //
children.translated_text: with sesame seeds and ghee, rice pudding, flowers, and <s>śatapuṣpa</s> (dill) and other substances separately.
At the conclusion of the oblation, with the <s>Aghora</s> and <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s> mantras, the disciple should be summoned —
one who is united with <s>Kālinī</s> <s>śakti</s> (feminine power) and devoted to the attainment of <s>rasasiddhi</s> (alchemical success).

children.text: yasyāstu kuñcitāḥ keśāḥ śyāmā yā padmalocanā /
children.translated_text: She whose hair is curly, who is dark-complexioned, lotus-eyed,

children.text: surūpā taruṇī bhinnā vistīrṇajaghanā śubhā // VRrs_6.32 //
children.translated_text: beautiful in form, youthful, deflowered, with broad hips, auspicious,
with a passionate heart, bowed down by the weight of her full breasts,
tender to kissing, embracing, and touch, and soft-spoken —
adorned with a <s>yoni</s> region resembling a <s>pīpal</s> leaf,

children.text: kṛṣṇapakṣe puṣpavatī sā nārī kālinī smṛtā /
children.translated_text: she who menstruates during the dark fortnight — that woman is known as <s>Kālinī</s>;

children.text: rasabandhe prayoge ca uttamā sā rasāyane // VRrs_6.34 //
children.translated_text: she is the most excellent in the binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), in its application, and in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation).

children.text: tadabhāve surūpā tu yā kācit taruṇāṅganā /
children.translated_text: In her absence, any beautiful young woman may serve;
she should be given for three weeks <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) mixed with ghee,

children.text: karṣaikaikaṃ prabhāte tu sā bhavetkālinīsamā // VRrs_6.35 //
children.translated_text: one <s>karṣa</s> each morning — she then becomes equal to a <s>Kālinī</s>.

children.text: evaṃ śaktiyuto yo 'sau dīkṣayet taṃ gurūttamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the supreme <s>guru</s> should initiate the one who is united with such a <s>śakti</s>;
having bathed him well, he should consecrate him with water from the <s>kalaśa</s> while reciting the <s>mantra</s>.
The excellent <s>guru</s> should bestow the <s>Aghorā</s> and <s>Aṅkuśī</s> <s>vidyā</s>s upon the disciple;
according to his capacity, the worthy disciple should offer <s>gurudakṣiṇā</s> (teacher's fee);

children.text: athājñayā gurormantraṃ lakṣaṃ lakṣaṃ pṛthagjapet // VRrs_6.37 //
children.translated_text: then, by the command of the <s>guru</s>, he should recite each <s>mantra</s> one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) times separately.

body.text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ adyoratara prasphuṭa 2 prakaṭa 2 kaha 2 śamaya 2 jāta 2 daha 2 pātaya 2 oṃ hrīṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hrūṃ aghorāya phaṭ imam aghoramantraṃ tu auṃ kāmarājaśaktibījarasāṅkuśāyai ājñayā vidyāṃ rasāṅkuśām |
body.translated_text: Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ — O <s>Adyoratara</s>, burst forth, burst forth, manifest, manifest, kaha kaha, pacify, pacify, burn, burn, burn, burn, cause to fall, cause to fall — Oṃ hrīṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hrūṃ, to <s>Aghora</s>, phaṭ! This is the <s>Aghora</s> mantra. Auṃ — by the command of the <s>Kāmarāja</s> seed-syllable, the <s>Śakti</s>-<s>bīja</s> <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s> (<s>vidyā</s>) —

body.text: anayā pūjayed devīṃ śaktim aṅkuśavidyayā // VRrs_6.38 //
body.translated_text: with this <s>Aṅkuśa</s> <s>vidyā</s> (goad-incantation), one should worship the goddess <s>Śakti</s>. // VRrs_6.38 //

children.translated_text: One should offer one-tenth (as oblation) in a triangular fire-pit (<s>kuṇḍa</s>) measuring one hand-span,
with <s>Jāti</s> (jasmine) flowers anointed with the three sweets; at the conclusion, worship of a maiden (<s>kanyakārcana</s>). // VRrs_6.39 //
Having done this, one should enter a clean, plastered room with an altar (<s>vedikā</s>).

children.text: ṣaṭkoṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ tatra sindūreṇa dvihastakam // VRrs_6.40 //
children.translated_text: There, a hexagonal (<s>ṣaṭkoṇa</s>) diagram (<s>maṇḍala</s>) of two hand-spans should be drawn with vermilion (<s>sindūra</s>) // VRrs_6.40 //
on the altar, and outside it an eight-petaled

children.text: kamalaṃ caturasraṃ ca caturdvāraiḥ suśobhitam // VRrs_6.41 //
children.translated_text: lotus, square-shaped, beautifully adorned with four gateways. // VRrs_6.41 //
In the pericarp (center), one should place an iron mortar inscribed with gold;
in its center, the king of <s>rasa</s>s (mercury), measuring a hundred <s>pala</s>s,
or fifty, or twenty-five, and worship it as a <s>Rasaliṅga</s> (mercury phallus). // VRrs_6.42 //
Diamond, <s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>Vajrābhra</s> (diamond-mica), magnetite (<s>Kānta</s>), <s>Pāṣāṇa</s> (stone), borax (<s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s>),

children.text: bhūnāgaḥ śaktayaścaitāḥ ṣaṭkoṇe pūjayet kramāt // VRrs_6.43 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūnāga</s> (earth-serpent) — these <s>Śakti</s>s (powers/energies) should be worshipped in the hexagon in order. // VRrs_6.43 //
Orpiment (<s>Gandha</s>), <s>Tālaka</s>, green vitriol (<s>Kāsīsa</s>), realgar (<s>Śilā</s>), <s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>Bhūṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: rājāvarto gairikaṃ ca khyātā uparasā amī /
children.translated_text: <s>Rājāvarta</s>, and red ochre (<s>Gairika</s>) — these are the well-known subsidiary <s>rasa</s>s (<s>uparasa</s>).
These should be worshipped on the eight petals, in order from east to northeast. // VRrs_6.44 //

children.text: rasakaṃ vimalā tāpyaṃ capalā tuttham añjanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Rasaka</s> (calamine), <s>Vimalā</s>, <s>Tāpya</s> (pyrite), <s>Capalā</s> (bismuth), blue vitriol (<s>Tuttha</s>), collyrium (<s>Añjana</s>),

children.text: hiṅgulaṃ sasyakaṃ caiva khyātā ete mahārasāḥ /
children.translated_text: cinnabar (<s>Hiṅgula</s>), and <s>Sasyaka</s> (blue vitriol) — these are the well-known great <s>rasa</s>s (<s>mahārasa</s>).
They should be worshipped on the petal-tips, from east to northeast in order. // VRrs_6.45 //
At the eastern gateway, gold and silver; at the southern, copper and lead;
at the western, tin and magnetite; at the northern, <s>Muṇḍa</s> (zinc) and <s>Tīkṣṇa</s> (steel).
All this should be worshipped with the <s>Aghora</s> (mantra) accompanied by the goad (<s>Aṅkuśa</s>). // VRrs_6.46 //
Corrosive salts (<s>viḍa</s>), <s>Kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) apparatus, alkalies, clays, and salts,
furnace (<s>koṣṭhī</s>), crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>), bellows-pipe (<s>vaṅkanāla</s>), husks, charcoal, and forest stones, // VRrs_7.47 //
bellows (<s>bhastrikā</s>), various tongs (<s>daṇḍikā</s>), grinding stone (<s>śilā</s>), mortar (<s>khalva</s>), and pestle (<s>ulūkhala</s>),
goldsmith's tools, and all types of scales, // VRrs_6.48 //
various vessels made of clay, wood, copper, and iron,
collections of divine herbs, coloring agents, and oils —

children.text: etāni dvārabāhye tu mūlamantreṇa pūjayet // VRrs_6.49 //
children.translated_text: all these should be worshipped outside the doorway with the root mantra (<s>mūlamantra</s>). // VRrs_6.49 //

children.text: vāṅmāyā hrīṃ tataḥ kṣeṃ ca kṣmaśca pañcākṣaro manuḥ /
children.translated_text: Vāṃ, Māyā, Hrīṃ, then Kṣeṃ, and Kṣma — (this is) the five-syllabled mantra (<s>manu</s>).
With this mantra, one should worship <s>Bhairava</s> there.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ rasasiddhānāṃ nāma saṃkīrtayet tadā // VRrs_6.50 //
children.translated_text: Then one should recite the names of all the <s>Rasasiddha</s>s (masters of mercury). // VRrs_6.50 //
<s>Vyālācārya</s>, <s>Candrasena</s>, <s>Subuddhi</s>, <s>Naravāhana</s>,
<s>Nāgārjuna</s>, <s>Ratnaghoṣa</s>, <s>Surānanda</s>, <s>Yaśodhana</s>, // VRrs_6.51 //
<s>Indra</s>, <s>Māṇḍavya</s>, <s>Carpaṭī</s>, <s>Śūrasenaka</s>,

children.text: āgamo nāgabuddhiś ca khaṇḍaḥ kāpāliko mataḥ // VRrs_6.52 //
children.translated_text: <s>Āgama</s>, <s>Nāgabuddhi</s>, <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, the <s>Kāpālika</s> (skull-bearer), // VRrs_6.52 //
<s>Kāmāri</s>, the <s>Tāntrika</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Laṅkā</s>, <s>Lampaṭa</s>, <s>Śārada</s>,

children.text: bāṇāsuro muniśreṣṭho govindaḥ kapilo baliḥ // VRrs_6.53 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bāṇāsura</s>, the best of sages, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Bali</s>. // VRrs_6.53 //

children.text: ete sarve tu sūtendrā rasasiddhā mahābalāḥ /
children.translated_text: All these are lords of mercury (<s>sūtendra</s>), <s>Rasasiddha</s>s of great power;
they roam in all worlds, eternal, devoted to enjoyment. // VRrs_6.54 //
Twenty-seven in number, they are the bestowers of success in mercury (alchemy).

children.text: vaidyāḥ pūjyāḥ prayatnena tataḥ kuryādrasārcanam // VRrs_6.55 //
children.translated_text: Physicians should be worshipped with effort; then one should perform the worship of mercury (<s>rasārcana</s>). // VRrs_6.55 //
Delighting the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s and gods, one should satiate the chosen deities,
maidens (<s>kumārī</s>), <s>Yoginī</s>s, lords of <s>yogī</s>s, practitioners of assemblies (<s>melaka</s>) —
one should satiate and worship with devotion, according to one's ability. // VRrs_6.56 //
Thus, equipped with all requisites, one should perform the mercury festival (<s>rasotsava</s>),
for the pacification of all obstacles, granting all desired fruits. // VRrs_6.57 //
Otherwise, a deluded person who, without the proper sequence of mantra initiation (<s>mantradīkṣā</s>),
and without a <s>guru</s> (teacher), wishes to accomplish the mastery of mercury — // VRrs_6.58 //
he does not attain success even by hundreds of crores of efforts.
Therefore, with all effort, one should perform the procedure prescribed in the treatise (<s>śāstra</s>). // VRrs_6.59 //

children.text: samyaksādhanasodyamā guruyutā rājājñayālaṃkṛtā nānākarmaparāṅmukhā rasaparāś cāḍhyā janaiścārthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Properly striving in practice, endowed with a <s>guru</s>, adorned with royal authorization, not averse to various labors, devoted to mercury, wealthy, and sought after by people,

children.text: mātrāyantrasupākakarmakuśalāḥ sarvauṣadhe kovidāḥ teṣāṃ sidhyati nānyathā vidhibalācchrīpāradaḥ pāradaḥ // VRrs_6.60 //
children.translated_text: skilled in dosage, apparatus, and proper cooking procedures, expert in all medicines — for such ones, the blessed mercury succeeds by the power of proper method, not otherwise. // VRrs_6.60 //
The science of <s>rasa</s> (alchemy) should be given to <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s for the sake of dharma,

children.text: rājñe vaiśyāya vṛddhyarthaṃ dāsyārtham itarasya ca // VRrs_6.61 //
children.translated_text: to a king and <s>Vaiśya</s> for the sake of prosperity, and to others for the sake of service. // VRrs_6.61 //
When the <s>guru</s> is pleased, <s>Śiva</s> is pleased; when <s>Śiva</s> is pleased, <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is likewise pleased.

children.text: rase tuṣṭe kriyāḥ sarvāḥ sidhyantyeva na saṃśayaḥ // VRrs_6.62 //
children.translated_text: When <s>rasa</s> is pleased, all procedures succeed — there is no doubt. // VRrs_6.62 //
The science of <s>rasa</s> must be firmly kept secret, as surely as one's mother's secret.

children.text: bhaved vīryavatī guptā nirvīryā ca prakāśanāt // VRrs_6.63 //
children.translated_text: When kept secret, it possesses power; when disclosed, it becomes powerless. // VRrs_6.63 //
The treatment should not be made known to the patient, nor known to many.
A medicine known by many patients becomes powerless. // VRrs_6.64 //
One should establish a mercury laboratory (<s>rasaśālā</s>) in a place free from all disturbances,
in a region abounding in all medicinal plants, pleasant, and possessing a well. // VRrs_7.1 //
In the direction presided over by <s>Yakṣa</s> (north), <s>Tryakṣa</s> (Śiva, northeast), and <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> (Indra, east) — in a splendid location,
equipped with various apparatus, beautifully adorned with an enclosure wall. // VRrs_7.2 //
In the eastern part of the laboratory, one should install <s>Rasabhairava</s> (the mercury deity).

children.text: vahnikarmāṇi cāgneye yāmye pāṣāṇakarma ca // VRrs_7.3 //
children.translated_text: Fire-operations in the southeast (<s>āgneya</s>); stone-working in the south (<s>yāmya</s>). // VRrs_7.3 //
Cutting operations in the southwest (<s>nairṛtya</s>); washing and the like in the west (<s>vāruṇa</s>).
Drying in the northwest (<s>vāyu</s>) direction; transmutation operations (<s>vedhakarma</s>) in the north;
storage of perfected substances should be done in the northeast (<s>īśa</s>) corner. // VRrs_7.4 //
A collection of materials should be made for the purpose of mercury processing:
a smelting furnace (<s>sattvapātana-koṣṭhī</s>), a dripping furnace (<s>jharat-koṣṭhī</s>), well-made, // VRrs_7.5 //
an underground furnace (<s>bhūmi-koṣṭhī</s>), a portable furnace (<s>calat-koṣṭhī</s>), and many water troughs,
