a pair of bellows, and likewise tubes (<s>nalikā</s>) of bamboo and iron. // VRrs_7.6 //
Cauldrons of gold-alloy, <s>Ghoṣa</s> (bell-metal), copper, and stone, and leather ones as well;
various implements and materials should also be gathered. // VRrs_7.7 //
Pounding mortars, grinding stones, small and round troughs,
iron heated mortars, and grinders of the same kind. // VRrs_7.8 //
For the purpose of filtering materials, (sieves) rich with thousands of fine holes,

children.text: cālanī ca kaṭatrāṇi śalākā hi ca kuṇḍalī // VRrs_7.9 //
children.translated_text: a sieve (<s>cālanī</s>), ladles (<s>kaṭatrāṇi</s>), a probe (<s>śalākā</s>), and a ring-tongs (<s>kuṇḍalī</s>). // VRrs_7.9 //

children.text: cālanī trividhā proktā tatsvarūpaṃ ca kathyate /
children.translated_text: The sieve is declared to be of three kinds; its nature is described:
one made of bamboo rods, woven with threads —

children.text: kīrtitā sā sadā sthūladravyāṇāṃ gālane hitā // VRrs_7.10 //
children.translated_text: that is always recommended for sifting coarse substances. // VRrs_7.10 //

body.text: cūrṇacālanahetośca cālanyanyāpi vaṃśajā // VRrs_7.11 //
body.translated_text: And for the purpose of sifting powder, another sieve also made of bamboo, // VRrs_7.11 //

children.translated_text: made from (bark of) <s>Karṇikāra</s>, <s>Śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton), or <s>Harijāta</s>,
with a frame of four <s>aṅgula</s>s (finger-breadths) in width — well-made. // VRrs_7.12 //
One <s>Aratni</s> (cubit) in width like a ring, wrapped in goat-skin,
with the bottom covered with horse-hair cloth — that is the superior sieve.

children.text: tayā pracālanaṃ kuryāddhartuṃ sūkṣmataraṃ rajaḥ // VRrs_7.13 //
children.translated_text: With it, one should sift to retain the finest powder. // VRrs_7.13 //
Crucible materials: clay, husks, cotton, forest-stones, and flour-paste.
Medicines are of three kinds: mineral-based, metal-based, and plant-root-based.

children.text: śikhitrā govaraṃ caiva śarkarā ca sitopalā // VRrs_7.14 //
children.translated_text: Also: <s>Śikhitrā</s> (peacock feather / embers), cow-dung, sugar, and rock-candy. // VRrs_7.14 //

body.text: śikhitrāḥ pāvakocchiṣṭā aṅgārāḥ kokilā matāḥ // VRrs_7.15 //
body.translated_text: <s>Śikhitrā</s>s are the remnants of fire — embers are called <s>Kokilā</s>. // VRrs_7.15 //

body.text: kokilāś cetitāṅgārā nirvāṇāḥ payasā vinā // VRrs_7.16 //
body.translated_text: <s>Kokilā</s>s are live embers; extinguished ones (cooled) without water (are different). // VRrs_7.16 //

children.text: piṣṭakaṃ chagaṇaṃ chāṇam upalaṃ cotpalaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Piṣṭaka</s>, <s>Chagaṇa</s>, <s>Chāṇa</s>, <s>Upala</s>, and <s>Utpala</s> likewise,
<s>Giriṇḍa</s>, <s>Upala</s>, <s>Sāṭhī</s> — these are names for dried cow-dung cakes. // VRrs_7.17 //

body.text: kācāyomṛdvarāṭānāṃ kūpikā caṣakāni ca // VRrs_7.18 //
body.translated_text: Bottles (<s>kūpikā</s>) and cups (<s>caṣaka</s>) of glass, iron, clay, and cowries; // VRrs_7.18 //

body.text: kūpikā kupikā siddhā golā caiva giriṇḍikā // VRrs_7.19 //
body.translated_text: <s>Kūpikā</s>, <s>Kupikā</s>, <s>Siddhā</s>, <s>Golā</s>, and <s>Giriṇḍikā</s> — // VRrs_7.19 //

children.text: caṣakaṃ ca kaṭorī ca vāṭikā khārikā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Caṣaka</s>, <s>Kaṭorī</s>, <s>Vāṭikā</s>, <s>Khārikā</s>,

children.text: kañcolī grāhikā ceti nāmānyekārthakāni hi // VRrs_7.20 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kañcolī</s>, and <s>Grāhikā</s> — these names are synonymous. // VRrs_7.20 //
Winnowing baskets and bamboo vessels, small bowls and conch-shells,
razors, cooking vessels, and whatever else is suitable there,
a ladle (<s>pālikā</s>), a small cup (<s>karṇikā</s>), and vegetable-cutting blades. // VRrs_7.21 //
From the sweeping of the laboratory to the final stage of mercury cooking —
whatever else is useful in that (process), all of it, by the supreme <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), // VRrs_7.22 //
the glorious <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s> — everything should be consecrated with mantras and worshipped.

children.text: anyathā tadgataṃ tejaḥ parigṛhṇanti bhairavāḥ // VRrs_7.23 //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, the <s>Bhairava</s>s seize the potency contained therein. // VRrs_7.23 //
Physicians learned in mercury science, those knowledgeable in lexicons (<s>nighaṇṭu</s>), and commentators,
those who know the languages of all regions — they too should be gathered by the practitioners. // VRrs_7.24 //

body.text: rasapākāvasānaṃ hi sadāghoraṃ ca jāpayet // VRrs_7.25 //
body.translated_text: From (the beginning to) the conclusion of mercury cooking, one should always recite the <s>Aghora</s> (mantra). // VRrs_7.25 //

body.text: sodyamāḥ śucayaḥ śūrā baliṣṭhāḥ paricārakāḥ // VRrs_7.26 //
body.translated_text: The attendants should be energetic, clean, brave, and strong. // VRrs_7.26 //

children.translated_text: Righteous, truthful, learned, a worshipper of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Keśava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>),
compassionate, and with lotus-marked hands — such a one should be appointed in mercury medicine. // VRrs_7.27 //
One whose palm bears the marks of a flag, water-pot, lotus, fish, bow, and hook —
and who has lines below the ring finger — he is one with the 'nectar hand' (<s>amṛtahasta</s>). // VRrs_7.28 //
One who is uninstructed, devoid of compassion, greedy, and without a <s>guru</s>,

children.text: kṛṣṇarekhākaro vaidyo dagdhahastaḥ sa ucyate // VRrs_7.29 //
children.translated_text: a physician who has black lines (on the palm) — he is called one with a 'burning hand' (<s>dagdhahasta</s>). // VRrs_7.29 //

body.text: nigrahamantrajñāste yojyā nidhisādhane // VRrs_7.30 //
body.translated_text: Those who know subjugation mantras should be employed in treasure-seeking (<s>nidhisādhana</s>). // VRrs_7.30 //

children.translated_text: Strong, truthful, red-eyed, and dark-bodied,
those who know the science of terrifying spirits — they should be employed in the accomplishment of ritual offerings (<s>balisādhana</s>). // VRrs_7.31 //
Non-greedy, truth-speakers, worshippers of gods and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s,
self-controlled, eating wholesome food — such ones should be employed in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). // VRrs_7.32 //
Wealthy, generous, equipped with all requisite materials,

children.text: guruvākyaratā nityaṃ dhātuvādeṣu te śubhāḥ // VRrs_7.33 //
children.translated_text: always devoted to the <s>guru</s>'s word — they are auspicious in metallic transmutation (<s>dhātuvāda</s>). // VRrs_7.33 //
Those who know the names of the respective medicines, who are pure and free from deceit,
who know the languages of various regions — they are regarded (as suitable) for the collection of medicines. // VRrs_7.34 //
For those who are pure, truthful in speech, of devout faith, and of firm mind,
whose consciousness is free from doubt — mercury always succeeds. // VRrs_7.35 //
Mercury perfected through the eighteen procedures — that (practitioner) is the best of adepts.

children.text: hā raso naṣṭamityuktvā sevetānyatra taṃ rasam // VRrs_7.36 //
children.translated_text: Saying 'Alas! The mercury is lost!' one should employ that mercury elsewhere (as a test). // VRrs_7.36 //

children.text: rasasiddho bhavenmartyo dātā bhoktā na yācakaḥ /
children.translated_text: A mortal who has perfected mercury becomes a giver, an enjoyer, and not a beggar;

children.text: jarāmukto jagatpūjyo divyakāntiḥ sadā sukhī // VRrs_7.37 //
children.translated_text: freed from old age, worshipped by the world, possessed of divine radiance, and always happy. // VRrs_7.37 //
The technical terminology (<s>paribhāṣā</s>) of the lord of mercury is now stated by <s>Somadeva</s> for the awakening of dull physicians,

children.text: paribhāṣā rasendrasya śāstraiḥ siddhaiśca bhāṣitā // VRrs_8.1 //
children.translated_text: as spoken in the treatises and by the accomplished masters. // VRrs_8.1 //

children.text: ardhaṃ siddharasasya tailaghṛtayorlehasya bhāgo 'ṣṭamaḥ saṃsiddhākhilalohacūrṇavaṭakādīnāṃ tathā saptamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Half of the perfected mercury (preparation); of oils and ghee, one-eighth is the portion of the electuary (<s>leha</s>); of all perfected metal-powder pills and the like, one-seventh —

children.text: yo dīyeta bhiṣagvarāya gadibhirnirdiśya dhanvantarim sarvārogyasukhāptaye nigadito bhāgaḥ sa dhanvantareḥ // VRrs_8.2 //
children.translated_text: that which is given by the patients to the best physician, invoking <s>Dhanvantari</s>, for the attainment of complete health and happiness — that portion is called the share of <s>Dhanvantari</s>. // VRrs_8.2 //
That eleventh part of the materials purchased for medicine

children.text: vaṇigbhyo gṛhyate vaidyai rudrabhāgaḥ sa ucyate // VRrs_8.3 //
children.translated_text: which is taken from the merchants by the physicians — that is called the share of <s>Rudra</s>. // VRrs_8.3 //
A physician of greedy mind who takes more than <s>Rudra</s>'s share

children.text: dāpayellubdhadhīr vaidyaḥ sa syād viśvāsaghātakaḥ // VRrs_8.4 //
children.translated_text: and administers improper medicine — he becomes a betrayer of trust. // VRrs_8.4 //
Mercury ground with minerals such as sulfur and the like, without liquid,
when very smooth and having the appearance of lampblack — that is called <s>Kajjalī</s> (black sulfide of mercury). // VRrs_8.5 //

body.text: sadravā marditā saiva rasapaṅka iti smṛtā // VRrs_8.6 //
body.translated_text: The same ground with liquid is known as <s>Rasapaṅka</s> (mercury paste). // VRrs_8.6 //

children.translated_text: From mercury equal in portion to the sun's share (one-twelfth), then sulfur equal to half a <s>niṣka</s>, grinding bit by bit in a mortar,

children.text: arkātape tīvratare vimardyāt piṣṭī bhavet sā navanītarūpā // VRrs_8.7 //
children.translated_text: grinding under the intense heat of the sun, it becomes <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste) — having the form of fresh butter. // VRrs_8.7 //

children.text: khalle vimardya gandhena dugdhena saha pāradam /
children.translated_text: Grinding mercury with sulfur and milk together in a mortar —

children.text: peṣaṇāt piṣṭatāṃ yāti sā piṣṭīti matā paraiḥ // VRrs_8.8 //
children.translated_text: that which attains a ground state through grinding is considered by others to be <s>piṣṭī</s> (amalgamation). // VRrs_8.8 //
With one-fourth part gold, mercury [ground for] sixty [strokes] —
that becomes the <s>pātana-piṣṭī</s> (sublimation amalgam), bestowing the highest perfection of mercury. // VRrs_8.9 //
Silver or gold, killed with mercury, sulphur, etc.,

children.text: samutthitaṃ ca bahuśaḥ sā kṛṣṭī hematārayoḥ // VRrs_8.10 //
children.translated_text: and revived many times — that is <s>kṛṣṭī</s> (extraction) of gold and silver. // VRrs_8.10 //

body.text: piṣṭīṃ kṣipet suvarṇātarna varṇo hīyate tayā // VRrs_8.11 //
body.translated_text: One should cast <s>piṣṭī</s> into gold — its color is not diminished by that. // VRrs_8.11 //

body.text: svarṇakṛṣṭyā kṛtaṃ bījaṃ rasasya parirañjanam // VRrs_8.12 //
body.translated_text: The <s>bīja</s> (seed-agent) made from gold-extraction serves for coloring mercury. // VRrs_8.12 //

children.translated_text: Copper combined with iron, melted and cast repeatedly
in a flux of sulphur and breadfruit extract — what comes out is the excellent metal;

body.text: tena raktīkṛtaṃ svarṇaṃ hemaraktītyudāhṛtam // VRrs_8.14 //
body.translated_text: gold reddened by that is called <s>hemaraktī</s> (gold-reddening). // VRrs_8.14 //

children.translated_text: When that [reddener] is cast into melted gold, it enhances the color;
it also colors silver and bestows the coloring of the seed-agent. // VRrs_8.15 //
In exactly the same way, the charming <s>tāraraktī</s> (silver-reddening) should be prepared —

children.text: rañjanī khalu rūpyasya bījānāmapi rañjanī // VRrs_8.16 //
children.translated_text: it colors silver and also colors the seed-agents. // VRrs_8.16 //

children.text: mṛtena vā baddharasena vānyallohena vā sādhitamanyaloham /
children.translated_text: A metal processed with killed mercury, or with bound mercury, or with another metal —

children.text: sitaṃ ca pītatvamupāgataṃ taddalaṃ hi candrānalayoḥ prasiddham // VRrs_8.17 //
children.translated_text: white [metal] that has become yellow — that is <s>dala</s> (leaf/foil), well known for [simulating] silver and gold. // VRrs_8.17 //
Combined with mercury bound by the <s>māsa</s> method,

children.text: sādhitaṃ vānyalohena sitaṃ pītaṃ ca taddalam // VRrs_8.18 //
children.translated_text: or processed with another metal — white or yellow, that is <s>dala</s> (foil). // VRrs_8.18 //
Copper killed with <s>mākṣika</s> (chalcopyrite) and revived ten times,
and likewise purified lead — two [parts], four <s>palas</s> [each]; // VRrs_8.19 //
killed again with <s>nīlāñjana</s> (antimony) and revived seven times —
this is proclaimed as the perfected copper-lead [alloy]. // VRrs_8.20 //
Mercury processed with that, held in the mouth by a person,
destroys in a mere month the host of urinary diseases especially. // VRrs_8.21 //
With proper diet for a year, along with grey hair and wrinkles [disappearing],
having vulture-keen vision, radiant strength, and endowed with complete health — // VRrs_8.22 //

children.text: lohaṃ lohāntare kṣiptaṃ dhmātaṃ nirvāpitaṃ drave /
children.translated_text: A metal cast into another metal, blown and quenched in a flux,
becoming pale-yellow in luster — that is called <s>piñjarī</s> (the yellowish alloy). // VRrs_8.23 //

children.text: bhāgāḥ ṣoḍaśa tārasya tathā dvādaśa bhāsvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Sixteen parts of silver and twelve parts of gold,
combined together — by that it is called <s>candrārka</s> (moon-sun alloy). // VRrs_8.24 //
If another metal is cast into the metal to be processed through a tube,

children.text: nirvāpaṇaṃ tu tatproktaṃ vaidyairnirvāhaṇaṃ khalu // VRrs_8.25 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>nirvāpaṇa</s> (quenching), and physicians call it <s>nirvāhaṇa</s> (finishing) indeed. // VRrs_8.25 //
One should cast the quenching substance into the material to be quenched in equal parts;

children.text: āvāhya vāpanīye ca bhāge dṛṣṭe ca dṛṣṭavat // VRrs_8.26 //
children.translated_text: for <s>āvāhya</s> (invocatory) and <s>vāpanīya</s> (casting) procedures, in the observed proportion, as observed. // VRrs_8.26 //

body.text: mṛtaṃ tarati yattoye lohaṃ vāritaraṃ hi tat // VRrs_8.27 //
body.translated_text: A killed metal that floats on water — that is indeed called <s>vāritara</s> (water-floater). // VRrs_8.27 //

children.translated_text: That which, when rubbed between thumb and index finger, enters the lines [of the skin] —
that is designated as killed metal, by the name <s>rekhāpūrva</s> (line-entering). // VRrs_8.28 //
Having the soft touch of jaggery and <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea) seeds, combined with honey and ghee,

children.text: nāyāti prakṛtiṃ dhmātād apunarbhavam ucyate // VRrs_8.29 //
children.translated_text: that which does not revert to its original form when blown — it is called <s>apunarbhava</s> (irreversible). // VRrs_8.29 //
One should place a heavy substance and grain on top of it;
that which crosses water like a swan — it is proclaimed as the best. // VRrs_8.30 //

children.text: raupyeṇa saha saṃyuktaṃ dhmātaṃ raupyeṇa cel laget /
children.translated_text: When combined with silver and blown, if it fuses with the silver,

children.text: tadā nirutthamityuktaṃ lohaṃ tad apunarbhavam // VRrs_8.31 //
children.translated_text: then it is called <s>niruttha</s> (non-rising), an irreversible metal. // VRrs_8.31 //
When through specific quenching it assumes various colors,
becoming soft and beautifully workable — that is called <s>bīja</s> (seed-agent). // VRrs_8.32 //
This very thing has been described by physicians as <s>uttaraṇa</s> (crossing over/transmutation) indeed —
the destruction of one metal through contact with another. // VRrs_8.33 //

body.text: pradhmātaṃ vaṅkanālena tattāḍanamudāhṛtam // VRrs_8.34 //
body.translated_text: That which is blown through a tube — that is called <s>tāḍana</s> (striking). // VRrs_8.34 //

children.translated_text: Powdered mica combined with rice, tied in cloth and placed in sour gruel —
what is extracted by rubbing through the cloth is called <s>dhānyābhra</s> (grain-mica). // VRrs_8.35 //
Combined with alkalis, acids, and fluxes, blown in a mine-furnace —
the essence that comes out from that is called <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence). // VRrs_8.36 //
A furnace with peak-filling bellows, through the method of blowing,
filled to the brim — that is considered <s>ekakolīsaka</s> (single-furnace operation). // VRrs_8.37 //

children.text: drāvaṇe sattvapāte ca mādhukāḥ khādirāḥ śubhāḥ /
children.translated_text: For melting and essence-extraction, <s>mādhuka</s> (Madhuca wood) and <s>khādira</s> (Acacia wood) charcoals are excellent;

children.text: durdrāve vaṃśajāste tu svedane bādarāḥ śubhāḥ // VRrs_8.38 //
children.translated_text: for difficult melting, bamboo [charcoals]; for steaming, <s>bādara</s> (jujube-wood) charcoals are excellent. // VRrs_8.38 //
Mercury extracted by grinding with ginger juice from a substance placed in the <s>vidyādhara</s>-named apparatus —

children.text: samākṛṣṭo raso yo 'sau hiṅgulākṛṣṭa ucyate // VRrs_8.39 //
children.translated_text: that mercury is called <s>hiṅgulākṛṣṭa</s> (cinnabar-extracted). // VRrs_8.39 //
Bell-metal with a small amount of orpiment, struck through a tube —

children.text: muktaraṅgaṃ hi tattāmraṃ ghoṣākṛṣṭam udāhṛtam // VRrs_8.40 //
children.translated_text: that copper, freed of its color, is called <s>ghoṣākṛṣṭa</s> (sound-extracted). // VRrs_8.40 //
Combined with iron and antimony, blown hard repeatedly —
the black, easily-melting, excellent lead — that is what is meant. // VRrs_8.41 //

body.text: mṛtasya punarudbhūtiḥ samproktotthāpanākhyayā // VRrs_8.42 //
body.translated_text: The revival of a killed [metal] is called by the name <s>utthāpana</s> (raising). // VRrs_8.42 //

body.text: drutadravasya nikṣepo drave tad ḍhālanaṃ matam // VRrs_8.43 //
body.translated_text: The casting of a melted liquid into a flux — that is considered <s>ḍhālana</s> (pouring). // VRrs_8.43 //

children.translated_text: Thirty <s>palas</s> of lead, ground with <s>bhānu</s> (Calotropis) milk,
should be repeatedly ground and calcined until one <s>karṣa</s> remains. // VRrs_8.44 //
That does not diminish at all even by a thousand calcinations;
this <s>capala</s> (bismuth) is prescribed by the practitioners as being born from lead. // VRrs_8.45 //

body.text: itthaṃ hi capalaḥ kāryo vaṅgasyāpi na saṃśayaḥ // VRrs_8.46 //
body.translated_text: Thus indeed <s>capala</s> should be prepared — from tin also, without doubt. // VRrs_8.46 //

body.text: tatspṛṣṭahastasaṃspṛṣṭaḥ kevalo badhyate rasaḥ // VRrs_8.47 //
body.translated_text: Mercury touched by a hand that has touched that [capala] alone becomes bound. // VRrs_8.47 //

children.text: sa raso dhātuvādeṣu śasyate na rasāyane /
children.translated_text: That mercury is praised in alchemical transmutation, not in rejuvenation therapy;

children.text: ayaṃ hi kharvaṇākhyena lokanāthena kīrtitaḥ // VRrs_8.48 //
children.translated_text: this was proclaimed by the lord known as <s>Kharvaṇa</s>. // VRrs_8.48 //
Washed with the excrement-water of earth-serpent (<s>bhūbhujaṅga</s>), the impurity removed —

children.text: kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ hi tatproktaṃ dhautākhyaṃ rasavādibhiḥ // VRrs_8.49 //
children.translated_text: the black-colored [mercury] is called <s>dhauta</s> (washed) by the mercury-practitioners. // VRrs_8.49 //

body.text: dravyayormardanādhmānād dvaṃdvānaṃ parikīrtitam // VRrs_8.50 //
body.translated_text: The grinding and blowing of two substances together is proclaimed as <s>dvaṃdvāna</s> (pairing). // VRrs_8.50 //

children.translated_text: The casting of a fraction or more into a base metal that matches its color or into gold —
or with liquids, a fire-fed portion — that is considered <s>bhañjanī</s> (the breaker) by practitioners. // VRrs_8.51 //

children.text: pataṅgīkalkato jātā lohe tāre ca hematā /
children.translated_text: The golden color produced in base metal and silver from the paste of <s>pataṅgī</s> (sappanwood) —

children.text: dināni katicitsthitvā yātyasau cullakā matā // VRrs_8.52 //
children.translated_text: that which, after standing for a few days, fades — that is considered <s>cullakā</s> (temporary coloring). // VRrs_8.52 //
The exudate from a long-colored metal, or from prolonged blowing,
is designated by the name <s>pataṅgīrāga</s> (sappanwood-coloring). // VRrs_8.53 //
The casting of another substance into a metal that is being processed —

children.text: sa āvāpaḥ pratīvāpas tadevācchādanaṃ matam // VRrs_8.54 //
children.translated_text: that is <s>āvāpa</s> (addition); <s>pratīvāpa</s> (counter-addition) is considered the same as <s>ācchādana</s> (covering). // VRrs_8.54 //
When metal is standing in fire, pausing for the duration of eight blinks,

children.text: salilasya parikṣepaḥ so 'bhiṣeka iti smṛtaḥ // VRrs_8.55 //
children.translated_text: the sprinkling of water — that is known as <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration/sprinkling). // VRrs_8.55 //

body.text: taptasyāpsu vinikṣepo nirvāpaḥ snapanaṃ ca tat // VRrs_8.56 //
body.translated_text: The casting of the heated [metal] into water is <s>nirvāpa</s> (quenching), also called <s>snapana</s> (bathing). // VRrs_8.56 //

body.text: pratīvāpādikaṃ kāryaṃ drute lohe sunirmale // VRrs_8.57 //
body.translated_text: The <s>pratīvāpa</s> and other procedures should be performed on the melted, thoroughly pure metal. // VRrs_8.57 //

children.translated_text: When the fire has blazing flames accompanied by the rising of white [color] —

children.text: śuddhāvartas tadā jñeyaḥ sa kālaḥ sattvanirgame // VRrs_8.58 //
children.translated_text: that should be known as <s>śuddhāvarta</s> (pure vortex), the time for essence-extraction. // VRrs_8.58 //
When a flame resembling the fluxing substance is seen during blowing —

children.text: drāvasyonmukhatā seyaṃ bījāvartaḥ sa ucyate // VRrs_8.59 //
children.translated_text: that is the readiness of the flux to melt; it is called <s>bījāvarta</s> (seed-vortex). // VRrs_8.59 //

body.text: vahnistham eva śītaṃ yattaduktaṃ svāṅgaśītalam // VRrs_8.60 //
body.translated_text: That which cools while still in the fire — that is called <s>svāṅgaśītala</s> (self-cooled). // VRrs_8.60 //

body.text: agnerākṛṣya śītaṃ yattadbahiḥ śītamucyate // VRrs_8.61 //
body.translated_text: That which is drawn from the fire and [then] cooled — that is called <s>bahiḥśīta</s> (externally cooled). // VRrs_8.61 //

children.translated_text: The cooking with alkalis, acids, or medicines of [a substance] placed in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus) —
that is called <s>svedana</s> (steaming), which loosens impurities. // VRrs_8.62 //
Grinding with the mentioned medicines, all sour substances, and sour gruels —
that is called <s>mardana</s> (trituration), which destroys external impurities. // VRrs_8.63 //
That which, through medicines prescribed for trituration, causes loss of the ground state [of mercury] —
that is <s>mūrchana</s> (swooning/fainting of mercury), which destroys the skin-like coating of tin and mercury. // VRrs_8.64 //
The restoration to its own form through steaming, heating, and other methods —
that is called <s>utthāpana</s> (reviving), which destroys the fainting condition. // VRrs_8.65 //

children.text: svarūpasya vināśena piṣṭatvād bandhanaṃ hi tat /
children.translated_text: The binding through destruction of its own form into a ground state —

children.text: vidvadbhirnirjitaḥ sūto naṣṭapiṣṭiḥ sa ucyate // VRrs_8.66 //
children.translated_text: mercury thus conquered by the wise is called <s>naṣṭapiṣṭi</s> (lost-ground). // VRrs_8.66 //
The extraction upward, downward, and sideways of mercury ground with the prescribed medicines and placed in an apparatus —
that is called <s>pātana</s> (sublimation), which destroys the skin-coating produced by contact with tin and mercury. // VRrs_8.67 //
The three-day sojourn in a pot of mercury combined with water and rock salt —

children.text: sthitir āsthāpanī kumbhe yāsau rodhanamucyate // VRrs_8.68 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>rodhana</s> (arresting/blocking). // VRrs_8.68 //
For the cessation of fickleness of mercury that has gained potency through arresting,

children.text: kriyate pārade svedaḥ proktaṃ niyamanaṃ hi tat // VRrs_8.69 //
children.translated_text: steaming is performed on mercury — that is called <s>niyamana</s> (restraining). // VRrs_8.69 //
Combined with minerals, stones, roots, etc., placed in a pot,

children.text: grāsārthaṃ tridinaṃ svedo dīpanaṃ tanmataṃ budhaiḥ // VRrs_8.70 //
children.translated_text: steaming for three days for the purpose of feeding — that is considered <s>dīpana</s> (kindling) by the wise. // VRrs_8.70 //
The measure of the edible substance for a given quantity of mercury —
the amount specified — that is called <s>grāsamāna</s> (the feeding dose). // VRrs_8.71 //

children.text: grāsasya cāraṇaṃ garbhe drāvaṇaṃ jāraṇaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: The digestion of the feed in the interior, and the melting — that is <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestion);

children.text: iti trirūpā nirdiṣṭā jāraṇā varavārttikaiḥ // VRrs_8.72 //
children.translated_text: thus the three forms [of digestion] are described by the excellent practitioners. // VRrs_8.72 //

body.text: grāsaḥ piṇḍaḥ pariṇāmastisraścākhyāḥ parā punaḥ // VRrs_8.73 //
body.translated_text: The feed, the lump, and the transformation — these are three further designations. // VRrs_8.73 //

body.text: samukhā nirmukhā ceti jāraṇā dvividhā punaḥ // VRrs_8.74 //
body.translated_text: <s>Jāraṇā</s> (digestion) is again of two kinds: <s>samukhā</s> (with mouth) and <s>nirmukhā</s> (without mouth). // VRrs_8.74 //

body.text: nirmukhā jāraṇā proktā bījādānena bhāgataḥ // VRrs_8.75 //
body.translated_text: <s>Nirmukhā jāraṇā</s> (mouthless digestion) is described as [accomplished] by adding the seed-agent in portions. // VRrs_8.75 //

body.text: śuddhaṃ svarṇaṃ ca rūpyaṃ ca bījam ityabhidhīyate // VRrs_8.76 //
body.translated_text: Pure gold and silver are called <s>bīja</s> (seed-agent). // VRrs_8.76 //

body.text: catuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśato bījaprakṣepo mukhamucyate // VRrs_8.77 //
body.translated_text: The addition of the seed-agent in a one-sixty-fourth portion is called <s>mukha</s> (mouth). // VRrs_8.77 //

children.text: evaṃ kṛte raso grāsalolupo mukhavān bhavet /
children.translated_text: When this is done, mercury becomes greedy for the feed and becomes 'with mouth';
it becomes capable of devouring even hard metals —

children.text: iyaṃ hi samukhā proktā jāraṇā mṛgacāriṇā // VRrs_8.78 //
children.translated_text: this is proclaimed as <s>samukhā jāraṇā</s> (with-mouth digestion) by <s>Mṛgacārin</s>. // VRrs_8.78 //
Combined with divine herbs, placed in open furnaces,
that which devours all metals etc. — that is the <s>rākṣasavaktravān</s> (demon-mouthed one). // VRrs_8.79 //

body.text: rasasya jaṭhare grāsakṣapaṇaṃ cāraṇā matā // VRrs_8.80 //
body.translated_text: The consumption of the feed in the belly of mercury is considered <s>cāraṇā</s> (internal digestion). // VRrs_8.80 //

body.text: grastasya drāvaṇaṃ garbhe garbhadrutir udāhṛtā // VRrs_8.81 //
body.translated_text: The melting of what has been consumed in the interior is called <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction). // VRrs_8.81 //

children.translated_text: Having externally liquefied in this way dense essences and the like,

children.text: jāraṇāya rasendrasya sā bāhyadrutir ucyate // VRrs_8.82 //
children.translated_text: for the digestion by the lord of mercury — that is called <s>bāhyadruti</s> (external liquefaction). // VRrs_8.82 //

children.text: nirlepatvaṃ drutatvaṃ ca tejastvaṃ laghutā tathā /
children.translated_text: Freedom from coating, liquidity, luster, lightness,
and non-combination with mercury — these are the five characteristics of <s>druti</s> (liquefaction). // VRrs_8.83 //
Through the method of blowing with medicines, metals, minerals, and the like

children.text: saṃtiṣṭhate dravākāraṃ sā drutiḥ parikīrtitā // VRrs_8.84 //
children.translated_text: assume a liquid form — that is proclaimed as <s>druti</s> (liquefaction). // VRrs_8.84 //
The transformation of the liquefied feed through <s>viḍa</s>-apparatus and other methods,

children.text: jāraṇetyucyate tasyāḥ prakārāḥ santi koṭiśaḥ // VRrs_8.85 //
children.translated_text: is called <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestion); its varieties are in the tens of millions. // VRrs_8.85 //
With alkalis, acids, sulphur and the like, and with sharp urines —
for the purpose of digesting the feed of mercury, that is proclaimed as <s>viḍa</s> (the digestive agent). // VRrs_8.86 //
Through the digestion of well-perfected seed-agents, minerals, etc. by mercury,
the generation of yellow and other colors — that is proclaimed as <s>rañjana</s> (coloring). // VRrs_8.87 //
The casting of gold etc. into mercury placed in an oiled apparatus —

children.text: vedhādhikyakaraṃ lohe sāraṇā sā prakīrttitā // VRrs_8.88 //
children.translated_text: that which increases the transmuting power in metal, is proclaimed as <s>sāraṇā</s> (the flowing). // VRrs_8.88 //
Mercury endowed with pervasive medicines, cast into a substance —

children.text: vedha ityucyate tajjñaiḥ sa cānekavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ // VRrs_8.89 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>vedha</s> (transmutation/penetration) by the experts; it is known to be of many kinds. // VRrs_8.89 //

body.text: lepaḥ kṣepaśca kuntaśca dhūmākhyaḥ śabdasaṃjñakaḥ // VRrs_8.90 //
body.translated_text: <s>Lepa</s> (smearing), <s>kṣepa</s> (casting), <s>kunta</s> (lance), <s>dhūma</s> (smoke), and <s>śabda</s> (sound) — // VRrs_8.90 //

children.text: lepanaṃ kurute lohaṃ svarṇaṃ vā rajataṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: When [mercury] makes a base metal into gold or silver by smearing —

children.text: lepavedhaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ puṭamatra ca saurakam // VRrs_8.91 //
children.translated_text: that should be known as <s>lepavedha</s> (smearing-transmutation); the <s>puṭa</s> (calcination) here is of the solar type. // VRrs_8.91 //

body.text: prakṣepaṇaṃ drute lohe vedhaḥ syātkṣepasaṃjñitaḥ // VRrs_8.92 //
body.translated_text: The casting into melted metal — that transmutation is called <s>kṣepasaṃjñita</s> (casting-type). // VRrs_8.92 //

children.translated_text: That which is the extraction of melted substances by mercury held with tongs,
the production of gold-ness and such, is called <s>kunta-vedha</s> (lance-penetration). // VRrs_8.93 //
By the smoke of mercury cast into a metal that is smoking in fire,

children.text: svarṇādyāpādanaṃ lohe vedhaḥ sa ucyate // VRrs_8.94 //
children.translated_text: the production of gold-ness and such in metal is called <s>dhūma-vedha</s> (smoke-penetration). // VRrs_8.94 //
By the smelting of a small quantity of metal with mercury placed in the mouth of the bellows,
the production of gold-ness or silver-ness is celebrated as <s>śabda-vedha</s> (sound-penetration). // VRrs_8.95 //
The removal of turbidity and such from a substance perfected by mercury,

children.text: prakāśanaṃ ca varṇasya tadudghāṭanam īritam // VRrs_8.96 //
children.translated_text: and the manifestation of its color—that is called <s>udghāṭana</s> (opening/revealing). // VRrs_8.96 //
When mercury is sealed in a vessel with alkalis, acids, and medicines, with great care,
and buried in the ground with effort—that is called <s>svedana</s> (sweating/steaming). // VRrs_8.97 //
When mercury combined with medicines, carefully sealed in a vessel,
is placed inside a stove with gentle fire—that is called <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (depositing). // VRrs_8.98 //
These two—<s>svedana</s> and <s>saṃnyāsa</s>—are certainly for the king of mercury;
they are generators of excellent qualities and also cause rapid pervasion. // VRrs_8.99 //
<s>Somadeva</s>, having gathered from all sides the jewel-like technical terms from the great ocean of alchemical scriptures, most clearly,

children.text: vyaracayadatiyatnāttairimāṃ kaṇṭhamālāṃ kalayatu bhiṣagagryo maṇḍanārthaṃ sabhāyām // VRrs_8.100 //
children.translated_text: composed with great effort this necklace of them—let the foremost physician wear it for adornment in the assembly. // VRrs_8.100 //
He who has studied this chapter becomes a reciter among alchemists;

children.text: rasakarmāṇi kurvāṇo na sa muhyati kutracit // VRrs_8.101 //
children.translated_text: while performing alchemical operations, he is never confused anywhere. // VRrs_8.101 //
Now the <s>yantras</s> (apparatus) of the science of mercury shall be described completely,
examined and summarized by <s>Somadeva</s> at this point. // VRrs_9.1 //
Since mercury is controlled with effort by skilled practitioners
to perform operations like steaming—therefore it is called <s>yantra</s> (instrument). // VRrs_9.2 //
A vessel half-filled with liquid substance and water,
with two openings made carefully on both sides of its mouth— // VRrs_9.3 //
in those openings one should insert a rod, and in the middle, tying a bundle of mercury,
one should steam it—this is known as the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus). // VRrs_9.4 //
One should place the substance to be cooked on a cloth tied over the mouth of a water-filled pot;
where it is cooked by covering—that is called the <s>svedanīyantra</s> (steaming apparatus). // VRrs_9.5 //
With a circumference of eight <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-widths), a width of ten <s>aṅgulas</s>,
a height of four <s>aṅgulas</s>, a water-receptacle below the neck— // VRrs_9.6 //
the mouth of the lower vessel should be inserted into the mouth of the upper vessel
which has a back sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> wide. // VRrs_9.7 //
On the sides, with buffalo milk, powder, and jaggery,
one should coat the joint and let it dry; one should put water in the water-receptacle;
one should place this on the stove—this is called the <s>pātanāyantra</s> (distillation apparatus). // VRrs_9.8 //
The wise one should coat and place the upper vessel in water,

children.text: dīptair vanopalaḥ kuryādadhaḥ pātaṃ prayatnataḥ // VRrs_9.9 //
children.translated_text: and with blazing forest stones, carefully effect the downward distillation. // VRrs_9.9 //
In the middle of a water-filled vessel, one should place a broad potsherd;

children.text: tadupari viḍamadhyagataḥ sthāpyaḥ sūtaḥ kṛtaḥ koṣṭhyām // VRrs_9.10 //
children.translated_text: upon it, mercury placed in the midst of alkali should be set up inside the furnace. // VRrs_9.10 //
Covering with a small light metal bowl, sealed at the joint with six layers of clay,
in the middle of the above-mentioned potsherd, with charcoal made from <s>khadira</s> (acacia) and <s>kola</s> (jujube) wood— // VRrs_9.11 //
by steaming and grinding, the mercury placed in the <s>kacchapayantra</s> (tortoise apparatus) becomes aged (matured);

children.text: agnibalenaiva tato garbhe dravanti sarvasattvāni // VRrs_9.12 //
children.translated_text: then, by the force of fire, all metallic essences melt in the interior. // VRrs_9.12 //
Inside the <s>kacchapayantra</s>, on an earthen pedestal, a lamp is placed;
that into which mercury drops is called the <s>dīpikāyantra</s> (lamp apparatus). // VRrs_9.13 //
In a hole below the neck of the vessel, one should insert a bamboo tube;
making a two-piece bronze vessel as a pair, filled with water inside— // VRrs_9.14 //

children.text: nalikāsya tatra yojyaṃ dṛḍhaṃ taccāpi kārayet /
children.translated_text: the mouth of the tube should be firmly joined there, and that too should be made firmly;

children.text: yuktadravyairvinikṣiptaḥ pūrvaṃ tatra ghaṭe rasaḥ // VRrs_9.15 //
children.translated_text: mercury, combined with proper substances, is first placed in that pot. // VRrs_9.15 //
Heated by fire, it drops through the tube into that water below;

children.text: yāvaduṣṇaṃ bhavet sarvaṃ bhājanaṃ tāvadeva hi /
children.translated_text: as long as the entire vessel remains hot,
the binding of mercury takes place—this is called the <s>ḍekīyantra</s> (ḍekī apparatus). // VRrs_9.16 //
Making a pair of metal crucibles of twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> in measure,
one of them with slight holes, combined with sulphur— // VRrs_9.17 //
in the crucible containing mercury, one should insert the other;
water should be below the mercury, and fire should be lit above and below. // VRrs_9.18 //
In the fine vessel, garlic juice, carefully filtered through cloth,
should be abundantly applied, flooding both mercury and sulphur. // VRrs_9.19 //
Covering the pot above with another sturdy pot,

children.text: saṃdhiṃ vilepayedyatnānmṛdā vastreṇa caiva hi // VRrs_9.20 //
children.translated_text: one should seal the joint carefully with clay and cloth. // VRrs_9.20 //
Between the two pots, a <s>kapota</s> (dove-grade) <s>puṭa</s> (calcination) should always be applied with measured fire;
below the apparatus, one should provide cow-dung fire or even strong fire. // VRrs_9.21 //

children.text: evaṃ tu tridinaṃ kuryāttato yantraṃ vimocayet /
children.translated_text: One should do this for three days, then release the apparatus;

children.text: taptodake taptacullyāṃ na kuryācchītalāṃ kriyām // VRrs_9.22 //
children.translated_text: when the water is hot and the stove is hot, one should not perform a cooling procedure. // VRrs_9.22 //

children.text: na tatra kṣīyate sūto na ca gacchati kutracit /
children.translated_text: In this process, mercury is not lost, nor does it go anywhere;
by this very method, one should perform the <s>gandhaka-jāraṇa</s> (sulphur-digestion by mercury). // VRrs_9.23 //
The apparatus should be known as <s>vidyādhara</s> (knowledge-bearer), formed from two pots joined together;

children.text: cullīṃ caturmukhīṃ kṛtvā yantrabhāṇḍaṃ niveśayet // VRrs_9.24 //
children.translated_text: making a four-mouthed stove, one should place the apparatus-vessel therein. // VRrs_9.24 //
Having placed the medicine inside and sealed the vessel's mouth,

children.text: yantraṃ vidyādharaṃ nāma tantrajñaiḥ parikīrtitam // VRrs_9.25 //
children.translated_text: this apparatus called <s>vidyādhara</s> is celebrated by knowers of the science. // VRrs_9.25 //
Fire above, water below, and in the middle the collection of mercury—
this is called <s>somānala</s> (moon-fire); it causes the digestion of mica and such. // VRrs_9.26 //
I shall describe the <s>garbhayantra</s> (womb apparatus) which makes <s>piṣṭikā</s> (tablet) ash;
four <s>aṅgulas</s> long and three <s>aṅgulas</s> in breadth— // VRrs_9.27 //
one should make a firm earthen crucible with a round mouth;

children.text: loṇasya viṃśatirbhāgā bhāga ekastu gugguloḥ // VRrs_9.28 //
children.translated_text: twenty parts of salt and one part of <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium)— // VRrs_9.28 //

children.text: suślakṣṇaṃ peṣayitvā tu vāraṃ vāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: having ground them very finely, again and again,
making a firm coating on the crucible with half-salt-and-clay water— // VRrs_9.29 //
one should heat it with husk-fire on the ground, steaming gently;

children.text: ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā rasendro bhasmatāṃ vrajet // VRrs_9.30 //
children.translated_text: in one day-and-night, or three nights, <s>rasendra</s> (mercury) turns to ash. // VRrs_9.30 //
Making a potsherd filled with sand and placing upon it

children.text: aparaṃ kharparaṃ tatra śanairmṛdvagninā pacet // VRrs_9.31 //
children.translated_text: another potsherd, one should cook gently with mild fire. // VRrs_9.31 //
With the five alkalis, urine, salt, and <s>viḍa</s> (a type of salt)—

children.text: haṃsapākaṃ samākhyātaṃ yantraṃ tad vārttikottamaiḥ // VRrs_9.32 //
children.translated_text: that is declared by the best practitioners as the <s>haṃsapāka</s> (goose-cooking) apparatus. // VRrs_9.32 //
A glass flask with contents, with concealed mouth, covered with soft cloth finger-thick,

children.text: śoṣitāṃ kācakalaśīṃ triṣu bhāgeṣu pūrayet // VRrs_9.33 //
children.translated_text: dried, should be filled to three parts. // VRrs_9.33 //
Well-established in sand in a vessel one span deep,
one should fill that vessel, covering it with three other [cloth layers]. // VRrs_9.34 //

children.text: bhāṇḍavaktraṃ maṇikayā saṃdhiṃ limpen mṛdā pacet /
children.translated_text: One should seal the mouth of the vessel with a lid, seal the joint with clay, and cook
on the stove, until the burning [sensation ceases] on the back of the lid;
this is the <s>vālukāyantra</s> (sand-bath apparatus); that apparatus depends on salt. // VRrs_9.35 //
Placing carefully in a vessel filled three-quarters with sand,
mercury-balls and such are cooked—this is called the <s>vālukāyantra</s> (sand-bath apparatus). // VRrs_9.36 //

body.text: evaṃ lavaṇanikṣepātproktaṃ lavaṇayantrakam // VRrs_9.37 //
body.translated_text: Likewise, with the addition of salt, it is called the <s>lavaṇayantra</s> (salt apparatus). // VRrs_9.37 //

children.translated_text: On the mouth of a copper vessel coated inside with mercury paste,

children.text: liptvā mṛllavaṇenaiva saṃdhiṃ bhāṇḍatalasya ca // VRrs_9.38 //
children.translated_text: sealing the joint with salt-clay, and on the bottom of the vessel— // VRrs_9.38 //
filling that vessel with sharp alkalis, one should cook as before;

children.text: eva lavaṇayantraṃ syād rasakarmaṇi śasyate // VRrs_9.39 //
children.translated_text: this is the <s>lavaṇayantra</s> (salt apparatus), recommended in mercury operations. // VRrs_9.39 //
Mercury placed in an iron tube, in a vessel filled with salt,
sealed and cooked as before—this is called the <s>nālikāyantra</s> (tube apparatus). // VRrs_9.40 //
A crucible containing mercury, with its entire body buried in sand in a pit—

children.text: dīptopalaiḥ saṃvṛṇuyād yantraṃ tad bhūdharāhvayam // VRrs_9.41 //
children.translated_text: one should cover it with blazing stones—that apparatus is called <s>bhūdhara</s> (earth-bearer). // VRrs_9.41 //
Mercury placed inside a two-piece saucer, in cow-dung fire,

children.text: paceccullyāṃ dviyāmaṃ vā rasaṃ tat puṭayantrakam // VRrs_9.42 //
children.translated_text: one should cook on the stove for two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours)—that is the <s>puṭayantra</s> (calcination apparatus). // VRrs_9.42 //
Sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> wide, one <s>hasta</s> (cubit) in length, uniform—
for the purpose of precipitating metallic essences, this is known as the <s>koṣṭhīyantra</s> (furnace apparatus). // VRrs_9.43 //
A metal vessel in which, on both sides, there are two rings;
a similarly smaller vessel, with a compartment threaded on the rings— // VRrs_9.44 //
placing it upon the first vessel, in the small vessel one should put

children.text: rasaṃ saṃmūrchitaṃ sthūlapātram āpūrya kāñjikaiḥ // VRrs_9.45 //
children.translated_text: mercury with its fainting agent; filling the large vessel with sour gruel— // VRrs_9.45 //
one should steam for two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours) for the purpose of reviving mercury;
this is the <s>valabhīyantra</s> (gallery apparatus), which produces six-fold quality in mercury;
mercury in a fine magnetite vessel becomes of superior quality. // VRrs_9.46 //
One should place mercury in a tall pot equipped with a tube bent downward at the bottom;
that tube should be inserted into the belly of another pot. // VRrs_9.47 //
There, sealing properly with clay the mouths of both pots,
one should light a strong fire beneath the mercury pot. // VRrs_9.48 //
In the other pot, one should put cool, fresh water;
this is indeed called <s>tiryakpātana</s> (lateral distillation) by practitioners. // VRrs_9.49 //
A round iron cup with an upward rod at the front end—
this is the <s>pālikāyantra</s> (pan apparatus), for the purpose of digesting <s>bali</s> (an offering/substance). // VRrs_9.50 //
Holding four <s>prasthas</s> of water, with a mouth of four <s>aṅgulas</s>—

children.text: ghaṭayantram idaṃ proktaṃ tadāpyāyanakaṃ smṛtam // VRrs_9.51 //
children.translated_text: this is called the <s>ghaṭayantra</s> (pot apparatus), also known as <s>āpyāyana</s> (nourishing). // VRrs_9.51 //

children.text: vidhāya vartulaṃ gartaṃ mallamatra nidhāya ca /
children.translated_text: Making a round pit and placing a crucible therein,
and placing there a fine brick with a hole in its middle— // VRrs_9.52 //
around the pit, one should make a rim one <s>aṅgula</s> high;

children.text: garte sūtaṃ vinikṣipya gartāsye vasanaṃ kṣipet // VRrs_9.53 //
children.translated_text: casting mercury into the pit, one should place cloth over the pit's mouth. // VRrs_9.53 //
One should place sulphur therein, and seal the mouth with a crucible;

children.text: mallapālikayormadhye mṛdā samyaṅ nirudhya ca // VRrs_9.54 //
children.translated_text: between the crucible and the rim, one should properly seal with clay. // VRrs_9.54 //

children.text: vanopalaiḥ puṭaṃ deyaṃ kapotākhyaṃ na cādhikam /
children.translated_text: A <s>kapota</s> (dove-grade) <s>puṭa</s> should be given with forest stones, not more;

children.text: iṣṭikāyantram etat syād gandhakaṃ tena jārayet // VRrs_9.55 //
children.translated_text: this is the <s>iṣṭikāyantra</s> (brick apparatus)—by this one should digest sulphur. // VRrs_9.55 //

children.text: sthālikopari vinyasya sthālīṃ samyaṅ nirudhya ca /
children.translated_text: Placing one pot upon another and properly sealing,

children.text: ūrdhvasthālyāṃ jalaṃ kṣiptvā vahniṃ prajvālayed adhaḥ /
children.translated_text: putting water in the upper pot and lighting fire below—
this is the <s>vidyādhara yantra</s>, for the purpose of extracting <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar). // VRrs_9.56 //
Over the apparatus-pot, placing another pot inverted, one should seal it;
that apparatus called <s>ḍamaruka</s> (drum-shaped) is useful for making mercury ash. // VRrs_9.57 //
One should make a pit in the middle of a crucible, and place mercury with sulphur there;
around the pit, one should make a wall one <s>aṅgula</s> high. // VRrs_9.58 //
Then one should properly cover it with a cow-udder-shaped crucible;
properly sealing with water-clay as described— // VRrs_9.59 //
ground like a paste with <s>babbūla</s> (acacia) decoction,
fine powder of old iron-slag combined with jaggery powder—

children.text: iyaṃ hi jalamṛt proktā durbhedyā salilaiḥ khalu // VRrs_9.60 //
children.translated_text: this is indeed called <s>jalamṛt</s> (water-clay), which is certainly impervious to water. // VRrs_9.60 //
With chalk, alkali, and iron-slag, moistened with buffalo milk—
this becomes <s>vahnimṛtsnā</s> (fire-clay), which certainly withstands the heat of fierce fire. // VRrs_9.61 //

children.text: etayā mṛtsnayā ruddho na gantuṃ kṣamate rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sealed with this clay, mercury is unable to escape,
like a man restrained by the mature love of a clever woman. // VRrs_9.62 //
<s>Nandin</s>, <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, <s>Brahmajyoti</s>, and the lord of sages—
and <s>Somadeva</s> knows [this] — no other on the earth. // VRrs_9.63 //
Then, pouring in water, one should kindle fire below;
this <s>nābhiyantra</s> (navel apparatus) was proclaimed by <s>Nandin</s>, the all-knowing;

children.text: anena jīryate sūto nirdhūmaḥ śuddhagandhakaḥ // VRrs_9.64 //
children.translated_text: by this, mercury is digested, and sulphur is purified smokeless. // VRrs_9.64 //
A crucible placed inside the interior of another crucible, round at beginning and end,

children.text: cipiṭāṃ ca tale proktaṃ grastayantraṃ manīṣibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: and flat at the bottom — that is called the <s>grastayantra</s> (swallowed apparatus) by the wise;
it is described by mercury-experts for the purpose of cooking the lord of mercury. // VRrs_9.65 //

children.text: sthālyāṃ tāmrādi nikṣipya mallenāsya nirudhya ca /
children.translated_text: Placing copper etc. in a pot, sealing its [mouth] with a lid,

children.text: pacyate sthālikādhastāt sthālīyantram idaṃ smṛtam // VRrs_9.66 //
children.translated_text: it is cooked from below the pot — this is known as the <s>sthālīyantra</s> (pot apparatus). // VRrs_9.66 //
One should make an iron vessel of eight <s>aṅgulas</s> [diameter] and eight <s>aṅgulas</s> in height;

children.text: kaṇṭhādho hy aṅgule deśe galādhāre hi tatra ca // VRrs_9.67 //
children.translated_text: below the neck, at a distance of one <s>aṅgula</s>, at the throat-support, there — // VRrs_9.67 //
one should insert thin iron rods horizontally across;
upon those, one should place thin gold leaves. // VRrs_9.68 //
Below the leaves, one should place what will be described here;
one should cover that vessel with another inverted vessel. // VRrs_9.69 //

children.text: mṛdā vilipya saṃdhiṃ ca vahniṃ prajvālayed adhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having sealed the joint with clay, one should kindle fire below;

children.text: tena pattrāṇi kṛtsnāni hatāny uktavidhānataḥ // VRrs_9.70 //
children.translated_text: by this, all the leaves are killed according to the prescribed method. // VRrs_9.70 //

children.text: rasaścarati vegena drutaṃ garbhe dravanti ca /
children.translated_text: Mercury moves with speed, and the molten [substances] melt in the interior;

children.text: gandhālakaśilānāṃ hi kajjalyā vā mṛtāhinā // VRrs_9.71 //
children.translated_text: by the <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulphide) of sulphur, orpiment, and realgar, or with killed serpent [mineral] — // VRrs_9.71 //
the fumigation of gold leaves is first proclaimed;
for silver, one should fumigate silver leaves with killed tin. // VRrs_9.72 //
And one should fumigate with other sub-minerals as appropriate;
this <s>dhūpayantra</s> (fumigation apparatus) is proclaimed for preparing digestion substances. // VRrs_9.73 //

children.text: sthūlasthālyāṃ jalaṃ kṣiptvā vāso baddhvā muke dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: Placing water in a large pot, tying cloth firmly over the mouth,

children.text: tatra svedyaṃ vinikṣipya tanmukhaṃ prapidhāya ca // VRrs_9.74 //
children.translated_text: placing the substance to be steamed thereon, and covering its mouth — // VRrs_9.74 //
one should light fire below; that apparatus is called <s>kanduka</s> (ball apparatus);
other wise persons call this the <s>svedanīyantra</s> (steaming apparatus). // VRrs_9.75 //

children.text: yadvā sthālyāṃ jalaṃ kṣiptvā tṛṇaṃ kṣiptvā mukhopari /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, placing water in a pot and placing straw over the mouth,
placing the substance to be steamed around, and making a lid,

children.text: adhastājjvālayedagniṃ yantraṃ tat kandukaṃ smṛtam // VRrs_9.76 //
children.translated_text: one should light fire below — that apparatus is known as <s>kanduka</s>. // VRrs_9.76 //

children.text: khallayogyā śilā nīlā śyāmā snigdhā dṛḍhā guruḥ /
children.translated_text: The stone suitable for a mortar is blue-black, unctuous, hard, and heavy,
sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> in height and nine <s>aṅgulas</s> in width. // VRrs_9.77 //
Twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> long, the grinding stone twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>;
or twenty <s>aṅgulas</s> long and ten <s>aṅgulas</s> in height —
this should be known as the measure of a mortar (<s>khalla</s>), the best for mercurial operations. // VRrs_9.78 //

body.text: khallayantraṃ tridhā proktaṃ rasādisukhamardane // VRrs_9.79 //
body.translated_text: The <s>khallayantra</s> (mortar apparatus) is said to be of three kinds, for easy grinding of mercury etc. // VRrs_9.79 //

body.text: nirudgārau sumasṛṇau kāryau putrikayā yutau // VRrs_9.80 //
body.translated_text: They should be made without projections, very smooth, and equipped with a rim (<s>putrikā</s>). // VRrs_9.80 //

children.text: utsedhe sa daśāṅgulaḥ khalu kalātulyāṅgulāyāmavān vistāreṇa daśāṅgulo munimitairnimnas tayaivāṅgulaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Ten <s>aṅgulas</s> in height, with a length equal to an <s>aṅgula</s> of the digit measurement, ten <s>aṅgulas</s> in width as determined by sages, with a depth of the same <s>aṅgulas</s>;

children.text: pālyāṃ dvyaṅgulivistaraśca masṛṇo 'tīvārdhacandropamo gharṣo dvādaśakāṅgulaśca tadayaṃ khallo mataḥ siddhaye // VRrs_9.81 //
children.translated_text: the rim two <s>aṅgulas</s> wide, very smooth, shaped like a half-moon; the grinding stone twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> — this mortar is considered [best] for perfection. // VRrs_9.81 //
In this [mortar], five <s>palas</s> of mercury should be ground for purification;
according to the suitability of each [procedure], one should employ the other mortars. // VRrs_9.82 //
A mortar twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> in width, of very smooth stone,
four <s>aṅgulas</s> deep, and very smoothly polished in the middle — // VRrs_9.83 //
the grinding stone flat on the bottom, easy to grasp at the top;

children.text: ayaṃ tu vartulaḥ khallo mardane 'tisukhapradaḥ // VRrs_9.84 //
children.translated_text: this round mortar is extremely comfortable for grinding. // VRrs_9.84 //

children.text: lauho navāṅgulaḥ khallo nimnatve ca ṣaḍaṅgulaḥ /
children.translated_text: An iron mortar of nine <s>aṅgulas</s>, six <s>aṅgulas</s> in depth,
with a grinding stone of eight <s>aṅgulas</s> — this is also called the <s>taptakhalla</s> (heated mortar). // VRrs_9.85 //
Having made a firepit in the shape of a mortar, filled with charcoal,

children.text: tasyāṃ niveśya taṃ khallaṃ pārśve bhastrikayā dhamet // VRrs_9.86 //
children.translated_text: placing the mortar therein, one should blow from the side with a bellows. // VRrs_9.86 //
The amalgam ground within, combined with alkalis and acids,
melts with great speed when steamed — there is no doubt;

children.text: kṛtaḥ kāntāyasā so 'yaṃ bhavet koṭiguṇo rasaḥ // VRrs_9.87 //
children.translated_text: made of magnetite iron, this mercury becomes of ten-million-fold quality. // VRrs_9.87 //

children.text: mūṣā hi krauñcikā proktā kumudī karahāṭikā /
children.translated_text: Crucibles (<s>mūṣā</s>) are indeed called <s>krauñcikā</s>, <s>kumudī</s>, <s>karahāṭikā</s>,
<s>pācanī</s>, and <s>vahnimitrā</s> — thus named by mercury practitioners. // VRrs_10.1 //

body.text: muṣṇāti doṣān mūṣā yā sā mūṣeti nigadyate // VRrs_10.2 //
body.translated_text: That which steals away (<s>muṣṇāti</s>) defects is called <s>mūṣā</s> (crucible). // VRrs_10.2 //

body.text: upādānaṃ bhavettasyā mṛttikā lohameva ca // VRrs_10.3 //
body.translated_text: Its material components are clay and metal. // VRrs_10.3 //

children.translated_text: Better is even a single <s>kākiṇī</s> (small coin) that has come from the mouth of a crucible
than a hundred thousand [coins] from bowing to wicked people — so the self-respecting declare. // VRrs_10.4 //
The binding of the crucible and its lid — the joining, the sealing of joints,

children.text: andhraṇaṃ randhraṇaṃ caiva saṃśliṣṭaṃ saṃdhibandhanam // VRrs_10.5 //
children.translated_text: the blinding [of holes], the making of holes, and the close-fitting joint-binding — // VRrs_10.5 //
Clay that is pale, coarse, sandy, reddish-pale,
that withstands prolonged blowing — it is highly praised for crucible-making;

children.text: tadabhāve ca vālmīkī kaulālī vā samīryate // VRrs_10.6 //
children.translated_text: in its absence, anthill clay or potter's clay is prescribed. // VRrs_10.6 //

children.text: yā mṛttikā dugdhatuṣaiḥ śaṇena śikhitrakair vā hayaladdinā ca /
children.translated_text: Clay that is beaten with dried-milk husks, hemp, peacock feathers, or horse-dung,

children.text: lauhena daṇḍena ca kuṭṭitā sā sādhāraṇā syāt khalu mūṣikārthe // VRrs_10.7 //
children.translated_text: and with an iron rod — that is suitable for general crucible purposes. // VRrs_10.7 //
White stones, burnt husks, peacock feathers, hemp, <s>kharpara</s> (zinc oxide),

children.text: laddiḥ kiṭṭaṃ kṛṣṇamṛtsnā saṃyojyā mūṣikāmṛdi // VRrs_10.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>laddi</s> (a mineral), iron slag, and black earth — these should be combined in the crucible clay. // VRrs_10.8 //
Three parts clay, one part each of hemp and <s>laddi</s>, one part of burnt husk and stone,

children.text: kiṭṭārdhabhāgaṃ parikhaṇḍya vajramūṣāṃ vidadhyātkhalu sattvapāte // VRrs_10.9 //
children.translated_text: half a part of iron slag — having cut [and mixed], one should make the <s>vajramūṣā</s> (diamond crucible) for essence-extraction. // VRrs_10.9 //
Earth with burnt charcoal husks, anthill clay,
combined with the respective <s>viḍa</s> (digestive agents) and coated with the respective <s>viḍas</s> — // VRrs_10.10 //

children.text: tayā yā vihitā mūṣā yogamūṣeti kathyate /
children.translated_text: a crucible made with that is called <s>yogamūṣā</s> (preparation crucible);

children.text: anayā sādhitaḥ sūto jāyate guṇavattaraḥ // VRrs_10.11 //
children.translated_text: mercury processed with this becomes of superior quality. // VRrs_10.11 //
With fire-stone, <s>bhūnāga</s> (earth-serpent mineral), and washed [residue], hemp, and burnt husks —

children.text: samaiḥ samā ca mūṣā mṛnmahiṣīdugdhamarditā // VRrs_10.12 //
children.translated_text: equal parts, the crucible clay ground with buffalo milk. // VRrs_10.12 //
<s>Krauñcikā</s> (crane-shaped) is but the measure of the apparatus, described in many ways;
a crucible made with that is suitable for melting diamond. // VRrs_10.13 //
With milk in sixfold quantity, fire-stone in eightfold, iron slag, charcoal, and hemp —
a crucible made with black earth is called <s>gāramūṣā</s> (fire-stone crucible);
it does not melt by fire even after blowing for two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours). // VRrs_10.14 //
Diamond, charcoal, and husks in equal parts, with four times that amount of clay,

children.text: gārā ca mṛttikātulyā sarvair etair vinirmitā /
children.translated_text: and fire-stone equal to the clay — made from all these,

children.text: varamūṣeti nirdiṣṭā yāmamagniṃ saheta sā // VRrs_10.15 //
children.translated_text: it is designated as <s>varamūṣā</s> (excellent crucible); it can withstand fire for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours). // VRrs_10.15 //
Free from stones, red, processed with the group of red substances,
a crucible prepared from [such] clay, coated with <s>kṣitikhecara</s> (a mineral) —

children.text: varṇamūṣeti sā proktā varṇotkarṣe niyujyate // VRrs_10.16 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>varṇamūṣā</s> (color crucible); it is employed for enhancing color. // VRrs_10.16 //
Free from stones, white, processed with the group of white substances,
a crucible prepared from [such] clay, coated with <s>kṣitikhecara</s> —

children.text: raupyamūṣeti sā proktā varṇotkarṣe niyujyate // VRrs_10.17 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>raupyamūṣā</s> (silver crucible); it is employed for enhancing color. // VRrs_10.17 //
Made from clay of the respective varieties, coated with the respective <s>viḍas</s>,
for the purpose of body-metal preparations — that is called <s>viḍamūṣā</s> (viḍa-crucible). // VRrs_10.18 //
With fire-stone, <s>bhūnāga</s>, and washed [residue], hemp, and burnt husks —

children.text: samaiḥ samā ca mūṣā mṛnmahiṣīdugdhamarditā // VRrs_10.19 //
children.translated_text: equal parts, the crucible clay ground with buffalo milk. // VRrs_10.19 //
<s>Krauñcikā</s> is indeed described in many ways as the measure of the apparatus;

children.text: tayā viracitā mūṣā liptā matkuṇaśoṇitaiḥ // VRrs_10.20 //
children.translated_text: a crucible made with that, coated with bedbug blood, // VRrs_10.20 //
and with <s>bālā</s>, <s>abdadhvani</s> roots — [this is] the <s>vajradrāvaṇa-krauñcikā</s> (diamond-melting crane crucible);

children.text: sahate 'gniṃ caturyāmaṃ draveṇa vyādhitā satī // VRrs_10.21 //
children.translated_text: it withstands fire for four <s>yāmas</s> (twelve hours) even when afflicted by molten [metal]. // VRrs_10.21 //
When the molten metal is about to liquefy from the crucible through blowing,
the momentary lifting [of the crucible] — that is called <s>mūṣāpyāyana</s> (crucible-nourishing). // VRrs_10.22 //
In an eggplant-shaped crucible, a tube of twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>,
like a <s>dhattūra</s> flower above, firmly attached like a flower-bud — // VRrs_10.23 //

children.text: aṣṭāṅgulaṃ ca sacchidraṃ sā syād vṛntākamūṣikā /
children.translated_text: eight <s>aṅgulas</s> with a hole — that is the <s>vṛntākamūṣikā</s> (eggplant crucible);
with this, one should extract the essence from <s>kharpara</s> (zinc oxide) and other soft [minerals]. // VRrs_10.24 //
A crucible shaped like a cow's udder, with a crest-equipped lid —

children.text: sattvānāṃ drāvaṇe śuddhau mūṣā sā gostanī bhavet // VRrs_10.25 //
children.translated_text: that becomes the <s>gostanī mūṣā</s> (cow-udder crucible), for melting and purifying essences. // VRrs_10.25 //
The <s>mallamūṣā</s> (wrestling crucible) is described as consisting of a pair of cup-shaped crucibles;
it is proclaimed for steaming <s>parpaṭī</s> and other mercurial preparations. // VRrs_10.26 //
That which is in the form of a potter's vessel, strong and well-fired —
that is called <s>pakvamūṣā</s> (fired crucible), for the cooking of <s>poṭalī</s> (pouches) and the like. // VRrs_10.27 //
Spherical in shape without an opening, containing the calcination substance in its interior —
that is called <s>golamūṣā</s> (spherical crucible), which quickly retains the melting [substance]. // VRrs_10.28 //
That which is elbow-shaped at the bottom, gradually widening upward,
thick like a large eggplant — that is known as <s>mahāmūṣā</s> (great crucible);

children.text: sā cāyo 'bhrakasattvādeḥ puṭāya drāvaṇāya ca // VRrs_10.29 //
children.translated_text: it is for the calcination and melting of iron, mica-essence, and the like. // VRrs_10.29 //
That which is frog-shaped, low in length and width,
of six <s>aṅgulas</s> measure — the crucible called <s>maṇḍūka</s> (frog crucible);

children.text: bhūmau nikhanya tāṃ mūṣāṃ dadyātpuṭamathopari // VRrs_10.30 //
children.translated_text: burying that crucible in the ground, one should give calcination fire above. // VRrs_10.30 //
A crucible that is flat at the base, round, and eight <s>aṅgulas</s> in height —

children.text: mūṣā sā mūsalākhyā syāccakribaddharase hitā // VRrs_10.31 //
children.translated_text: that crucible is called <s>mūsala</s> (pestle-shaped); it is useful for mercury bound in circular form. // VRrs_10.31 //
For the purpose of precipitating essences, and for the purification of precipitated [essences] —
furnaces (<s>koṣṭhikā</s>) of various shapes; their characteristics are now described. // VRrs_10.32 //
One royal cubit in height, half that in length and width,

children.text: caturasrā ca kuḍyena veṣṭitā mṛnmayena ca // VRrs_10.33 //
children.translated_text: square and enclosed with an earthen wall — // VRrs_10.33 //
in one wall there should be a doorway of one span's width;

children.text: dvāraṃ sārdhavitastyā ca saṃmitaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ śubham // VRrs_10.34 //
children.translated_text: the door should measure one and a half spans, firm and well-made. // VRrs_10.34 //
Below the threshold, provision should be made for the bellows as appropriate;
a wall of one span measure above the upper grate — // VRrs_10.35 //
and a doorway of one span measure should be made above;

children.text: tataśceṣṭikayā ruddhvā dvārasaṃdhiṃ vilipya ca // VRrs_10.36 //
children.translated_text: then, blocking with bricks and sealing the door-joints — // VRrs_10.36 //
filling it with charcoal, one should blow with a pair of bellows;
one should cast the charcoal and blowing material through the upper door. // VRrs_10.37 //
The essence-precipitating globules, five at a time, again and again —
this becomes the <s>aṅgārakoṣṭhī</s> (charcoal furnace), which precipitates the essence of hard [minerals]. // VRrs_10.38 //
In firm ground, one should make a round pit of one span's measure,

children.text: vartulaṃ cātha tanmadhye gartamanyaṃ prakalpayet // VRrs_10.39 //
children.translated_text: and then in the middle, one should fashion another pit — // VRrs_10.39 //
four <s>aṅgulas</s> in width and depth,
with a horizontal tube extending from the pit to the ground surface. // VRrs_10.40 //
Slightly raised, sloping downward toward the outer pit;
one should place a clay disc with five holes in the interior of the inner pit. // VRrs_10.41 //
Filling the furnace with charcoal, one should blow with a single bellows;
this is the <s>pātālakoṣṭhikā</s> (underground furnace), which precipitates the essence of soft [minerals];
it was proclaimed by <s>Nandin</s> for substances that require blowing. // VRrs_10.42 //
That which is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> deep and one span in measure,
with a ring four <s>aṅgulas</s> above — // VRrs_10.43 //
one should place a disc with many holes upon the ring;
placing charcoal therein, one should blow through a tube;
this is called the <s>gārakoṣṭhī</s> (fire-stone furnace), which destroys impure metals. // VRrs_10.44 //
One should make [a furnace] from crucible-clay, one cubit in measure, firm,

children.text: adhomukhaṃ ca tadvaktre nālaṃ pañcāṅgulaṃ khalu /
children.translated_text: inverted, with a tube of five <s>aṅgulas</s> at its mouth —

children.text: vaṅkanālam idaṃ proktaṃ dṛḍhadhmānāya kīrtitam // VRrs_10.45 //
children.translated_text: This is called the bellows-tube (<s>vaṅkanāla</s>), declared for strong blowing. // VRrs_10.45 //
The furnace (<s>koṣṭhī</s>) is prescribed for the preparation of perfected mercury and the like.
It should be twelve <s>aṅgula</s>s (finger-breadths) in height, four <s>aṅgula</s>s at the base,
with a lateral blowing aperture, and suited for purifying soft substances. // VRrs_10.46 //
<s>Puṭa</s> (calcination) is the means of knowing the proper measure of cooking for mercury and other substances.

children.text: neṣṭo nyūnādhikaḥ pākaḥ supākaṃ hitam auṣadham // VRrs_10.47 //
children.translated_text: Cooking that is deficient or excessive is undesirable; a well-cooked medicine is beneficial. // VRrs_10.47 //
Through <s>puṭa</s>, metals attain irreversibility, increase of qualities, and hence superiority;

children.text: anapsu majjanaṃ rekhāpūrṇatā puṭato bhavet // VRrs_10.48 //
children.translated_text: non-sinking in water and fullness of lustre result from <s>puṭa</s>. // VRrs_10.48 //

children.text: puṭād grāvṇo laghutvaṃ ca śīghravyāptiśca dīpanam /
children.translated_text: Through <s>puṭa</s>, stones become light, and there is rapid pervasion and stimulation (of digestive fire);
the quality of metals (treated by puṭa) is superior even to that (achieved by) the lord of mercury through digestion. // VRrs_10.49 //
Just as fire enters a stone through the application of external <s>puṭa</s>,
so too, through being powdered, the acquisition of qualities is certain in metals. // VRrs_10.50 //
In a pit two <s>hasta</s>s (cubits) square, with depth and width,
filled with a thousand cow-dung cakes (<s>vanopala</s>) — the medicine to be calcined, // VRrs_10.51 //
sealed in a crucible (<s>krauñcī</s>) with care, should be placed on top of the cake-bed.
Half a thousand cow-dung cakes should be arranged on top of the crucible.
One should light fire there — this is known as <s>Mahāpuṭa</s> (great calcination). // VRrs_10.52 //
A square pit, measured by the king's hand-span, depressed,
filled with cow-dung cakes (<s>upalasāṭhī</s>) up to the neck-level — then one should place // VRrs_10.53 //
the <s>kumudī</s> (crucible) there, filled with the substance to be calcined.
One should cast half as many cow-dung cakes as fill (the pit) on top.
This is called the <s>Gajapuṭa</s> (elephant calcination), which produces great qualities. // VRrs_10.54 //

body.text: itthaṃ cāratnike kuṇḍe puṭaṃ vārāhamucyate // VRrs_10.55 //
body.translated_text: Likewise, in a pit of one <s>aratni</s> (cubit), the <s>puṭa</s> is called <s>Vārāha</s> (boar calcination). // VRrs_10.55 //

children.translated_text: A <s>puṭa</s> on the ground surface, two <s>vitasti</s>s (spans) in height
and equally wide at the base — that is the <s>Kukkuṭaka puṭa</s> (hen calcination). // VRrs_10.56 //
The <s>puṭa</s> that is given on the ground with eight cow-dung cakes,
sealed, for the purpose of making mercury or <s>Arka</s> (Calotropis) ash — that is called <s>Kapota puṭa</s> (dove calcination). // VRrs_10.57 //
Dried, powdered cow-dung from inside a cow-pen where cows have trodden —
that is declared as <s>Govara</s> (cow-dung fuel), the best in mercury processing. // VRrs_10.58 //
The <s>puṭa</s> where either <s>Govara</s> or husks are used
is called <s>Govarapuṭa</s>, for the perfection of mercury ash. // VRrs_10.59 //
In a large pot filled with husks, with a crucible placed in the middle,
cooking done with fire — that is called <s>Bhāṇḍapuṭa</s> (pot calcination). // VRrs_10.60 //
The crucible is covered below and above
with heated sand — wherever that is done, that is <s>Vālukāpuṭa</s> (sand-bath calcination). // VRrs_10.61 //
One should bury the friend of fire (the crucible) properly in the ground, two <s>aṅgula</s>s deep;

children.text: upariṣṭātpuṭaṃ yatra puṭaṃ tad bhūdharāhvayam // VRrs_10.62 //
children.translated_text: where the <s>puṭa</s> (is applied) from above — that <s>puṭa</s> is called <s>Bhūdhara</s> (earth-bearer). // VRrs_10.62 //
A <s>puṭa</s> from above using sixteen (cow-dung cakes or their equivalent in) cow urine, or husks, or cow-dung —
that is called <s>Lāvaka</s> (quail calcination), for processing very soft substances. // VRrs_10.63 //
When the measure of <s>puṭa</s> is not specified, based on the strength or weakness of the substance to be processed,
the <s>puṭa</s> should be determined and applied by those skilled in reasoning and counter-reasoning. // VRrs_10.64 //

children.text: piṣṭakaṃ chagaṇaṃ chāṇam utpalaṃ copalaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Piṣṭaka</s>, <s>Chagaṇa</s>, <s>Chāṇa</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, and <s>Upala</s> likewise,
<s>Giriṇḍa</s>, <s>Upala</s>, <s>Sāṭhī</s>, and <s>Varāṭī</s> — these are synonyms for cow-dung cakes. // VRrs_10.65 //

children.text: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ trapu sīsakam āyasam /
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, tin, lead, and iron —

children.text: ṣaḍetāni ca lohāni kṛtrimau kāṃsyapittalau // VRrs_10.66 //
children.translated_text: these are the six metals; and the two artificial ones are bell-metal (<s>kāṃsya</s>) and brass (<s>pittala</s>). // VRrs_10.66 //

children.text: lavaṇāni ṣaḍ ucyante sāmudraṃ saindhavaṃ viḍam /
children.translated_text: Six salts are enumerated: sea salt (<s>sāmudra</s>), rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), <s>viḍa</s> salt,

children.text: sauvarcalaṃ romakaṃ ca cūllikālavaṇaṃ tathā // VRrs_10.67 //
children.translated_text: <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt), <s>romaka</s> salt, and <s>cūllikā</s> salt. // VRrs_10.67 //

body.text: kṣāratrayaṃ samākhyātaṃ yavasarjikaṭaṅkaṇam // VRrs_10.68 //
body.translated_text: The triad of alkalies is declared to be: <s>yavakṣāra</s> (barley alkali), <s>sarjikā</s> (sodium carbonate), and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>). // VRrs_10.68 //

children.translated_text: The alkalies of <s>Palāśa</s> (Butea) and <s>Muṣkaka</s>, barley alkali, <s>Suvarcikā</s>,
and the alkali derived from sesame stems — these five together constitute the <s>kṣārapañcaka</s> (five alkalies). // VRrs_10.69 //

body.text: ghṛtaṃ guḍo mākṣikaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ madhuratrayam // VRrs_10.70 //
body.translated_text: Ghee, jaggery, and honey — these should be known as the sweet triad (<s>madhuratrayam</s>). // VRrs_10.70 //

children.translated_text: <s>Kaṅguṇī</s>, <s>Tumbinī</s>, <s>Ghoṣā</s>, (oil) derived from <s>Karīra</s> and <s>Śrīphala</s> (wood-apple),
pungent nightshade (<s>Kaṭuvārttāka</s>), mustard (<s>Siddhārtha</s>), <s>Somarājī</s>, and that derived from <s>Vibhītaka</s>, // VRrs_10.71 //
that derived from linseed (<s>Atasī</s>), <s>Mahākālī</s>, neem (<s>Nimba</s>), and sesame (<s>Tila</s>),
from <s>Apāmārga</s>, <s>Devadālī</s>, <s>Dantī</s>, <s>Tumburu</s>, and <s>Vigraha</s>, // VRrs_10.72 //
from <s>Aṅkola</s>, <s>Unmatta</s> (Datura), <s>Bhallātaka</s> (marking nut), and <s>Palāśa</s> (Butea) likewise —
extracting oil from these, one should employ them in mercury operations. // VRrs_10.73 //
Fat (<s>vasā</s>) of the jackal (<s>jambūka</s>), frog (<s>maṇḍūka</s>), and that derived from the tortoise (<s>kacchapa</s>),
of the crab (<s>karkaṭī</s>), crocodile (<s>śiśumārī</s>), cow, pig (<s>śūkara</s>), and human,
of goat, camel, donkey, ram, and buffalo likewise — // VRrs_10.74 //
Urines of elephant, young elephant, she-buffalo, donkey, and horse,

children.text: go 'jāvīnāṃ striyaḥ puṃsāṃ puṣpaṃ bījaṃ tu yojayet // VRrs_10.75 //
children.translated_text: of cow, she-goat, and ewe; menstrual blood (<s>puṣpa</s>) and semen (<s>bīja</s>) of women and men should be employed. // VRrs_10.75 //
Buffalo water (urine), curd, milk, ghee, and cow-dung juice —
these are known as the five buffalo products (<s>pañcamāhiṣa</s>); likewise the five goat products. // VRrs_10.76 //
<s>Amlavetasa</s> (tamarind), <s>Jambīra</s> (citron), <s>Nimbuka</s> (lime), <s>Bījapūraka</s> (citrus),

children.text: cāṅgerī caṇakāmlaṃ ca amlīkaṃ koladāḍimam // VRrs_10.77 //
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṅgerī</s> (wood-sorrel), sour chickpea water (<s>caṇakāmla</s>), tamarind (<s>Amlīka</s>), jujube (<s>Kola</s>), and pomegranate (<s>Dāḍima</s>), // VRrs_10.77 //
<s>Ambaṣṭhā</s>, <s>Tintiḍīka</s> (tamarind), dried ginger (<s>Nāgara</s>), <s>Rasapattrikā</s>,
and <s>Karavanda</s>, and whatever else — this is declared as the sour group (<s>amlavarga</s>). // VRrs_10.78 //
Among all of them, sour chickpea water alone is commended.
Or <s>Amlavetasa</s> alone is the best of the best of all,

children.text: rasādīnāṃ viśuddhyarthaṃ drāvaṇe jāraṇe hitam // VRrs_10.79 //
children.translated_text: for the purification of mercury and the like, beneficial for dissolution and digestion. // VRrs_10.79 //
The juices of jujube, pomegranate, <s>Vṛkṣāmla</s> (kokum), <s>Cullikā</s>, and vinegar (<s>Cukrikā</s>) —
these are designated as the five sour substances (<s>pañcāmlaka</s>), also called <s>āmlapañcaka</s>. // VRrs_10.80 //
Brick, red ochre, salt, ash, and anthill clay —
these are declared by those skilled in mercury practice as the five clays (<s>pañcamṛttikā</s>). // VRrs_10.81 //
<s>Śṛṅgīka</s> (horn-poison), <s>Kālakūṭa</s>, <s>Vatsanābha</s> (aconite), with <s>Kṛtrima</s> (artificial poison),

children.text: pittaṃ ca viṣavargo 'yaṃ sa varaḥ parikīrtitaḥ // VRrs_10.82 //
children.translated_text: and bile (<s>pitta</s>) — this is the poison group (<s>viṣavarga</s>), declared to be excellent. // VRrs_10.82 //
This (group) is commended in mercury operations and in the procedure of piercing (metals) as well;
but if used improperly, it certainly kills. // VRrs_10.83 //
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>Viṣamuṣṭi</s>, <s>Karavīra</s> (oleander), <s>Jayā</s> (hemp),

children.text: nīlakaḥ kanako 'rkaśca vargo hy upaviṣātmakaḥ // VRrs_10.84 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nīlaka</s>, <s>Kanaka</s>, and <s>Arka</s> (Calotropis) — this is the sub-poison group (<s>upaviṣavarga</s>). // VRrs_10.84 //
(Milk of) she-elephant, horse-mare, woman, cow, she-donkey, she-goat, and ewe,
she-camel, <s>Udumbara</s> (fig), <s>Aśvattha</s> (peepal), <s>Bhānu</s> (Calotropis), banyan (<s>Nyagrodha</s>), and <s>Tilvaka</s>, // VRrs_10.85 //
<s>Dugdhikā</s> (milkweed), <s>Snuk</s> (Euphorbia), and likewise <s>Uttamakaṇṭikā</s> —

children.text: eṣāṃ dugdhair vinirdiṣṭo dugdhavargo rasādiṣu // VRrs_10.86 //
children.translated_text: the milk group (<s>dugdhavarga</s>) prescribed for mercury and the like is composed of their milks. // VRrs_10.86 //
Of the pigeon (<s>pārāvata</s>), the blue jay (<s>cāṣa</s>), the dove (<s>kapota</s>), the peacock (<s>kalāpin</s>),
the vulture (<s>gṛdhra</s>), and the hen (<s>kukkuṭa</s>) — their droppings (<s>viṃgaṇa</s>) are prescribed.
The purification of all metals is indeed through <s>puṭa</s> and smearing. // VRrs_10.87 //
Safflower (<s>Kusumbha</s>), <s>Khadira</s> (Acacia catechu), lac (<s>Lākṣā</s>), <s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> (Indian madder), red sandalwood (<s>Raktacandana</s>),
<s>Akṣī</s>, <s>Bandhujīva</s> (Pentapetes), and <s>Karpūragandhinī</s>,
and <s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrite) — this should be known as the red group (<s>raktavarga</s>), for deep coloring. // VRrs_10.88 //
<s>Kiṃśuka</s> (Butea flowers), <s>Karṇikāra</s>, and the two turmerics (<s>Haridrā</s>) —
this is prescribed as the yellow group (<s>pītavarga</s>) for operations with the king of mercury. // VRrs_10.89 //

children.text: tagaraḥ kuṭajaḥ kundo guñjā jīvantikā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Tagara</s>, <s>Kuṭaja</s>, <s>Kunda</s> (jasmine), <s>Guñjā</s>, <s>Jīvantikā</s>,
and the root of white lotus — this is called the white group (<s>śvetavarga</s>). // VRrs_10.90 //

children.text: kadalī kāravellī ca triphalā nīlikā nalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Plantain (<s>Kadalī</s>), <s>Kāravellī</s> (bitter gourd), <s>Triphala</s>, indigo (<s>Nīlikā</s>), reed (<s>Nala</s>),
mud (<s>Paṅka</s>), green vitriol (<s>Kāsīsa</s>), and unripe mango (<s>Bālāmra</s>) — this is called the black group (<s>kṛṣṇavarga</s>). // VRrs_10.91 //
The substance that serves as a digesting agent, treated with the red and other groups,
should be carefully impregnated to achieve the corresponding color. // VRrs_10.92 //

body.text: kācaṭaṅkaṇakṣiprābhiḥ śodhanīyo gaṇo mataḥ // VRrs_10.93 //
body.translated_text: Glass (<s>kāca</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), and <s>kṣiprā</s> — these constitute the purifying group (<s>śodhanīya gaṇa</s>). // VRrs_10.93 //

children.translated_text: It destroys the impurities of metallic essences (<s>sattva</s>), bound mercury (<s>baddhasūta</s>), and metals;
practitioners of mercury science say it destroys <s>Kāpālī</s> and <s>Kaṅguṇa</s> (impurities). // VRrs_10.94 //
<s>Mahiṣī</s> (buffalo milk), <s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>Kaliṅga</s>, combined with <s>Dhava</s> seeds,
and hare's bones — this formula destroys the hardness of metals. // VRrs_10.95 //
With jaggery, <s>Guggulu</s> (bdellium), <s>Guñjā</s> (Abrus), ghee, <s>Sāra</s>, and <s>Ghaiṣa</s>, combined with borax —
this group is regarded as (suitable) for melting all metals and the like that are hard to melt. // VRrs_10.96 //
All alkalies destroy impurities; sour substances (serve for) purification and digestion;

children.text: māndyaṃ viṣāṇi nighnanti snaigdhyaṃ snehāḥ prakurvate // VRrs_10.97 //
children.translated_text: poisons destroy sluggishness; and oily substances produce unctuousness. // VRrs_10.97 //

children.text: ṣaṭ truṭyaś caikalikṣā syāt ṣaḍ likṣā yūkam ucyate /
children.translated_text: Six <s>truṭi</s>s make one <s>likṣā</s>; six <s>likṣā</s>s are called one <s>yūka</s>;

children.text: ṣaḍyūkāstu rajaḥsaṃjñaṃ kathitaṃ tava suvrate // VRrs_11.1 //
children.translated_text: six <s>yūka</s>s are termed <s>rajas</s> — thus it is told to you, O virtuous one. // VRrs_11.1 //

children.text: ṣaḍrajaḥ sarṣapaḥ sākṣātsiddhārthaḥ sa ca kīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Six <s>rajas</s> make one <s>sarṣapa</s> (mustard seed), which is also called <s>siddhārtha</s>;
by six <s>siddhārtha</s>s, O goddess, one <s>yava</s> (barley grain) is declared. // VRrs_11.2 //
Six <s>yava</s>s make one <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seed); three <s>guñjā</s>s are called one <s>valla</s>.
By six <s>guñjā</s>s indeed, one <s>māṣa</s> is declared.

children.text: māṣā dvādaśa tolaḥ syādaṣṭau tolāḥ palaṃ bhavet // VRrs_11.3 //
children.translated_text: Twelve <s>māṣa</s>s make one <s>tola</s>; eight <s>tola</s>s make one <s>pala</s>. // VRrs_11.3 //
A <s>truṭi</s> consists of six <s>aṇu</s>s (atoms); by six of those, a <s>likṣā</s> is declared;

children.text: tābhiḥ ṣaḍbhirbhaved yūkā ṣaḍyūkās tad rajaḥ smṛtam // VRrs_11.4 //
children.translated_text: by six of those, a <s>yūka</s> is formed; six <s>yūka</s>s are known as one <s>rajas</s>. // VRrs_11.4 //
Six <s>rajas</s> are declared as one <s>sarṣapa</s>; by six of those, a <s>yava</s> is stated.

children.text: ekā guñjā yavaiḥ ṣaḍbhirniṣpāvastu dviguñjakaḥ // VRrs_11.5 //
children.translated_text: One <s>guñjā</s> equals six <s>yava</s>s; a <s>niṣpāva</s> (flat bean) equals two <s>guñjā</s>s. // VRrs_11.5 //

children.text: syādguñjātritayaṃ vallo dvau vallau māṣa ucyate /
