children.translated_text: Three <s>guñjā</s>s make one <s>valla</s>; two <s>valla</s>s are called one <s>māṣa</s>.

children.text: dvau māṣau dharaṇaṃ te dve śāṇaniṣkakalāḥ smṛtāḥ // VRrs_11.6 //
children.translated_text: Two <s>māṣa</s>s make one <s>dharaṇa</s>; two of those are known as <s>śāṇa</s>, <s>niṣka</s>, and <s>kalā</s>. // VRrs_11.6 //

children.text: niṣkadvayaṃ tu vaṭakaḥ sa ca kola itīritaḥ /
children.translated_text: Two <s>niṣka</s>s make one <s>vaṭaka</s>; that is also called <s>kola</s> (jujube).
Three <s>kola</s>s make one <s>tola</s>; a <s>karṣa</s> equals four <s>niṣka</s>s. // VRrs_11.7 //
<s>Udumbara</s> (fig), <s>pāṇitala</s> (palm), <s>suvarṇa</s> (gold), and <s>kavalagraha</s> (a mouthful) —
<s>akṣa</s>, <s>biḍālapadaka</s> (cat's paw), and <s>śukti</s> (shell) equal two <s>pāṇitala</s>s. // VRrs_11.8 //
Two <s>śukti</s>s make one <s>pala</s> according to some; others know it as three <s>śukti</s>s.

children.text: tadeva kathitaṃ muṣṭiḥ prakuñco bilvamityapi // VRrs_11.9 //
children.translated_text: That same is called <s>muṣṭi</s> (fistful), <s>prakuñca</s>, and <s>bilva</s> (bael fruit) as well. // VRrs_11.9 //
Two <s>pala</s>s make one <s>prasṛta</s>; two of those make one <s>kuḍava</s> (or <s>añjali</s>, a double-handful).

children.text: kuḍavau mānikā tau syātprastho dve mānike smṛtaḥ // VRrs_11.10 //
children.translated_text: Two <s>kuḍava</s>s make one <s>mānikā</s>; two <s>mānikā</s>s are known as one <s>prastha</s>. // VRrs_11.10 //

children.text: prasthadvayaṃ śubhaṃ tau dvau pātrakaṃ dvayamāḍhakam /
children.translated_text: Two <s>prastha</s>s make one <s>śubha</s>; two of those make a <s>pātraka</s>; two (pātrakas) make one <s>āḍhaka</s>.
By four of those, one <s>ghaṭa</s> (pot measure); <s>nalva</s>, <s>nārmaṇa</s>, and <s>śūrpaka</s> // VRrs_11.11 //

children.text: droṇasya śabdāḥ paryāyāḥ palānāṃ śatakaṃ tulā /
children.translated_text: are synonyms of <s>droṇa</s>; one hundred <s>pala</s>s make one <s>tulā</s> (balance).
A <s>tulā</s> of forty hundred (four thousand) <s>pala</s>s is declared to be one <s>bhāra</s> (load). // VRrs_11.12 //
Having examined treatises such as the <s>Rasārṇava</s> and the like, I have stated (this);

children.text: rasopayogi yat kiṃcid diṅmātraṃ tatpradarśitam // VRrs_11.13 //
children.translated_text: whatever is useful for mercury — just a general indication of that has been shown. // VRrs_11.13 //

body.text: adhunā rasarājasya saṃskārān sampracakṣmahe // VRrs_11.14 //
body.translated_text: Now we shall describe the <s>saṃskāra</s>s (purificatory procedures) of the king of mercury. // VRrs_11.14 //

children.text: syātsvedanaṃ tadanu mardanamūrchane ca utthāpanaṃ patanarodhaniyāmanāni /
children.translated_text: There are: steaming (<s>svedana</s>), then grinding (<s>mardana</s>), fainting (<s>mūrchana</s>), reviving (<s>utthāpana</s>), precipitation (<s>patana</s>), restraining (<s>rodhana</s>), and binding (<s>niyamana</s>),

children.text: saṃdīpanaṃ gaganabhakṣaṇamānamatra saṃcāraṇā tadanu garbhagatā drutiśca // VRrs_11.15 //
children.translated_text: stimulating (<s>saṃdīpana</s>), sky-devouring (<s>gaganabhakṣaṇa</s>), and consumption (<s>ānama</s>) herein; then circulation (<s>saṃcāraṇa</s>), then entering the womb (<s>garbhagatā</s>), and internal fluidity (<s>druti</s>). // VRrs_11.15 //

children.text: bāhyā drutiḥ sūtakajāraṇā syād grāsastathā sāraṇakarma paścāt /
children.translated_text: External fluidity (<s>bāhyā druti</s>), digestion by mercury (<s>sūtakajāraṇā</s>), then assimilation (<s>grāsa</s>), then the operation of spreading (<s>sāraṇakarma</s>),

children.text: saṃkrāmaṇaṃ vedhavidhiḥ śarīre yogas tathāṣṭādaśadhātra karma // VRrs_11.16 //
children.translated_text: transference (<s>saṃkrāmaṇa</s>), the method of transmutation (<s>vedhavidhi</s>), and application to the body (<s>śarīre yoga</s>) — thus there are eighteen operations here. // VRrs_11.16 //

body.text: na yojyo marmaṇi chinne na ca kṣārāgnidagdhayoḥ // VRrs_11.17 //
body.translated_text: It should not be applied to a wound at a vital point (<s>marma</s>), nor to (wounds from) alkali or fire burns. // VRrs_11.17 //

body.text: śuddhaḥ sa mṛdvagnisaho mūrchito vyādhināśanaḥ // VRrs_11.18 //
body.translated_text: When purified, it withstands gentle fire; when fainted (<s>mūrchita</s>), it destroys diseases. // VRrs_11.18 //

children.translated_text: When killed (calcined, <s>mṛta</s>), with steady force and withstanding fierce fire, it grants longevity and health.
Poison (<s>viṣa</s>), fire (<s>vahni</s>), and impurity (<s>mala</s>) — these are the three natural defects // VRrs_11.19 //

body.text: rase maraṇasaṃtāpamūrchānāṃ hetavaḥ kramāt // VRrs_11.20 //
body.translated_text: of mercury, being the causes respectively of killing (<s>maraṇa</s>), burning (<s>saṃtāpa</s>), and fainting (<s>mūrchana</s>). // VRrs_11.20 //

body.text: yogikau nāgavaṅgau dvau tau jāḍyādhmānakuṣṭhadau // VRrs_11.21 //
body.translated_text: The two acquired (defects) are <s>Nāga</s> (lead) and <s>Vaṅga</s> (tin); they cause torpor, bloating, and leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>). // VRrs_11.21 //

children.translated_text: And furthermore, the other accidental (defects) are declared to be the seven sheaths (<s>saptakañcuka</s>):

children.text: bhūmijā girijā vārjās te ca dve nāgavaṅgajau // VRrs_11.22 //
children.translated_text: earth-born, mountain-born, water-born, and the two born of lead and tin. // VRrs_11.22 //

body.text: dvādaśaite rase doṣāḥ proktā rasaviśāradaiḥ // VRrs_11.23 //
body.translated_text: These twelve are declared by experts in mercury to be the defects of mercury. // VRrs_11.23 //

children.text: bhūmijāḥ kurvate kuṣṭhaṃ girijā jāḍyameva ca /
children.translated_text: Earth-born (mercury) causes leprosy, mountain-born causes torpor,
water-born causes accumulation of <s>vāta</s> (wind); that of <s>nāga</s> (lead) and <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) is full of defects. // VRrs_11.24 //

children.text: parpaṭī pāṭinī bhedī drāvī malakarī tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Parpaṭī</s> (scaly), <s>pāṭinī</s> (splitting), <s>bhedī</s> (breaking), <s>drāvī</s> (flowing), <s>malakarī</s> (impurity-producing),

children.text: andhakārī tathā dhvāṅkṣī vijñeyāḥ sapta kañcukāḥ // VRrs_11.25 //
children.translated_text: <s>andhakārī</s> (darkness-causing), and <s>dhvāṅkṣī</s> (crow-like) — these seven sheaths (<s>kañcukas</s>) should be known. // VRrs_11.25 //
Therefore, for the purpose of processing mercury, equipped with skilled assistants,
gathering all equipment, one should commence the alchemical work. // VRrs_11.26 //

children.text: dve sahasre palānāṃ tu sahasraṃ śatameva vā /
children.translated_text: Two thousand <s>palas</s>, or one thousand, or a hundred,

children.text: aṣṭāviṃśat palānyeva daśa pañcaikameva vā // VRrs_11.27 //
children.translated_text: or twenty-eight <s>palas</s>, or ten, or five, or even one — // VRrs_11.27 //
even with half a <s>pala</s>, the processing of mercury should be undertaken;
on an auspicious day under a favourable constellation, one should commence the purification of mercury. // VRrs_11.28 //
Adding <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> (the three pungents), salt, <s>āsurī</s> (mustard), <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago), fresh ginger, and radish,

children.text: kṣiptvā sūto muhuḥ svedyaḥ kāñjikena dinatrayam // VRrs_11.29 //
children.translated_text: mercury should be steamed repeatedly with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>) for three days. // VRrs_11.29 //
Soot-powder, brick-powder, and curd mixed with jaggery,
combined with salt and <s>āsurī</s> (mustard) — one should grind the mercury with these. // VRrs_11.30 //

children.text: ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ tu tad dravyaṃ sūtamānān niyojayet /
children.translated_text: That substance should be one-sixteenth the measure of mercury;

children.text: sūtaṃ kṣiptvā samaṃ tena dināni trīṇi mardayet // VRrs_11.31 //
children.translated_text: adding the mercury equally with that, one should grind for three days. // VRrs_11.31 //

children.text: jīrṇābhrakaṃ tathā bījaṃ jīrṇasūtaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Calcined <s>abhraka</s> (mica), <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal), and digested mercury likewise —

children.text: nairmalyārthaṃ hi sūtasya khalle dhṛtvā vimardayet // VRrs_11.32 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of purifying mercury, one should grind them in a mortar. // VRrs_11.32 //

children.text: gṛhṇāti nirmalo rāgān grāse grāse vimarditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, when ground, absorbs colouring agents dose by dose;

children.text: mardanākhyaṃ hi yatkarma tatsūtaguṇakṛd bhavet // VRrs_11.33 //
children.translated_text: the process called grinding (<s>mardana</s>) indeed enhances the qualities of mercury. // VRrs_11.33 //
<s>Gṛhakanyā</s> (aloe) destroys impurities, <s>triphalā</s> destroys digestive fire defects,

children.text: citramūlaṃ viṣaṃ hanti tasmād ebhiḥ prayatnataḥ // VRrs_11.34 //
children.translated_text: <s>Citramūla</s> (Plumbago root) destroys poison — therefore with these, carefully, // VRrs_11.34 //
mercury mixed with substances should be fainted (<s>mūrchana</s>) seven times;

children.text: itthaṃ saṃmūrchitaḥ sūto doṣaśūnyaḥ prajāyate // VRrs_11.35 //
children.translated_text: thus fainted, mercury becomes free of defects. // VRrs_11.35 //
After this purgation, the purified mercury should then be precipitated;
extracted from the sour-gruel decoction, for the removal of putrid defects. // VRrs_11.36 //
Making a cake with copper, one should precipitate it in an upper vessel;

children.text: vaṅganāgau parityajya śuddho bhavati sūtakaḥ // VRrs_11.37 //
children.translated_text: separating <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) and <s>nāga</s> (lead), mercury becomes purified. // VRrs_11.37 //

body.text: śullena pātayet piṣṭīṃ tridhordhvaṃ saptadhā tv adhaḥ // VRrs_11.38 //
body.translated_text: One should precipitate the cake with a ladle — three times upward and seven times downward. // VRrs_11.38 //

children.translated_text: With <s>triphalā</s>, <s>śigru</s> (Moringa), and <s>śikhi</s> (Apamārga), combined with salt and <s>āsurī</s> (mustard),
making the mercury into a paste, one should apply it to the upper vessel;
then with blazing <s>utpalas</s> (charcoals) below, one should cause downward precipitation. // VRrs_11.39 //
With <s>haridrā</s> (turmeric), <s>aṅkola</s>, <s>śampāka</s> (Michelia champaca), <s>kumārī</s> (aloe), <s>triphalā</s>, <s>agni</s> (Plumbago),
<s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> (Amaranthus), <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), rock salt, and honey — // VRrs_11.40 //
mercury ground with salts, or with <s>sarpākṣī</s> and similar herbs,

children.text: pātayed athavā devi vraṇaghno yakṣalocanaiḥ // VRrs_11.41 //
children.translated_text: should be precipitated, or, O goddess, with <s>yakṣalocana</s> for healing wounds. // VRrs_11.41 //

children.text: itthaṃ hy adhaūrdhvapātena pātito 'sau yadā bhavet /
children.translated_text: When mercury is thus precipitated by upward and downward precipitation,

children.text: tadā rasāyane yogyo bhaved dravyaviśeṣataḥ // VRrs_11.42 //
children.translated_text: then it becomes suitable for rejuvenative use, by virtue of specific substances. // VRrs_11.42 //

body.text: athavā dīpakayantre nipātitaḥ sarvadoṣanirmuktaḥ // VRrs_11.43 //
body.translated_text: Or, precipitated in a lamp-apparatus, it becomes freed from all defects. // VRrs_11.43 //

children.translated_text: Mercury, the king of <s>rasas</s>, precipitated by the method of lateral distillation (<s>tiryakpātana</s>),
finely ground <s>abhraka</s> (mica) flakes combined with mercury and then with sour gruel (<s>āranāla</s>) — // VRrs_11.44 //

children.text: khale dattvā mṛditaṃ yāvat tan naṣṭapiṣṭatām eti /
children.translated_text: placed in a mortar and ground until it reaches a paste-like state,
one should perform lateral distillation of the mercury, gradually with strong fire. // VRrs_11.45 //

children.text: saṃsvedyaḥ pātyo 'sau na patati yāvad dṛḍhaś cāgnau /
children.translated_text: It should be steamed and then precipitated — as long as it does not fall when held firmly in fire,

children.text: tadāsau śudhyate sūtaḥ karmakārī bhaveddhruvam // VRrs_11.46 //
children.translated_text: then that mercury is purified and will surely become efficacious in operations. // VRrs_11.46 //

body.text: mardanair mūrchanaiḥ pātairmandaḥ śānto bhaved rasaḥ // VRrs_11.47 //
body.translated_text: By grinding, fainting, and precipitation, inert and calmed becomes the mercury. // VRrs_11.47 //

children.translated_text: By creation-lotuses (specific herbs) and by restraint, mercury then becomes capable of absorption (<s>mukhakara</s>);
through steaming and other processes, mercury attains supreme potency. // VRrs_11.48 //
It should then be properly restrained, for the cessation of its volatility;
with <s>karkoṭī</s>, <s>phaṇinetra</s> (cobra-lily), <s>vṛścika</s> (scorpion plant), <s>ambuja</s> (lotus), and <s>mārkava</s>,
combined in equal parts with sour gruel, one should steam for three days. // VRrs_11.49 //
With black pepper, <s>bhūkhaga</s> (earth-snake plant), combined with salt, <s>āsurī</s> (mustard), <s>śigru</s> (Moringa), and borax,
mixed with sour gruel, steaming for three days makes mercury eager to absorb. // VRrs_11.50 //

With the three alkalis, <s>sindhu</s> (rock salt), <s>khaga</s> (Apamārga), <s>bhū</s> (earthen substances), <s>śikhi</s> (Apamārga), <s>śigru</s> (Moringa), <s>rājī</s> (mustard), <s>tīkṣṇā</s> (long pepper), sour cane, with salts, pungents, and acids,
Nepal copper flakes dried in sour gruel, with sour liquor and sour calcination — that is the kindling of mercury. // VRrs_11.51 //
One should steam with sour liquor for the enhancement of potency and vigour;

children.text: yathopayogaṃ svedyaḥ syān mūlikānāṃ raseṣu ca // VRrs_11.52 //
children.translated_text: mercury should be steamed as required in the juices of the roots. // VRrs_11.52 //
<s>Sarpākṣī</s>, <s>kṣīriṇī</s>, <s>vandhyā</s> (barren one), <s>matsyākṣī</s>, <s>śaṅkhapuṣpikā</s>,
<s>kākajaṅghā</s>, <s>śikhiśikhā</s>, <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s>, <s>ākhukarṇikā</s>, // VRrs_11.53 //
<s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>kambukī</s>, <s>dūrvā</s> (Bermuda grass), <s>sairyaka</s>, <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), <s>śimbikā</s>,
<s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>vajralatā</s>, <s>vajrakanda</s>, <s>agnikarṇikā</s>, // VRrs_11.54 //
white <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), <s>śigru</s> (Moringa), <s>dhattūra</s> (Datura), <s>mṛgadūrvā</s>, <s>rasāṅkuśa</s>,
<s>rambhā</s> (plantain), red <s>abha</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo), <s>lajjālu</s> (sensitive plant), <s>suradālikā</s>, // VRrs_11.55 //
<s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s> (Centella), <s>pātālī</s>, <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago), <s>grīṣmasundarā</s>,
<s>kākamācī</s> (Solanum nigrum), <s>mahārāṣṭrī</s>, <s>haridrā</s> (turmeric), <s>tilaparṇikā</s>, // VRrs_11.56 //
<s>jātī</s> (jasmine), <s>jayantī</s>, <s>śrīdevī</s>, <s>bhūkadamba</s>, <s>kusumbhaka</s> (safflower),

children.text: kośātakī nīraṃ kaṇā lāṅgalī kaṭutumbikā // VRrs_11.57 //
children.translated_text: <s>kośātakī</s> (luffa), water, <s>kaṇā</s> (long pepper), <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>kaṭutumbikā</s> (bitter gourd), // VRrs_11.57 //
<s>cakramarda</s> (Cassia tora), <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora), <s>kanda</s> (tuber), <s>sūryāvarta</s>, <s>puṅkhikā</s>,

children.text: vārāhī hastiśuṇḍī ca prāyeṇa rasamūlikāḥ // VRrs_11.58 //
children.translated_text: <s>vārāhī</s>, and <s>hastiśuṇḍī</s> — these are generally the roots used with mercury. // VRrs_11.58 //

children.text: rasasya bhāvane svede mṛṣālepe ca pūjitāḥ /
children.translated_text: They are esteemed in the soaking, steaming, and false-coating of mercury.
Thus, these eight processes of mercury (<s>sūtasaṃskāra</s>) are equal in importance for substances and rejuvenatives;

children.text: kāryāste prathamaṃ śeṣā noktā dravyopayoginaḥ // VRrs_11.59 //
children.translated_text: these should be performed first — the remaining ones, not stated, are for specific substance applications. // VRrs_11.59 //
We shall now describe the twenty-five types of mercury-binding (<s>rasabandha</s>);

children.text: yena yena hi cāñcalyaṃ durgrahatvaṃ ca naśyati /
children.translated_text: by whichever means the volatility and ungraspability

children.text: rasarājasya samprokto bandhanārtho hi vārttikaiḥ // VRrs_11.60 //
children.translated_text: of the king of <s>rasas</s> is destroyed — that is declared by the experts as the binding procedure. // VRrs_11.60 //
<s>Haṭha</s> (forcible), <s>āroṭa</s> (purified), <s>ābhāsa</s> (lustrous), <s>kriyāhīna</s> (action-deficient), <s>piṣṭikā</s> (cake-form),

children.text: kṣāraḥ khoṭaśca poṭaśca kalkabandhaśca kajjaliḥ // VRrs_11.61 //
children.translated_text: <s>kṣāra</s> (alkaline), <s>khoṭa</s> (lump), <s>poṭa</s> (flake), <s>kalkabandha</s> (paste-binding), and <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulphide), // VRrs_11.61 //
<s>sajīva</s> (with life), <s>nirjīva</s> (lifeless), <s>nirbīja</s> (seedless), and <s>sabījaka</s> (with seed),
<s>śṛṅkhalā</s> (chain-bound), <s>druti</s> (fluid-bound), <s>bālaka</s> (infant), and <s>kumāraka</s> (youth), // VRrs_11.62 //

children.text: taruṇaś ca tathā vṛddho mūrtibaddhas tathāparaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>taruṇa</s> (young), <s>vṛddha</s> (old), <s>mūrtibaddha</s> (form-bound), and another —
<s>jalabandha</s> (water-bound), <s>agnibandha</s> (fire-bound), the one called <s>susaṃskṛtakṛta</s> (well-processed),
and <s>mahābandha</s> (great binding) — thus twenty-five are declared. // VRrs_11.63 //
Some say there is a twenty-sixth called <s>jalūkābandha</s> (leech-binding);

children.text: sa tāvanneṣyate dehe strīṇāṃ drāve 'tiśasyate // VRrs_11.64 //
children.translated_text: that is not recommended for the body but is highly praised for liquefaction of metals in women's (formulations). // VRrs_11.64 //

children.text: haṭho rasaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ samyak śuddhivivarjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Haṭha</s> (forcible) is that mercury which is completely devoid of proper purification;

children.text: sa sevito nṛṇāṃ kuryān mṛtyuṃ vā vyādhimuddhatam // VRrs_11.65 //
children.translated_text: consumed by men, it causes death or severe disease. // VRrs_11.65 //
Mercury that is well-purified is called <s>āroṭa</s>;
it is excellent for field-preparation (body purification) and gradually destroys diseases. // VRrs_11.66 //

children.text: puṭito yo raso yāti yogaṃ muktvā svabhāvatām /
children.translated_text: Mercury that, when calcined, reverts to its original nature, losing its combination —
when processed with mineral roots and the like, is called <s>ābhāsa</s>, due to alteration of qualities. // VRrs_11.67 //
Mercury that has been prepared with unpurified metals and the like,

children.text: kriyāhīnaḥ sa vijñeyo vikriyāṃ yātyapathyataḥ // VRrs_11.68 //
children.translated_text: that is known as <s>kriyāhīna</s> (action-deficient) — it undergoes adverse reactions from improper regimen. // VRrs_11.68 //
In intense heat, by very vigorous grinding, it becomes a <s>piṣṭī</s> (cake) with a butter-like form;

children.text: sa rasaḥ piṣṭikābandho dīpanaḥ pācanastarām // VRrs_11.69 //
children.translated_text: that mercury is called <s>piṣṭikābandha</s> (cake-binding) — it is highly appetizing and digestive. // VRrs_11.69 //
Mercury prepared with conch-shell, oyster-shell, cowrie, and similar substances —
that is <s>kṣārabandha</s> (alkaline binding), which is supremely radiance-giving, nourishing, and colic-destroying. // VRrs_11.70 //

children.text: bandho yaḥ khoṭatāṃ yāti dhmāto dhmātaḥ kṣayaṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: The binding that becomes a lump (<s>khoṭa</s>) when smelted, and diminishes with repeated smelting —

children.text: khoṭabandhaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ śīghraṃ sarvagadāpahaḥ // VRrs_11.71 //
children.translated_text: that is known as <s>khoṭabandha</s> (lump-binding); it quickly cures all diseases. // VRrs_11.71 //
Fluid <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulphide), flattened on a plantain leaf,

children.text: sa poṭaḥ parpaṭī saiva bālādyakhilaroganut // VRrs_11.72 //
children.translated_text: that is <s>poṭa</s> (flake), and that same as <s>parpaṭī</s> (flake) — it destroys all diseases from infancy onward. // VRrs_11.72 //
Mercury prepared by steaming and other processes, having attained a paste-like state,
that is known as <s>kalkabaddha</s> (paste-bound) — it bestows the results prescribed for each formulation. // VRrs_11.73 //
<s>Kajjalī</s>, produced from mercury and sulphur, very fine and resembling collyrium —
combined according to a specific formulation, it is called <s>kajjalībandha</s> (collyrium-binding). // VRrs_11.74 //

children.text: bhasmīkṛto gacchati vahniyogād rasaḥ sajīvaḥ sa khalu pradiṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury that, when subjected to fire, becomes ash yet retains its vitality — that is known as <s>sajīva</s> (with life);

children.text: saṃsevito 'sau na karoti bhasmakāryaṃ javād rogavināśanaṃ ca // VRrs_11.75 //
children.translated_text: consumed, it does not cause the effects of ash, and it rapidly destroys diseases. // VRrs_11.75 //
Mercury with calcined <s>abhraka</s> (mica), or with fully digested sulphur, made into ash along with the best of all metals —

children.text: nirjīvanāmā hi sa bhasmasūto niḥśeṣarogān vinihanti sadyaḥ // VRrs_11.76 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>nirjīva</s> (lifeless) ash-mercury; it instantly destroys all diseases without remainder. // VRrs_11.76 //
Mercury that has digested a quarter-part of coloured (metal), made into cake with sulphur,

children.text: tulyāṃśagandhaiḥ puṭitaḥ krameṇa nirbījanāmā sakalāmayaghnaḥ // VRrs_11.77 //
children.translated_text: calcined gradually with an equal amount of sulphur — that is called <s>nirbīja</s> (seedless), destroyer of all ailments. // VRrs_11.77 //
Mercury digested with the essences of <s>abhraka</s> (mica), gold, <s>tārā</s> (silver), <s>arka</s> (copper), and <s>kānta</s> (loadstone) made into cakes,
then killed with six times its weight of sulphur — that is <s>sabīja</s> (with seed) binding, of great potency. // VRrs_11.78 //
Mercury killed by <s>vajra</s> (diamond) and other substances, and mercury killed as described above —
mercury bound in the <s>śṛṅkhalā</s> (chain) manner transforms the body and metals;

children.text: citraprabhāvāṃ vegena vyāptiṃ jānāti śaṃkaraḥ // VRrs_11.79 //
children.translated_text: it manifests wondrous powers with speed — <s>Śaṃkara</s> (Lord Śiva) knows its extent. // VRrs_11.79 //

children.text: yukto 'pi bāhyadrutibhiśca sūto bandhaṃgato vā bhasitasva paḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury, even when combined with external fluids, when in a bound state or in its own ash form,

children.text: sa rājikāpādamito nihanti duḥsādhyarogān drutibaddhanāmā // VRrs_11.80 //
children.translated_text: in a dose the size of a mustard seed, destroys incurable diseases — that is called <s>drutibaddha</s> (fluid-bound). // VRrs_11.80 //

children.text: samābhrajīrṇaḥ śivajastu bālaḥ saṃsevito yogayuto javena /
children.translated_text: Having digested an equal amount of <s>abhraka</s> (mica), born of <s>Śiva</s>, that is called <s>bālaka</s> (infant); consumed in a formulation, swiftly
it is a rejuvenative, destroyer of future diseases, and eliminates diseases accompanied by complications and fatal signs. // VRrs_11.81 //

children.text: harodbhavo yo dviguṇābhrajīrṇaḥ sa syātkumāro mitataṇḍulo 'sau /
children.translated_text: Born of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva), having digested twice its weight in <s>abhraka</s> (mica) — that is <s>kumāra</s> (youth), measured by a rice grain;

children.text: triḥ saptarātraiḥ khalu pāparogasaṃghātaghātī ca rasāyanaṃ ca // VRrs_11.82 //
children.translated_text: in thrice-seven nights (21 days), it destroys clusters of sinful diseases and is a rejuvenative. // VRrs_11.82 //
Having consumed four times its weight of <s>vyoma</s> (mica), this foremost rejuvenative is called <s>taruṇa</s> (young);
within seven nights, it destroys all ailments, is a rejuvenative, and bestows potency and strength. // VRrs_11.83 //

children.text: yasyābhrakaḥ ṣaḍguṇito hi jīrṇaḥ prāptāgnisakhyaḥ sa hi vṛddhanāmā /
children.translated_text: That which has digested six times its weight of <s>abhraka</s> (mica), having become a friend of fire — that is called <s>vṛddha</s> (old);

children.text: dehe ca lohe ca niyojanīyaḥ śivādṛte ko 'sya guṇān pravakti // VRrs_11.84 //
children.translated_text: it should be employed both on the body and on metals — who but <s>Śiva</s> can declare its virtues? // VRrs_11.84 //
Mercury that has been made supremely fire-resistant with divine roots,
without the digestion of <s>abhraka</s> (mica) — that is <s>mūrtibandha</s> (form-binding), a great mercury preparation. // VRrs_11.85 //

children.text: ayaṃ hi jāryamāṇastu nāgninā kṣīyate rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: This mercury, even when being digested, is not diminished by fire;
employed in all formulations, it bestows incomparable results. // VRrs_11.86 //
Mercury bound with waters from rock-juices and similar fluids — that is <s>jalabandha</s> (water-bound);
it destroys aging, disease, and death, and bestows the results described in the <s>kalpas</s> (ritual texts). // VRrs_11.87 //
Whether alone or in formulations, when smelted it takes the form of a pill;
undiminished, that is <s>agnibaddha</s> (fire-bound), which grants <s>khecaratva</s> (power of flight through the sky) and other powers. // VRrs_11.88 //
With <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>śaśilatā</s>, <s>kumbhī</s>, <s>kanakamūla</s>,
<s>viśālā</s>, <s>nāginī</s>, <s>kanda</s>, <s>vyāghrapādī</s>, <s>kuruṇṭaka</s>, // VRrs_11.89 //
<s>vṛścikālī</s>, <s>bhaśuṇḍī</s>, <s>haṃsapādā</s>, along with <s>āsurī</s> (mustard),

children.text: aprasūtagavāṃ mūtraiḥ piṣṭaṃ vā kulake pacet // VRrs_11.90 //
children.translated_text: ground with the urine of cows that have not calved, one should cook in a <s>kulaka</s> vessel. // VRrs_11.90 //
Thus cooked, ground with calcined metals, one should process the mercury;

children.text: yantreṣu mūrchā sūtānāmeṣa kalpaḥ samāsataḥ // VRrs_11.91 //
children.translated_text: the fainting of mercury in apparatus — this is the procedure in brief. // VRrs_11.91 //

children.text: hemnā vā rajatena vā sahacaro dhmāto vrajatyekatām akṣīṇo nibiḍo guruśca guṭikākāro 'tidīrghojjvalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Smelted together with gold or silver as a companion, it attains unity — undiminished, compact, heavy, pill-shaped, exceedingly lustrous and elongated —

children.text: cūrṇatvaṃ paṭuvat prayāti nihato ghṛṣṭo na muñcenmalaṃ nirgandho dravati kṣaṇātsa hi mahābandhābhidhāno rasaḥ // VRrs_11.92 //
children.translated_text: it turns to powder like alkali, when ground it does not release impurities, is odorless, and melts instantly—this mercury is called <s>mahābandha</s> (great binding). // VRrs_11.92 //
Into mercury impregnated in the womb, with half gold or a quarter part lead, with the juices of five-fingered <s>śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton), intoxicating, phlegm-plant, and <s>ātabīja</s> seeds,

children.text: tadvat tejinīkolakākhyaphalajaiś cūrṇaṃ tilaṃ pattrakaṃ tapte khallatale nidhāya mṛdite jātā jalūkā varā // VRrs_11.93 //
children.translated_text: likewise with powders made from the fruits called <s>tejinī</s>, <s>kola</s>, and others, and sesame and leaf—placing on a heated mortar-surface and grinding, excellent <s>jalūkā</s> (leech-shaped suppositories) are produced. // VRrs_11.93 //

children.text: saiṣā syātkapikacchūromapaṭale candrāvatī tailake candre ṭaṅkaṇakāmapippalījale svinnā bhavet tejinī /
children.translated_text: That same, when wrapped in a covering of <s>kapikacchu</s> (cowhage) hair, in <s>candrāvatī</s> oil, in moon-borax and long-pepper water, steamed, becomes <s>tejinī</s>;

children.text: tapte khallatale vimardya vidhivadyatnādvaṭī yā kṛtā sā strīṇāṃ madadarpanāśanakarī khyātā jalūkā varā // VRrs_11.94 //
children.translated_text: ground properly on a heated mortar-surface with effort, a pill made thus—it destroys the intoxication and pride of women—this excellent <s>jalūkā</s> is well-known. // VRrs_11.94 //

children.text: bālye cāṣṭāṅgulā yojyā yauvane ca daśāṅgulā /
children.translated_text: For young women, eight <s>aṅgulas</s> should be used; in youth, ten <s>aṅgulas</s>;

children.text: dvādaśaiva pragalbhānāṃ jalaukā trividhā matā // VRrs_11.95 //
children.translated_text: for mature women, twelve—thus the <s>jalūkā</s> is considered threefold. // VRrs_11.95 //
Holding a vessel at the mouth of the mercury, one should pour ewe's milk;
one should keep it in strong sunlight for twenty-one days. // VRrs_11.96 //

children.text: dvitīyātra mayā proktā jalaukā drāvaṇe hitā /
children.translated_text: This second <s>jalūkā</s> described by me is useful for dissolving;

children.text: puruṣāṇāṃ sthitā mūrdhni drāvayedbījam adbhutam // VRrs_11.97 //
children.translated_text: placed on the head of men, it dissolves the seed wonderfully. // VRrs_11.97 //
The juice of <s>munipatra</s> and <s>śālmalī</s> stem water,
water of <s>jātīmūla</s> (jasmine root), combined with <s>śiṃśapā</s> (rosewood) water, // VRrs_11.98 //
<s>śleṣmātaka</s> fruit, <s>triphalā</s> powder,

children.text: kokilākṣasya cūrṇaṃ ca pāradaṃ mardayed budhaḥ // VRrs_11.99 //
children.translated_text: and <s>kokilākṣa</s> powder—the wise one should grind mercury with these. // VRrs_11.99 //
A divine <s>jalūkā</s> is produced, captivating the minds of women;

children.text: sā yojyā kāmakāle tu kāmayetkāminī svayam // VRrs_11.100 //
children.translated_text: it should be applied at the time of desire, and the woman will desire of her own accord. // VRrs_11.100 //
In <s>triphalā</s>, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>mahauṣadha</s> (ginger), honey, ghee, goat's milk, and cow's urine,

children.text: nāgaṃ saptaniṣiktaṃ samarasajāritaṃ jalūkā syāt // VRrs_11.101 //
children.translated_text: lead quenched seven times, then digested with equal mercury, becomes a <s>jalūkā</s>. // VRrs_11.101 //
Mercury in the amount of the number of days of the sun (twelve), and its gold counterpart,
one should purify with the juices of <s>aṅkola</s>, <s>rājavṛkṣaka</s>, and <s>kanyā</s> (aloe). // VRrs_11.102 //
With the powders of <s>śaśirekhā</s>, <s>varṇinī</s>, <s>kokilākṣa</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, and <s>kanaka</s>,
one should grind properly for twenty-one days. // VRrs_11.103 //

children.text: niśāyāḥ kāñjikaṃ yūṣaṃ dattvā yonau praveśayet /
children.translated_text: Adding sour gruel of turmeric, one should insert it into the vagina;
it should be applied to young, middle-aged, and mature women, knowing the proper sequence;
even women of passionless men will become eager for union. // VRrs_11.104 //

children.text: rasabhāgaṃ catuṣkaṃ ca vaṅgabhāgaṃ ca pañcamam /
children.translated_text: Four parts of mercury and a fifth part of tin,
combined with an equal amount of <s>surasāra</s> (a mineral), along with borax— // VRrs_11.105 //

children.text: tridinaṃ mardayitvā ca golakaṃ taṃ rasodbhavam /
children.translated_text: having ground for three days, that mercury-born ball,
placed at the tip of the organ in the vagina, brings pleasure for a lifetime. // VRrs_11.106 //

children.text: karpūrasūraṇasubhṛṅgasumeghanādair nāgaṃ niṣicya tu mitho valayed rasena /
children.translated_text: Having quenched lead with camphor, <s>sūraṇa</s> (elephant yam), <s>bhṛṅga</s> (eclipta), and <s>meghanāda</s> (a plant) juices, one should coat it with mercury;

children.text: liṅgasthitena valayena nitambinīnāṃ svāmī bhavatyanudinaṃ sa tu jīvahetuḥ // VRrs_11.107 //
children.translated_text: with a ring placed on the organ, one becomes the master of women daily—it is the cause of vitality. // VRrs_11.107 //
With borax and long pepper, <s>sūraṇa</s>, camphor, and citron juices,

children.text: kṛtvā svaliṅgalepaṃ yoniṃ vidrāvayet strīṇām // VRrs_11.108 //
children.translated_text: making a coating on one's own organ, it dissolves the vaginal resistance of women. // VRrs_11.108 //
Into lead roasted on fire, one should cast <s>harabīja</s> (a seed), then double that;

children.text: munikanakanāgasarpair dantyātha siñyāc ca tanmadhyam // VRrs_11.109 //
children.translated_text: with <s>muni</s>, <s>kanaka</s>, <s>nāga</s>, <s>sarpa</s>, and <s>dantī</s> (croton), one should sprinkle in its middle. // VRrs_11.109 //
Having ground with buttermilk and a group of herbs, one should make a <s>madanavalaya</s> (love-ring);
at the time of intercourse, it destroys the pride of passion in women. // VRrs_11.110 //
Juice of <s>vyāghrī</s> and <s>bṛhatī</s> fruits, <s>sūraṇa</s> tuber, sour <s>caṇaka</s> (gram) leaves,
<s>kapikacchu</s> (cowhage), <s>vajravallī</s>, long pepper, and sour powder— // VRrs_11.111 //
lead roasted on fire, ground nine times with these cooling substances,
making a <s>smaravalaya</s> (love-ring), it causes dissolving in women. // VRrs_11.112 //
<s>Palāśa</s> (butea) seed with red lemon juice and mercury,

children.text: sajīvaṃ marditaṃ yantre pācitaṃ mriyate dhruvam // VRrs_11.113 //
children.translated_text: with <s>sajīva</s> (a substance), ground together in the apparatus and cooked—it certainly kills (mercury). // VRrs_11.113 //
With the seeds of <s>kharamañjari</s> and lotus seeds, finely powdered, making a paste,

children.text: kṛtvā sūtaṃ puṭayed dṛḍhamūṣāyāṃ bhavedbhasma // VRrs_11.114 //
children.translated_text: one should calcine mercury in a firm crucible—it becomes ash. // VRrs_11.114 //
<s>Hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) well-treated with the milk of wild fig tree,
by the process of grinding and calcination, indeed turns mercury to ash. // VRrs_11.115 //
One should grind <s>devadālī</s> and <s>harikrāntā</s> with sour gruel;
with that liquid, mercury ground and fainted seven times. // VRrs_11.116 //

children.text: tatsūtaṃ kharpare dadyāddattvā dattvā tu taddravam /
children.translated_text: One should place that mercury on a potsherd, adding that liquid again and again,

children.text: cullyopari pacec cāhni bhasma syāllavaṇopamam // VRrs_11.117 //
children.translated_text: and cook it on the stove during the day—it becomes ash like salt. // VRrs_11.117 //
One should powder the seeds of <s>apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes) and castor;
that powder should be applied to mercury in a crucible, layered above and below;

children.text: ruddhvā laghupuṭaiḥ pacyāc caturbhir bhasmatāṃ nayet // VRrs_11.118 //
children.translated_text: sealed, one should cook with four light <s>puṭas</s> (calcinations)—it becomes ash. // VRrs_11.118 //
In a tuber grown from a bitter gourd, in its core, soaked with woman's milk,

children.text: saptadhā sveditaḥ sūto mriyate gomayāgninā // VRrs_11.119 //
children.translated_text: mercury steamed seven times is killed by cow-dung fire. // VRrs_11.119 //
One should grind mercury on the mortar with water from <s>aṅkola</s> root,
combined with sulphur; at the end of the day, one should seal it;

children.text: puṭayedbhūdhare yantre dinānte sa mṛto bhavet // VRrs_11.120 //
children.translated_text: calcining in the <s>bhūdhara yantra</s> (earth-bearer apparatus), at the day's end it becomes dead (calcined). // VRrs_11.120 //
One should grind mercury and mica with <s>vaṭa</s> (banyan) milk for three <s>praharas</s> (nine hours);
cooking it with that fuel, the mercury becomes ash. // VRrs_11.121 //
Now, the patient should worship the teacher of alchemy, who is directly the god <s>Maheśvara</s>,
and the perfected mercury held in a horn, tooth, bamboo, or the like container. // VRrs_11.122 //
Having worshipped according to one's ability the gods, cows, and brahmins,

children.text: parṇakhaṇḍe dhṛtaṃ sūtaṃ jagdhvā syādanupānataḥ // VRrs_11.123 //
children.translated_text: having consumed mercury placed on a leaf-piece, one should take it with an after-drink of: // VRrs_11.123 //
ghee, rock salt, coriander, cumin, and fresh ginger as accompaniments,
<s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> (amaranth), coriander, <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), <s>alambuṣā</s>, and such— // VRrs_11.124 //
well-digested rice in cow's urine, cow's milk, ghee, yogurt,
<s>haṃsodaka</s> (a preparation), mung bean soup—this is the wholesome diet in summary. // VRrs_11.125 //
<s>Bṛhatī</s> (nightshade), <s>bilva</s> (wood apple), ash-gourd, bamboo shoots, bitter gourd,

children.text: māṣaṃ masūraṃ niṣpāvaṃ kulatthaṃ sarṣapaṃ tilam // VRrs_11.126 //
children.translated_text: black gram, lentils, flat beans, horse gram, mustard, sesame— // VRrs_11.126 //
fasting, massage, bathing, copper vessels, wine and fermented drinks,
meat of marshy animals, sour grains, eating on banana leaves,

children.text: kāṃsye ca guruviṣṭambhi tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ ca bhṛśaṃ tyajet // VRrs_11.127 //
children.translated_text: in bronze, and heavy, constipating, sharp-hot foods—one should strictly avoid these. // VRrs_11.127 //

children.text: kaṇṭārīphalakāñjikaṃ ca kamaṭhastailaṃ tathā rājikām nimbūkaṃ katakaṃ kaliṅgakaphalaṃ kūṣmāṇḍakaṃ karkaṭī /
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṇṭārī</s> fruit sour gruel, turtle oil, mustard, lemon, <s>kataka</s>, <s>kaliṅgaka</s> fruit, ash-gourd, cucumber,

children.text: kārī kukkuṭakāravellakaphalaṃ karkoṭikāyāḥ phalam vṛntākaṃ ca kapitthakaṃ khalu gaṇaḥ proktaḥ kakārādikaḥ // VRrs_11.128 //
children.translated_text: <s>kārī</s>, chicken, bitter gourd fruit, <s>karkoṭikā</s> fruit, eggplant, and wood-apple—indeed, this is the group called the 'ka-group.' // VRrs_11.128 //
This <s>kakārādi</s> (ka-initial) group is stated as given in the <s>Devīśāstra</s>;
that prescribed in other texts is described differently. // VRrs_11.129 //

children.text: kaṅguḥ kandukakolakukkuṭakalakroḍāḥ kulatthāstathā kaṇṭārī kaṭutailakṛṣṇagalakaḥ kūrmaḥ kalāyaḥ kaṇā /
children.translated_text: Millet, <s>kanduka</s>, jujube, chicken, <s>kala</s>, boar, horse gram, <s>kaṇṭārī</s>, pungent oil, black galangal, turtle, field pea, long pepper,

children.text: karkāruśca kaṭhillakaṃ ca katakaṃ karkoṭakaṃ karkaṭī kālī kāñjikameṣakādikagaṇaḥ śrīkṛṣṇadevoditaḥ // VRrs_11.130 //
children.translated_text: <s>karkāru</s>, <s>kaṭhillaka</s>, <s>kataka</s>, <s>karkoṭaka</s>, cucumber, <s>kālī</s>, sour gruel, and ram—this ka-group is stated by Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇadeva</s>. // VRrs_11.130 //
In whichever mercury preparation the <s>kakārādi</s> group is prohibited by verbal tradition,
there it should be avoided; its appropriateness follows from other considerations. // VRrs_11.131 //
If eructation occurs, one should take yogurt-rice with black fish and cumin;
for wind disturbance, massage with oils such as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and others. // VRrs_11.132 //
For restlessness, sprinkling cold water on the head;
for thirst, coconut water and mung bean with sugar. // VRrs_11.133 //
One should take fruits of grapes, pomegranate, dates, and banana;
for increasing the potency of the mercury, yogurt, milk, sugarcane, and sugar;

children.text: śītopacāram anyaṃ ca rasatyāgavidhau punaḥ // VRrs_11.134 //
children.translated_text: cooling treatments and such are further prescribed when mercury is to be discontinued. // VRrs_11.134 //

body.text: bhakṣayed bṛhatīṃ bilvaṃ sakṛtsādhāraṇo vidhiḥ // VRrs_11.135 //
body.translated_text: One should eat <s>bṛhatī</s> (nightshade) and <s>bilva</s> (wood apple) once—this is the general rule. // VRrs_11.135 //

children.translated_text: For fever, for bleeding disorders,
for cough, for asthma and hiccup, // VRrs_12.1 //
for hoarseness, heart disease, for thirst, alcohol-induced hemorrhoids,
for reverse peristalsis, diarrhea, for chronic bowel disease, colic, and tenesmus, // VRrs_12.2 //
for cholera, for weak digestive fire, for urinary difficulty, and stone disease,

children.text: mehasya somarogasya piṭikānāṃ ca vidradheḥ // VRrs_12.3 //
children.translated_text: for urinary disorders, menstrual disease, for boils, and abscesses, // VRrs_12.3 //
for hernia, abdominal tumors and other diseases, for colics, and for ascites,
for anemia, edema, erysipelas, for leprosy, vitiligo, and flatulence, // VRrs_12.4 //
for gout, for blocked channels, for barrenness, for diseases of pregnant women,
for diseases of women after delivery and of children, for insanity and epilepsy also, // VRrs_12.5 //
for eye disease, ear disease, for nasal disease and oral disease,
for diseases arising in the head, for wounds, fractures, and fistula, // VRrs_12.6 //
for cysts and such minor diseases, for genital diseases, and for poisoning,
for aging, for childless women, and for the purpose of nourishing the seed— // VRrs_12.7 //
in this order, the treatment of all diseases
I shall describe here with formulations of mercury, metals, and poisons, according to tradition. // VRrs_12.8 //
Horripilation, trembling, sweetness in the mouth, yawning, headache, and burning sensation—

children.text: vātajvarasyoktam idaṃ hi lakṣma bhuktottaraṃ syādyadi śaśvadeva // VRrs_12.9 //
children.translated_text: this is stated as the sign of <s>vāta</s> (wind) fever, if it occurs constantly after eating. // VRrs_12.9 //
Purging, emaciation, pungent taste in the mouth, intense heat, delirium, dizziness, and fainting—

children.text: etāni pittajvaralakṣaṇāni vamiḥ satṛṣṇāṅgavidāhitā ca // VRrs_12.10 //
children.translated_text: these are the signs of <s>pitta</s> (bile) fever, along with vomiting, thirst, and burning sensation in the body. // VRrs_12.10 //
Cough, dyspnea, numbness in the mouth, sweetness, excessive sleepiness,
perspiration, and mild burning—these are the signs of <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) fever. // VRrs_12.11 //

body.text: miśritaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yattu dvayos triṣu bhavecca tat // VRrs_12.12 //
body.translated_text: Mixed symptoms of two or three <s>doṣas</s> constitute that (combined fever). // VRrs_12.12 //

children.text: vimarditābhyāṃ rasagandhakābhyāṃ nīreṇa kuryādiha golakaṃ tam /
children.translated_text: Having ground mercury and sulphur together, one should make a ball with water;

children.text: bhāṇḍe navīne viniveśya paścāttadgolakasyopari tāmrapātram // VRrs_12.13 //
children.translated_text: placing it in a new vessel, then upon that ball a copper plate. // VRrs_12.13 //

children.text: sārdhaṃ muhūrtaṃ vinirudhya dhīmān uddīpayed dīptakṛśānunāsya /
children.translated_text: Sealing for one and a half <s>muhūrtas</s> (about 72 minutes), the wise one should light strong fire at its mouth;
below, the <s>parpaṭī</s> (flaky preparation) is produced—it is a forest-fire-cloud against fresh fever. // VRrs_12.14 //

children.text: vilipya pūrvaṃ rasanāṃ ca tāludeśaṃ ca sindhūdbhavajīrakārdraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having first anointed the tongue and palate with rock salt, cumin, and fresh ginger,

children.text: vallonmitāṃ cārdrakatoyamiśrām enāṃ niyojya sthagayet paṭena // VRrs_12.15 //
children.translated_text: one should administer this, mixed with ginger water, measured by a betel leaf, and cover with cloth. // VRrs_12.15 //

children.text: gharmodgamo yāvadataḥ paraṃ ca takraudanaṃ pathyamiha prayojyam /
children.translated_text: Until sweating occurs, and after that, buttermilk-rice is the proper diet here;

children.text: kuryāddinānāṃ tritayaṃ yadītthaṃ jvarasya śaṅkāpi tadā bhavetkim // VRrs_12.16 //
children.translated_text: if one does this for three days, then what fear can there be of fever? // VRrs_12.16 //

Mercury, <s>arka</s> (calotropis), sulphur, <s>capala</s> (bismuth), <s>jayapāla</s> (croton), <s>tiktā</s> (gentian), <s>pathyā</s> (chebulic myrobalan), <s>trivṛt</s> (operculina), and substances from <s>viṣatinduka</s> (strychnos), in equal parts—

children.text: saṃbhāvya vajripayasā madhunā trivallas trailokyaḍambararaso 'bhinavajvaraghnaḥ // VRrs_12.17 //
children.translated_text: combined with <s>vajra</s> (diamond) milk and honey in three-<s>valla</s> dose, this is the <s>Trailokyadaṃbara</s> (Thunderer of Three Worlds) formula, destroyer of fresh fever. // VRrs_12.17 //
One-quarter part of <s>sārarava</s> (a substance), equal parts of sulphur, well-cooked, ground in its own decoction—

children.text: rasaḥ kramānmāṣamito 'nilādijvareṣu nāmnā kila meghanādaḥ // VRrs_12.18 //
children.translated_text: mercury, in a dose of one <s>māṣa</s>, sequentially for wind and other fevers—this is named <s>Meghanāda</s> (Thunder-cloud). // VRrs_12.18 //

children.text: daradajaladayuktaṃ śuddhasūtaṃ ca gandhaṃ praharamatha supiṣṭaṃ vallayugmaṃ ca dadyāt /
children.translated_text: Purified mercury and sulphur combined with cinnabar and water, finely ground for one <s>prahara</s> (three hours), one should administer two <s>valla</s> doses;

children.text: jvaragajaharisaṃjñaṃ śṛṅgaverodakena prathamajanitadāhī kṣīrabhaktena bhojyaḥ // VRrs_12.19 //
children.translated_text: this is named <s>Jvaragajahari</s> (Elephant-slayer of Fever)—with <s>śṛṅgavera</s> (ginger) water, it first causes sweating; the diet should be milk and rice. // VRrs_12.19 //
A portion of heated lead, mercury, sulphur, and long pepper,

children.text: samabhāgaṃ pṛthak tatra melayecca yathāvidhi // VRrs_12.20 //
children.translated_text: in equal parts individually, one should combine them properly. // VRrs_12.20 //
One should grind everything in lemon juice for three days.
and in the juice of <s>Meghanāda</s> and <s>Kumārī</s> (aloe), and also in <s>rasa</s> (mercury) for three days, // VRrs_12.21 //
for two days in goat's urine, and in cow's urine for three days;
one should process it as appropriate, and add these [substances] to it. // VRrs_12.22 //
<s>Saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>Citraka</s> (Plumbago zeylanica), and a portion of <s>Sauvarcala</s> (black salt) and <s>Lavaṇa</s> (salt),

children.text: tena sammelanaṃ kṛtvā bhāvayecca punaḥ punaḥ // VRrs_12.23 //
children.translated_text: combining these together, one should triturate again and again. // VRrs_12.23 //

children.text: anena vidhinā samyak siddho bhavati tadrasaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this method, properly [prepared], that <s>rasa</s> (mercurial preparation) becomes perfected;
one should administer it in a dose of three <s>vallas</s>, combined with sugar and ghee. // VRrs_12.24 //
Wheat porridge is the recommended diet, along with <s>Māṣa</s> (black gram) soup and <s>Vāstuka</s> (Chenopodium album);
combined with <s>Dhātrīphala</s> (Emblica officinalis), it destroys all fevers;
this is proclaimed by the knowers of <s>tantras</s> (alchemical treatises) as <s>Dīpikā Rasa</s>. // VRrs_12.25 //
<s>Pārada</s> (mercury), <s>Rasaka</s> (calamine), <s>Tāla</s> (orpiment), <s>Tuttha</s> (copper sulfate), <s>Gandhaka</s> (sulfur), and <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax)—
all these in equal parts, purified, [should be ground] with the juices of <s>Kāravallī</s> (bitter gourd) for one day. // VRrs_12.26 //
One should grind them, and with that paste smear the interior of a copper vessel
to a thickness of half a finger; then cook it in the apparatus called <s>Sikatā</s> (sand-bath) // VRrs_12.27 //
in the <s>yantra</s> (apparatus), until the rice grains on its surface burst open;

children.text: tataḥ suśītalaṃ grāhyaṃ tāmrapātrodarād bhiṣak // VRrs_12.28 //
children.translated_text: then the physician should extract it, well-cooled, from inside the copper vessel. // VRrs_12.28 //
This is named <s>Śītabhañjī Rasa</s>; one should powder it together with black pepper,
and take one <s>māṣa</s> dose with a piece of <s>Parṇa</s> (betel leaf); it destroys fever—
within three days, [it cures] irregular, severe, quotidian, tertian, and quartan fevers. // VRrs_12.29 //
<s>Sūta</s> (mercury), <s>Tāla</s> (orpiment), and <s>Śilā</s> (realgar), in equal parts, should be ground in the juice of <s>Karkaṭī</s> (Momordica dioica);
that paste, made into <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulfide of mercury), should be placed in a copper vessel. // VRrs_12.30 //
One should cook it in a <s>Vālukāyantra</s> (sand-bath apparatus) by the method described above; then
the excellent physician should administer it in a dose of one <s>māṣa</s>, with black pepper powder. // VRrs_12.31 //
One should drink a mouthful of hot water, for cold fever;
this is that <s>Śītabhañjī Rasa</s>, the remover of cold fevers. // VRrs_12.32 //

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍacūrṇatilajaiḥ praviśuddhatālaṃ gāḍhaṃ vimardya suṣavīsalilena tulyam /
children.translated_text: Having thoroughly purified <s>Tāla</s> (orpiment) with the powders of <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (ash gourd), sesame, and <s>Jai</s> (jasminum), triturating it firmly with <s>Suṣavī</s> water in equal parts,

children.text: sūtena hiṅgulabhuvā sikatākhyayantre golaṃ vidhāya parivṛttakapālamadhye // VRrs_12.33 //
children.translated_text: with mercury derived from <s>Hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), forming a bolus in the apparatus called <s>Sikatā</s> (sand-bath), placed within an inverted <s>kapāla</s> (crucible lid), // VRrs_12.33 //

children.text: pattreṇa taṃ dinapateśca pidhāya ruddhvā saṃdhiṃ tayorguḍasudhākhaṭikāśivābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: covering it with a leaf of <s>Dinapati</s> (Calotropis) and sealing the junction of the two [vessels] with jaggery, lime, chalk, and <s>Śivā</s> (Terminalia chebula),

children.text: vahnau pacenmṛduni pātraśiraḥsthaśālīvaivarṇyamātram avadhiṃ pravidhāya dhīmān // VRrs_12.34 //
children.translated_text: the wise one should cook it on a gentle fire, setting the limit as the mere discoloration of rice placed atop the vessel. // VRrs_12.34 //

children.text: vallaṃ tataḥ surasamiśramamuṣya dadyāt sarpiḥ sitākaṇapayomadhu cānupeyam /
children.translated_text: Then one should administer a <s>valla</s> dose of this mixed with <s>Surasā</s> (holy basil); ghee, sugar candy, milk, and honey should be the accompanying drinks;

children.text: jetuṃ jvarān praviṣamān iha vāntiśāntyai maulau suśītalajalasya dadīta dhārām // VRrs_12.35 //
children.translated_text: to conquer irregular fevers, and for the cessation of vomiting, one should pour a stream of very cool water on the head. // VRrs_12.35 //
Now, [I describe] the crest-jewel of the king of <s>rasas</s> (mercurial preparations), the ender of diseases, named <s>Mṛtajīvana</s> (reviver of the dead),

children.text: sudhāraseneva rasena yena saṃjīvanaṃ syāt sahasāturāṇām // VRrs_12.36 //
children.translated_text: by which <s>rasa</s> (mercurial medicine), like the essence of nectar, there would be sudden revival of the sick. // VRrs_12.36 //
With the petals of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), <s>Hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), and <s>Jepāla</s> (Croton tiglium), ground in increasing [proportions] with <s>Dantī</s> (Baliospermum montanum) water,

children.text: dinārdhena jvaraṃ hanyādguñjaikaṃ sitayā saha // VRrs_12.37 //
children.translated_text: within half a day it destroys fever; the dose is one <s>guñjā</s>, taken with sugar. // VRrs_12.37 //

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ viṣaṃ gandhaṃ dhūrtabījaṃ tribhiḥ samam /
children.translated_text: Purified <s>Sūta</s> (mercury), <s>Viṣa</s> (aconite), <s>Gandha</s> (sulfur), and <s>Dhūrta</s> (Datura) seeds, each equal to three [parts],

children.text: caturbhiśca samaṃ vyoṣaṃ cūrṇīkṛtya nidhāpayet // VRrs_12.38 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents: ginger, pepper, long pepper) equal to four parts, should be powdered and stored. // VRrs_12.38 //

children.text: dantabhāṇḍe 'tha vā śārṅge kāṣṭhe naiva kadācana /
children.translated_text: In an ivory container, or in horn—never in wood;

children.text: vātaśleṣmajvare deyaṃ dvaṃdvaje vā tridoṣaje // VRrs_12.39 //
children.translated_text: it should be given in <s>Vāta-Śleṣma</s> (wind-phlegm) fever, in dual-<s>doṣa</s> fever, or in tri-<s>doṣa</s> fever. // VRrs_12.39 //
With the juice of <s>Śṛṅgavera</s> (ginger), or alternatively of <s>Jambīra</s> (lemon),
the dose is two <s>guñjās</s>; and when it is digested, one should take curd-rice as food. // VRrs_12.40 //
Within one, two, or three days, it destroys fevers according to the order of <s>doṣas</s>;
this <s>rasa</s> is called <s>Mahājvarāṅkuśa</s> (the great fever-hook), taught by <s>Śambhu</s> (Lord Śiva). // VRrs_12.41 //

children.text: tālaṃ tāmrarajo rasaśca gaganaṃ gandhaśca nepālakaṃ dīnārapramitaṃ tadardhamuditaṃ ṭaṅkaṃ śilāmākṣikam /
children.translated_text: <s>Tāla</s> (orpiment), copper filings, mercury, <s>Gagana</s> (mica), <s>Gandha</s> (sulfur) of <s>Nepāla</s> origin, measured at one <s>Dīnāra</s>; half that amount of <s>Ṭaṅka</s> (borax), <s>Śilā</s> (realgar), and <s>Mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite);

children.text: dīnāradvitayaṃ viṣasya śikhinaḥ piṣṭvā rasaiḥ pācito yaścintāmaṇivajjvaraughavijayī nāmnā tu mṛtyuṃjayaḥ // VRrs_12.42 //
children.translated_text: two <s>Dīnāras</s> of <s>Viṣa</s> (aconite) and peacock [feather ash]—ground and cooked with juices, this conquers the host of fevers like a <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem); its name is <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> (conqueror of death). // VRrs_12.42 //

children.text: tālaṃ tāmram ayorajaśca capalā tutthābhrakaṃ kāntakaṃ nāgaṃ syācca samāṃśakaṃ sumṛditaṃ mūlaṃ ca paunarnavam /
children.translated_text: <s>Tāla</s> (orpiment), copper, iron filings, mercury, <s>Tuttha</s> (copper sulfate), <s>Abhraka</s> (mica), <s>Kāntaka</s> (magnetic iron), and <s>Nāga</s> (lead)—all in equal parts, well-ground, along with the root of <s>Punarnava</s> (Boerhavia diffusa);

the paste [triturated] with juices extracted from the leaves of <s>Bhṛṅgī</s> (Eclipta), <s>Kāsa</s> (Saccharum), <s>Harī</s> (Terminalia), <s>Punarnava</s>, and <s>Mahāmandāra</s> (Erythrina), cooked in a sand-bath apparatus—this destroys all fevers. // VRrs_12.43 //

children.text: tutthena tulyaḥ śivajaśca gandho jambīranīreṇa vimardanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Gandha</s> (sulfur), born of <s>Śiva</s>, equal in amount to <s>Tuttha</s> (copper sulfate), should be triturated with <s>Jambīra</s> (lemon) juice

children.text: dinatrayaṃ melaya tena tulyaṃ vyoṣaṃ tataḥ sidhyati candrasūryaḥ // VRrs_12.44 //
children.translated_text: for three days; then mix with it an equal amount of <s>Vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents)—thus <s>Candrasūrya</s> (Moon-Sun preparation) is perfected. // VRrs_12.44 //

children.text: vallo vijetuṃ viṣamāvalambi dalena deyo bhujagākhyavallyāḥ /
children.translated_text: A <s>valla</s> dose to conquer irregular [fevers]; it should be given with a leaf of <s>Bhujagākhyavallī</s> (the serpent-named creeper, Rauwolfia);

children.text: dugdhaṃ hitaṃ syādiha śṛṅgaverarasena śaityeṣu niṣevaṇīyaḥ // VRrs_12.45 //
children.translated_text: milk is the recommended [vehicle]; with the juice of <s>Śṛṅgavera</s> (ginger), it should be used in cold [fevers]. // VRrs_12.45 //
Buttermilk [is recommended] for fever with pregnancy and for colic; with grape-water, the diet prescribed next [should follow];

children.text: rodhaṃ varāyāḥ salilena śūlaṃ jambīranīreṇa varājalena // VRrs_12.46 //
children.translated_text: for constipation, [give it] with the water of <s>Varā</s> (Terminalia chebula); for colic, with <s>Jambīra</s> (lemon) juice and <s>Varā</s> water. // VRrs_12.46 //
In loss of consciousness, one should employ anointing with the milky sap of <s>Bimba</s> (Coccinia) fruits;

children.text: ghṛtaudanaṃ syādiha bhojanāya jambīranīreṇa nihanti gulmam // VRrs_12.47 //
children.translated_text: ghee-rice should be the food here; with <s>Jambīra</s> (lemon) juice, it destroys abdominal tumors. // VRrs_12.47 //
It should be given with the juice of <s>Hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), <s>Amlikā</s> (tamarind), and <s>Nimbu</s> (lime) in splenic enlargement; here, buttermilk-rice is the diet;

children.text: stambhārthamasminsasitaṃ payaḥ syād guḍo niyojyo vamanapraśāntyai // VRrs_12.48 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of arresting [diarrhea], milk with sugar should be given; jaggery should be employed for the cessation of vomiting. // VRrs_12.48 //

children.text: aśītir yasya varṣāṇi vasuvarṣāṇi yasya vā /
children.translated_text: One who is eighty years old, or one who is [only] eight years old—

children.text: viṣaṃ tasya na dātavyaṃ dattaṃ ced doṣakārakam // VRrs_12.49 //
children.translated_text: to such a person, <s>Viṣa</s> (aconite/poison) should not be given; if given, it causes harm. // VRrs_12.49 //
<s>Megha</s> (tin/lead), <s>Pārada</s> (mercury), <s>Gandha</s> (sulfur), <s>Aśma</s> (mineral calcium), <s>Viṣa</s> (aconite), <s>Vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents), and <s>Paṭu</s> (sharp salts),
along with the two types of <s>Jīraka</s> (cumin)—all these should be made in equal parts. // VRrs_12.50 //
With the juice of <s>Sinduvāra</s> (Vitex negundo), and with the juice of <s>Laśuna</s> (garlic),
and with the juice of <s>Apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes aspera), one should triturate for seven nights. // VRrs_12.51 //
That [preparation], cooked in a <s>Vālukāyantra</s> (sand-bath apparatus), should be administered in a dose of one <s>guñjā</s>;
with <s>Nāgavallī</s> (betel leaf) and pepper; then one should give cold water to drink. // VRrs_12.52 //
This <s>rasa</s> named <s>Umāprasādana</s> (grace of <s>Umā</s>) removes cold fevers;

children.text: cāturthikaṃ trirātraṃ vā nāśayet kimutāparān // VRrs_12.53 //
children.translated_text: it destroys quartan fever within three nights—what to speak of other [fevers]? // VRrs_12.53 //
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), <s>Rasa</s> (mercury), and <s>Gandha</s> (sulfur) should be prepared in equal parts;

children.text: nepālaṃ dviguṇaṃ dattvā mardayet khallamadhyataḥ // VRrs_12.54 //
children.translated_text: adding double the amount of <s>Nepāla</s> (Nepali aconite), one should grind in a mortar. // VRrs_12.54 //
One should grind it slowly until it attains smoothness;

children.text: saindhavaṃ maricaṃ śaṅkhaṃ ciñcākṣāraṃ samākṣikam // VRrs_12.55 //
children.translated_text: <s>Saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>Marica</s> (black pepper), <s>Śaṅkha</s> (conch-shell powder), <s>Ciñcākṣāra</s> (tamarind alkali), and <s>Mākṣika</s> (honey/iron pyrite)—
making these equal to that [previous mixture], one should then grind with <s>Nimbū</s> (lime) water;
one should take a pill the size of a gram for three days. // VRrs_12.56 //

children.text: aikāhikaṃ dvyāhikaṃ ca tryāhikaṃ ca caturthakam /
children.translated_text: Quotidian, tertian, quartan, and every-fourth-day fevers—
for the destruction of all fevers, this is known as <s>Jvarāṅkuśa</s> (the fever-hook). // VRrs_12.57 //
<s>Abhraka</s> (mica), <s>Gandhaka</s> (sulfur), and <s>Sūta</s> (mercury), each one <s>tola</s>,
taking half a <s>tola</s> of <s>Viṣa</s> (aconite) and half a <s>tola</s> of <s>Tintiḍīphala</s> (tamarind fruit), // VRrs_12.58 //
combining all these equally, one should grind in a mortar;

children.text: ślakṣṇatāṃ yāti tadyāvat tāvat saṃmardayecchanaiḥ // VRrs_12.59 //
children.translated_text: one should grind slowly until it attains smoothness. // VRrs_12.59 //

children.text: vistāre pariṇāhe ca gartāṃ kṛtvā ṣaḍaṅgulām /
children.translated_text: Having made a pit six <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths) in width and circumference,
one should cast leaves of <s>Phaṇivallī</s> (betel) inside the pit. // VRrs_12.60 //

children.text: parṇeṣu sūtakalkaṃ taṃ gartāyāṃ sthāpayed dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: One should firmly place the mercury paste on those leaves in the pit;

children.text: kalkād upari tatparṇair gartāvaktraṃ prapūrayet // VRrs_12.61 //
children.translated_text: above the paste, one should fill the mouth of the pit with those leaves. // VRrs_12.61 //
Then one should give <s>puṭa</s> (calcination) in the pit using wild lotus [dung-cakes];
knowing that it has become cool to the touch, one should then extract it. // VRrs_12.62 //
One should grind the paste together with the mercury-smeared leaves in a mortar,
adding half a <s>tola</s> of <s>Amṛta</s> (Tinospora cordifolia) and half a <s>tola</s> of <s>Tintiḍīphala</s> (tamarind fruit). // VRrs_12.63 //
One should place the ground paste and administer it in a dose of one <s>guñjā</s>,
combined with <s>Śṛṅgavera</s> (ginger) water, along with sharp <s>Citraka</s> (Plumbago) and <s>Saindhava</s> (rock salt). // VRrs_12.64 //
In <s>Sannipāta</s> (tri-doṣa derangement) fever, in <s>Vāta</s> (wind) fever, in tri-<s>doṣa</s> and irregular fevers,

children.text: agnimāndye grahiṇyāṃ ca tathā deyo 'tisāriṇi // VRrs_12.65 //
children.translated_text: in diminished digestive fire, in chronic diarrhea (<s>Grahiṇī</s>), and likewise it should be given to those with dysentery. // VRrs_12.65 //
Curd-rice should be employed as food with this <s>rasa</s>;

children.text: vyādhyādikaṃ yathā kuryādudakaṃ ḍhālayet tataḥ // VRrs_12.66 //
children.translated_text: as appropriate to the disease, one should then administer water [for purging]. // VRrs_12.66 //
This excellent <s>yoga</s> (formulation), auspicious and life-giving to living beings,
is renowned as <s>Cintāmaṇi Rasa</s> (wish-fulfilling gem preparation), beautifying all limbs. // VRrs_12.67 //

children.text: sūtendraṃ parimardya pañcapaṭubhiḥ kṣārais tribhis taṃ tataḥ piṇḍe hiṅgumahauṣadhāsurīmaye saṃsvedya dhānyodake /
children.translated_text: Having triturated the lord of mercury with the five pungent substances, then with three <s>kṣāras</s> (alkalis), sweating it in a bolus made of <s>Hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), <s>Mahauṣadha</s> (ginger), and <s>Surī</s>, in grain-water,

with the waters extracted from <s>Nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo), <s>Hutāśa</s> (fire-plant), <s>Mantha</s> (churning herb), <s>Tilaparṇī</s> (sesame-leaved plant), <s>Unmatta</s> (Datura), <s>Bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), <s>Ārdraka</s> (ginger), <s>Kāmātā</s>, <s>Girikarṇikā</s>, <s>Plava</s> (Cyperus), and <s>Pañcāṅgula</s> (Ricinus) leaves— // VRrs_12.68 //

children.text: sūtendreṇa samair vimardya sahajaiḥ pittaistato bhāvayed daṃṣṭricchāgalulāyamatsyaśikhināṃ sā saṃnipātāñjayet /
children.translated_text: grinding with natural biles of <s>Daṃṣṭrī</s> (boar), goat, fox, fish, and peacock, in equal parts with the lord of mercury, and then processing—she conquers <s>Sannipāta</s> (tri-doṣa derangement);

children.text: vikhyātā bhuvi lokanāthaguṭikā mārīcamātrā hitā syādasyāḥ sahitaṃ dadhīkṣuśakalaṃ vīryaṃ bhavecchītalam // VRrs_12.69 //
children.translated_text: renowned in the world as <s>Lokanātha Guṭikā</s> (the Lord of the World pill), beneficial in the dose of a black pepper grain; with it, curd and sugarcane pieces [are the adjuvant]; its potency is cooling. // VRrs_12.69 //
The <s>bhasma</s> (calx) of <s>Vajra</s> (diamond) and <s>Vaikrānta</s> (tourmaline), each measured at one <s>niṣka</s>,

children.text: śṛṅgīviṣaṃ dviniṣkaṃ ca triniṣkaṃ cūlikāpaṭu // VRrs_12.70 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgī</s> (aconite) poison at two <s>niṣkas</s>, and three <s>niṣkas</s> of the pungent <s>Cūlikā</s> (a variety of aconite), // VRrs_12.70 //
five <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>Agnijāra</s> (fire-born mineral, a form of calcined metal)—all these should be combined together;
one should grind that much <s>bhasma</s> with mercury for three days. // VRrs_12.71 //
One should process it with the alkaline water of <s>Śārṅga</s> and the eight [medicinal] groups,

children.text: trayoviṃśativārāṇi vimardya ca viśoṣya ca // VRrs_12.72 //
children.translated_text: grinding and drying twenty-three times. // VRrs_12.72 //
Then, grinding for one day, one should place it in an ivory casket;
this <s>rasa</s> is called <s>Mṛtasañjīvana</s> (reviver of the dead), [also known as] <s>Sūcikābharaṇa</s> (needle-adorned). // VRrs_12.73 //
For one who is about to die from severe <s>Sannipāta</s> (tri-doṣa crisis), fallen upon the ground,
one should make an incision in the palate and deposit this <s>rasa</s> there. // VRrs_12.74 //
With an extremely fine needle, pierced [to create an opening] for water, with great care,

children.text: tatastailena taṃ liptvā nirvāte saṃniveśayet // VRrs_12.75 //
children.translated_text: then, anointing him with oil, one should place him in a draft-free location. // VRrs_12.75 //
Then, after half a <s>prahara</s> (approximately 1.5 hours), having released urine and feces,

children.text: labdhasaṃjñaṃ pratāpāḍhyaṃ dolayantaṃ śiro muhuḥ // VRrs_12.76 //
children.translated_text: having regained consciousness, full of vitality, nodding the head repeatedly, // VRrs_12.76 //
one should recognize him as one who will live; otherwise, [the prognosis is] otherwise indeed.

children.text: tataḥ śītāmbusampūrṇe kaṭāhe taṃ niveśayet // VRrs_12.77 //
children.translated_text: Then one should place him in a cauldron filled with cold water. // VRrs_12.77 //
There, removing the water that has become heated, one should add fresh [cold water];

children.text: yācamānam amuṃ paścāt pāyayet sasitaṃ payaḥ // VRrs_12.78 //
children.translated_text: afterward, when he asks [for drink], one should give him milk with sugar. // VRrs_12.78 //
Or curd mixed with sugar, and also coconut water;

children.text: rambhāphalāni dadyācca mriyate so 'nyathā khalu // VRrs_12.79 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rambhā</s> (plantain) fruits should also be given—otherwise he will surely die. // VRrs_12.79 //
When he has regained consciousness, is speaking, and is asking for fruits and such,

children.text: tasmādākṛṣya tailāktaṃ tailaṃ piṣṭvāpanīya ca // VRrs_12.80 //
children.translated_text: then, withdrawing [the medicine], having applied oil and removing the paste, // VRrs_12.80 //
one should anoint him with fragrant camphor from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head;
with such cooling substances, one should treat him for seven nights. // VRrs_12.81 //
One should repeatedly place cotton pads in the ears, eyes, nostrils, and mouth;
on the arrival of the eighth day, the juice extracted from <s>Dardurī</s> (frog-plant) root, // VRrs_12.82 //
mixed with sugar, should be given to drink, in order to bring down the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) [from the palate];

children.text: rase 'vatārite paścād yatheṣṭaṃ bhojanaṃ dadhi // VRrs_12.83 //
children.translated_text: after the <s>rasa</s> has descended, then food and curd as desired [may be given]. // VRrs_12.83 //
If [the patient shows] breathing with inhalation and exhalation, along with other signs of released life-force,
one should immerse him in a cauldron filled with water, for the attainment of consciousness. // VRrs_12.84 //
Having regained consciousness, one should withdraw him and treat as before;

children.text: jīvitvā yāvad āyuṣyaṃ mriyate tadanantaram // VRrs_12.85 //
children.translated_text: having lived out his allotted lifespan, he dies thereafter. // VRrs_12.85 //
One drowning in the ocean of death due to terrible <s>Sannipāta</s> (tri-doṣa crisis)—

children.text: uddharettasya dharmasya brahmāpyantaṃ na vindati // VRrs_12.86 //
children.translated_text: he rescues; even <s>Brahmā</s> cannot find the end of that <s>dharma</s> (virtue/power of this medicine). // VRrs_12.86 //
The person freed from the fear of the great death of <s>Sannipāta</s>—
one should worship the life-giving teacher (<s>prāṇācārya</s>) even by giving everything one possesses. // VRrs_12.87 //
Otherwise, one [remains] in hell as long as the duration of the cosmic cycle;

children.text: ityājñā śāṃkarī jñeyā śambhunā parikīrtitā // VRrs_12.88 //
children.translated_text: this command of <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva) should be known, as proclaimed by <s>Śambhu</s>. // VRrs_12.88 //
The fundamental [teachings] of mercury-transmutation should never be made public;
the foolish give them away without [consulting] the treatise, out of desire for wealth;
having obtained the teacher's grace, it should be employed in <s>saṃnipāta</s> (complex febrile conditions). // VRrs_12.89 //

children.text: śārṅgaṣṭā ca tathā vyāghrī karīras tilaparṇikā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śārṅgaṣṭā</s>, and likewise <s>vyāghrī</s> (Solanum), <s>karīra</s> (Capparis), <s>tilaparṇikā</s>,
<s>indravāruṇikā</s> (colocynth), <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus), turmeric, and <s>aṅkolamūlikā</s> (Alangium root). // VRrs_12.90 //

children.text: apāmārgaḥ kaṇā svarṇaṃ kaṭutumbī ca tintiḍī /
children.translated_text: <s>Apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes), long pepper, gold, bitter gourd, and tamarind —
this is the <s>śārṅgaṣṭādi</s> group, supremely destroying <s>saṃnipāta</s>. // VRrs_12.91 //

children.text: sūtaṃ gandhakatālakaṃ maṇiśilāṃ tāpyaṃ lavaṃ tutthakaṃ jepālaṃ viṣaṭaṅkaṇaṃ madhuphalaṃ kṛtvā samāṃśaṃ dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: Mercury, sulphur, orpiment, realgar, <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite), salt, copper sulfate, <s>jepāla</s> (croton seeds), poison, borax, and <s>madhuphala</s> (sweet fruit) — taking these in equal parts firmly,

children.text: kṛtvā kajjalikāṃ viṣolbaṇaphaṇeḥ pittaiśca saṃbhāvayet kṣiptvā sīsakakūpike rasavaraṃ sūcīmukhaṃ nāmataḥ // VRrs_12.92 //
children.translated_text: making a <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulphide) and combining with the bile of a powerful venomous serpent, casting into a lead cup — this is called <s>Sūcīmukha</s> (Needle-mouth) by name. // VRrs_12.92 //

children.text: brahmadvāri vikīrṇalohitalave guñjaikamātraṃ daded dattvā sampuṭabaddhatandrikadhanurvāte saśākhāhime /
children.translated_text: Applied at the <s>brahmadvāra</s> (anterior fontanelle), on a surface spread with blood, in the dose of one <s>guñjā</s>; having given it, covering the patient firmly in a bent-bow posture in wind and cold,

children.text: kāsaṃ śvāsamarocakaṃ pralapanaṃ kampaṃ ca hikkāturaṃ mūkatvaṃ badhiratvam unmadam apasmāraṃ jayet tatkṣaṇāt // VRrs_12.93 //
children.translated_text: it conquers instantly cough, asthma, loss of appetite, delirium, trembling, painful hiccups, muteness, deafness, madness, and epilepsy. // VRrs_12.93 //
Mercury, sulphur, copper, mica, <s>lāṅgalī</s> (Gloriosa), fire [substance], <s>rāmaṭha</s> (asafoetida),
<s>vandhyāpaṭola</s> (sterile Trichosanthes), <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex), fragrant neem leaves — // VRrs_12.94 //
<s>pāṭhā</s> (Cissampelos), the three alkalis, <s>kṣveḍa</s> (costus), <s>bola</s> (myrrh), <s>dhattūra</s> (thorn-apple) seeds —
with <s>śṛṅgī</s> (Aconitum) and liquorice essence, one should grind with lemon juice. // VRrs_12.95 //
One should make pills of one <s>niṣka</s> measure; it controls
<s>saṃnipāta</s> with sweating, burning, and seizure — [this is] <s>Saṃnipātagajāṅkuśa</s> (the Elephant-goad for Complex Fever). // VRrs_12.96 //

children.text: sasārā vaiṣṇavī senā acalā kādi kaṅkaṇā /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> army, full of vigor, steadfast, adorned with <s>kādi-kaṅkaṇa</s>,
endowed with <s>Rāga</s> and <s>Rudra</s>-like [potency], powerful, headed by the commander. // VRrs_12.97 //

children.text: tribhāgaṃ tālakaṃ vidyād ekabhāgaṃ tu pāradam /
children.translated_text: Three parts orpiment, one part mercury,

children.text: tadardhaṃ gandhakaṃ caiva tadardhaṃ tu manaḥśilā // VRrs_12.98 //
children.translated_text: half that of sulphur, and half of that, realgar. // VRrs_12.98 //
One should grind with the juice of bitter gourd leaves for three <s>praharas</s> (nine hours);
cooked in the sand-bath apparatus — [this is] the mercury that destroys quartan fever. // VRrs_12.99 //
Sulphur combined with mercury should be charming;
tripled with <s>hiyāvallī</s>, ground with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice — // VRrs_12.100 //
that should be combined seven times with fresh ginger juice;
it destroys continuous and other fevers — [this is] <s>Cāturthikagajāṅkuśa</s> (Elephant-goad for Quartan Fever). // VRrs_12.101 //
<s>Tāpya</s> (pyrite), orpiment, croton, <s>vatsanābha</s> (aconite), and realgar,
copper, sulphur, and mercury, ground with <s>musalī</s> (Chlorophytum) juice;
known as <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> (Conqueror of Death), cooked by <s>kukkuṭī puṭa</s> (hen-grade calcination). // VRrs_12.102 //
Two pills should be administered; the diet should be yogurt-rice as desired;
this great mercury [preparation] destroys new fevers and <s>saṃnipāta</s>. // VRrs_12.103 //

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ viṣaṃ gandhaṃ maricaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kaṇām /
children.translated_text: Pure mercury, poison, sulphur, black pepper, borax, and long pepper —

children.text: mardayed dhūrtajadrāvair dinam ekaṃ tu śoṣayet // VRrs_12.104 //
children.translated_text: one should grind with <s>dhūrta</s> (Datura) fruit juices for one day, then dry. // VRrs_12.104 //
Called <s>Pañcavaktra</s> (Five-faced) mercury, in a dose of two <s>guñjās</s>, it conquers <s>saṃnipāta</s>;
one should drink it as an adjuvant with <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) root decoction with the three pungents;

children.text: dadhyodanaṃ hitaṃ tatra jalayogaṃ ca kārayet // VRrs_12.105 //
children.translated_text: yogurt-rice is the proper diet; one should also give water. // VRrs_12.105 //
Mercury and sulphur in equal parts, with <s>dhattūra</s> fruit juices,

children.text: mardayed dinamekaṃ tu tattulyaṃ trikaṭu kṣipet /
children.translated_text: ground for one day; then add an equal amount of the three pungents;

children.text: unmattākhyo raso nāmnā nasye syātsaṃnipātajit // VRrs_12.106 //
children.translated_text: called <s>Unmatta</s> (the Mad One) by name, used as nasal application, it conquers <s>saṃnipāta</s>. // VRrs_12.106 //
Skinned <s>jepāla</s> (croton) seeds, ten <s>niṣkas</s>, should be powdered;

children.text: maricaṃ pippalīṃ sūtaṃ pratiniṣkaṃ vimiśrayet // VRrs_12.107 //
children.translated_text: black pepper, long pepper, and mercury, one <s>niṣka</s> each, should be mixed. // VRrs_12.107 //
It should be treated with lemon juices for seven days with great care;

children.text: saṃnipātaṃ nihantyāśu añjane yaḥ śivaḥ smṛtaḥ // VRrs_12.108 //
children.translated_text: [applied as] collyrium, it quickly destroys <s>saṃnipāta</s> — this is known as <s>Śiva</s> (the Auspicious One). // VRrs_12.108 //
<s>Madanaphala</s> (emetic nut), <s>viḍa</s> salt, and mustard seeds — two <s>niṣkas</s> each;
having powdered, one should drink with <s>triphalā</s> decoction and borax. // VRrs_12.109 //

children.text: kuṣṭhe jvare kāmalāyāṃ kaṇṭharoge hy ajīrṇake /
children.translated_text: In leprosy, fever, jaundice, throat disease, and indigestion;
as a nasal application, one seed of <s>girikarṇī</s> (Clitoria) with cold water. // VRrs_12.110 //

children.text: pratyekaṃ rasagandhayor dvipalayoḥ kṛtvā maṣīṃ śuddhayor ramyāṃ mlecchalulāyalocanamanodhātrīprakuñcatrayam /
children.translated_text: Two <s>palas</s> each of pure mercury and sulphur, made into black sulphide; the charming <s>mlecchalulāya</s> (a plant), eye, mind, <s>dhātrī</s> (āmalaka) — three <s>prakuñcas</s>;

children.text: pathyāyā badaratrikaṃ trikaṭu ṣaṭśāṇaṃ vacā dharmiṇī vellāmbhodharapattrakadviradakiñjalkāśvagandhāhvayam // VRrs_12.111 //
children.translated_text: <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula), three <s>badara</s> (jujube), the three pungents — six <s>śāṇas</s>, <s>vacā</s> (calamus), <s>dharmiṇī</s>, cardamom, <s>ambhodhara</s> (camphor), <s>pattra</s> (bay leaf), elephant-pollen, and <s>aśvagandhā</s> (Withania). // VRrs_12.111 //

children.text: piṣṭvaitat samasāram akhilaṃ karṣonmitaṃ nyasya tat pronmardyārdhakarañjakāmṛtayutaṃ sāgastikatryūṣaṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having ground all this together, placing one <s>karṣa</s> measure of each, then vigorously triturating with half <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia) and <s>amṛta</s> (Tinospora) combined with <s>āgastika</s> (Sesbania) and the three pungents;

children.text: bhūdhātrīvijayāsaritpatiphalaṃ jvālāmukhīmārkavaiḥ pratyekaṃ vidadhīta niścalamatiḥ sapta kramādbhāvanāḥ // VRrs_12.112 //
children.translated_text: with <s>bhūdhātrī</s> (Phyllanthus), <s>vijayā</s> (Cannabis), <s>saritpati</s> (camphor) fruit, <s>jvālāmukhī</s> (a plant), and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) — one should perform seven successive treatments, each individually, with firm determination. // VRrs_12.112 //

children.text: pittairatho pañca vidhāya pañcabhiḥ karañjapattrāmṛtadhūpanaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then performing five [treatments] with five [types of] biles, then fumigation with <s>karañja</s> leaves and <s>amṛta</s>;

children.text: dattvārdrakasya svarasena taṇḍulākṛtiṃ vidadhyādguṭikāṃ bhiṣagvaraḥ // VRrs_12.113 //
children.translated_text: then, with the juice of fresh ginger, the best physician should make pills the size of rice grains. // VRrs_12.113 //

children.text: deyaikā saṃnipāte pratihataviṣaye mohanetraprasuptyoḥ syādgulme sājamodā pavanavikṛtiṣu tryūṣaṇena grahaṇyām /
children.translated_text: One [pill] should be given in <s>saṃnipāta</s>; in cases of obstructed conditions, unconsciousness and eye-numbness, it should be given with <s>ajamoda</s> (celery) for abdominal tumors; with the three pungents in wind-disorders; with cumin for dysentery;

children.text: dātavyā jīrakeṇa dvipaturaganṛṇāṃ prāṇasaṃrakṣaṇāya kāyāmbhodhir etaṃ rasakasamarasaṃ vaidyanātho 'bhyadhatta // VRrs_12.114 //
children.translated_text: it is to be given in a dose of two [pills] for saving the lives of quadrupeds and horses — [this is] <s>Kāyāmbhodhi</s> (Ocean of the Body), a mercury [preparation] of equal efficacy, bestowed by <s>Vaidyanātha</s>. // VRrs_12.114 //
Mercury equal to sulphur and mica, ground with <s>vārāhī</s> (Dioscorea) juice,
cooked in the sand-bath apparatus with <s>triphalā</s>, the three pungents, and <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago) — // VRrs_12.115 //
the three alkalis, five salts, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium), and <s>dīpyaka</s> (caraway),
with cumin, <s>indrayava</s> (Wrightia seeds), each equal to one part of mercury — // VRrs_12.116 //
in a dose of one <s>māṣa</s>, with two <s>palas</s> of hot water as adjuvant;
for those suffering from seizure, digestive fire-loss, dysentery, anemia, and abdominal tumors — // VRrs_12.117 //
it effects the preservation of life; therefore it is known as <s>Prāṇeśvara</s> (Lord of Life);

children.text: vyādhivṛddhau prayogo 'sya dvau vārau vaidyasaṃmataḥ // VRrs_12.118 //
children.translated_text: in aggravated disease, its use two times is approved by physicians. // VRrs_12.118 //
Mercury, iron, the three pungents, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> (arsenic), realgar, orpiment, mica, cinnabar,
<s>kumbhī</s> (Trayamāna), <s>agni</s> (Plumbago), <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), <s>mārī</s>, <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> (Amaranthus), and <s>mākṣika</s> (chalcopyrite), // VRrs_12.119 //
combined with <s>hastiśuṇḍī</s> (Heliotropium), all in equal parts; half that of <s>śiva</s> (quicklime) and sulphur;

children.text: tryaham ārdrāmbunā piṣṭvā kūpīsthaṃ vālukāgninā // VRrs_12.120 //
children.translated_text: ground for three days with fresh ginger water, placed in a glass flask [and heated] with sand-fire; // VRrs_12.120 //
one should add the waters of <s>jayā</s> (a plant), lemon, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and <s>cāṅgerī</s> (wood sorrel);
cooking for fourteen days, grinding with moist [substances], and drying — // VRrs_12.121 //
this mercury called <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s> (Reviver of the Dead), taken in a pill dose,

children.text: drāg jayedauṣadhaṃ saṃnipātādīn sakalān gadān // VRrs_12.122 //
children.translated_text: quickly conquers as a medicine all diseases including <s>saṃnipāta</s>. // VRrs_12.122 //
One part mercury; sulphur is considered double;
poison, orpiment, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, realgar, cinnabar, and iron, // VRrs_12.123 //
<s>vahni</s> (Plumbago), the three pungents, <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), gold, <s>mākṣika</s> (chalcopyrite), and mica,
<s>hastiśuṇḍī</s>, poison, <s>kumbhī</s>, <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>, and copper — // VRrs_12.124 //
taking one part of each, one should powder;
and grind with fresh ginger juice for three days. // VRrs_12.125 //
Lemon juice should be taken, measured at three <s>palas</s>;

children.text: triphalāyāśca nirguṇḍyāḥ pratyekaṃ ca palatrayam // VRrs_12.126 //
children.translated_text: and three <s>palas</s> each of <s>triphalā</s> and <s>nirguṇḍī</s> [juice] — // VRrs_12.126 //
one <s>pala</s> measure of mercury, and as proclaimed, [one pala] of <s>cāṅgerī</s> (wood sorrel);

children.text: kācakūpyāṃ vinikṣipya yantre kṣiptvā prayatnavān // VRrs_12.127 //
children.translated_text: casting into a glass flask and placing in the apparatus with care — // VRrs_12.127 //
extracting and grinding with fresh ginger extract, one should dry;
this mercury called <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvana</s> (Reviver of the Dead) is known on earth;
a dose of two <s>guñjās</s> should be given for the removal of <s>saṃnipāta</s>. // VRrs_12.128 //

children.text: vaṅgaṃ nāgaṃ ca sūtaṃ ca nepālaṃ gandhakaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Tin, lead, mercury, <s>nepāla</s> (aconite), and sulphur,

children.text: śulbaṃ viṣaṃ samāṃśena rasenārdreṇa mardayet // VRrs_12.129 //
