children.translated_text: copper and poison — in equal parts, one should grind with fresh [ginger] juice. // VRrs_12.129 //
One should grind again with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> and <s>cāṅgerī</s> juices;
with the pill-dose method, this mercury removes <s>saṃnipāta</s>. // VRrs_12.130 //

children.text: gandhakaṃ ca rasaṃ śuddhaṃ pratyekaṃ karṣasammitam /
children.translated_text: Sulphur and pure mercury, one <s>karṣa</s> each,

children.text: ekatra kajjalīṃ kṛtvā tataḥ kurvīta golakam // VRrs_12.131 //
children.translated_text: making <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulphide) together, then forming a pellet — // VRrs_12.131 //
placing in a new vessel and covering with a copper plate,

children.text: dṛḍhaṃ nirudhya tat pātramagnāvāropayet tataḥ // VRrs_12.132 //
children.translated_text: sealing that vessel firmly and placing it on fire — // VRrs_12.132 //
only until the rice-grains burst, one should remove it self-cooled;
in new fever, one should use the mercury called <s>Parpaṭikā</s> (the Flaky One). // VRrs_12.133 //
With fresh ginger juice, three pills for three days — the physician
should cover the feverish [patient] firmly until sweat appears. // VRrs_12.134 //
Buttermilk-rice should be the proper diet for the person freed from fever;
this enemy of new fever is an exceedingly rare mercury [preparation];

children.text: vātajvare viśeṣeṇa rasaḥ sādhāraṇo mataḥ // VRrs_12.135 //
children.translated_text: especially in <s>vāta</s>-fever, this mercury is considered generally [applicable]. // VRrs_12.135 //
Borax, mercury, sulphur, and black pepper in equal parts —

children.text: sarvaṃ jambīranīreṇa dināni trīṇi mardayet // VRrs_12.136 //
children.translated_text: all should be ground with lemon juice for three days. // VRrs_12.136 //
Having dried, combined with sugar, one should treat with fish bile;
that mercury thus prepared is perfected with fresh ginger juices for three days. // VRrs_12.137 //

children.text: vallaṃ vāratrayaṃ deyaṃ pānārthaṃ vāri śītalam /
children.translated_text: One pill should be given three times; the drink should be cold water;
buttermilk-rice with eggplant fruit should be the proper diet;

children.text: sarvān navajvarān hanti raso 'yaṃ jalamañjarī // VRrs_12.138 //
children.translated_text: this mercury destroys all new fevers — it is [called] <s>Jalamañjarī</s> (Water-Cluster). // VRrs_12.138 //
One should make ash from magnetite needle-pierceable vessels;
equal to that: mercury, sulphur, and borax — with neem water,

children.text: tataḥ saṃpeṣya tatkalkaṃ mardayettridinaṃ punaḥ // VRrs_12.139 //
children.translated_text: then grinding that paste, one should triturate again for three days. // VRrs_12.139 //
One should treat with fish bile equal to the mercury;
this <s>Kāntarasa</s> (Magnetite Mercury) is indeed perfected, to be employed in new fever,
with ginger as adjuvant, in proper dose, by the best physicians. // VRrs_12.140 //
Mercury, sulphur, tin, and mica in equal parts;

children.text: melayitvātha vaṅgena samaṃ sūtaṃ vimardayet // VRrs_12.141 //
children.translated_text: having combined, one should grind the mercury equal to the tin. // VRrs_12.141 //
Having unified with the sulphur and mica, it should be ground with lemon juice;

children.text: sāmānyaṃ puṭam ādadyāt saptadhā sādhitaṃ rasam // VRrs_12.142 //
children.translated_text: one should give ordinary calcination seven times — [this is] the perfected mercury. // VRrs_12.142 //
Having treated seven times with <s>kumārī</s> (aloe) and <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago) also,

children.text: guḍena jīrakeṇāpi jvare jīrṇe prayojayet // VRrs_12.143 //
children.translated_text: with jaggery and cumin, one should employ it in chronic fever. // VRrs_12.143 //
In cough and asthma, with <s>kumārī</s> and <s>triphalā</s> decoction;
for madness and tetanus, with <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora) decoction;
thus this mercury called <s>Candrodaya</s> (Moonrise) destroys the torment of diseases. // VRrs_12.144 //

children.text: nāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ rasaṃ tāmraṃ gandhakaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Lead, tin, mercury, copper, sulphur, and borax,

children.text: viṣaṃ ca nepālaṃ haritālaṃ samaṃ tathā // VRrs_12.145 //
children.translated_text: poison, <s>nepāla</s> (aconite), and orpiment — all in equal parts — // VRrs_12.145 //
grinding all with banyan milk, one should make a pellet;
that pellet should be cooked in a vessel over lamp-fire. // VRrs_12.146 //

children.text: taṃ golaṃ śītalaṃ kṛtvā bhṛṅgarājena mardayet /
children.translated_text: Having cooled that pellet, one should grind with <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta) [juice];

children.text: ārdrakasya rasenāpi mardayecca punaḥ punaḥ // VRrs_12.147 //
children.translated_text: and grind again and again with fresh ginger juice. // VRrs_12.147 //
Pills of chickpea size should be given with fresh [ginger] juice;
in a dose of two <s>guñjās</s>, it destroys chronic fever. // VRrs_12.148 //

children.text: haraśca gandhakaṃ caiva kunaṭī ca samaṃ samam /
children.translated_text: <s>Hara</s> (Terminalia chebula), sulphur, and <s>kunaṭī</s> (a plant) — equal, equal parts;
should be ground and employed with the juice of <s>karkoṭikā</s> (bitter gourd). // VRrs_12.149 //
<s>Murāri</s> (Enemy of Mura) [mercury] conquers new fever; [given as] a pill with sugar;
with <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> (Amaranthus) juice as adjuvant, or also with sugar;
in a dose of two <s>guñjās</s>, it forcefully destroys new fevers. // VRrs_12.150 //
